docs.title: Meta-Evolve
docs.text:
Improve anything you can propose and evaluate.

Code, prompts, agents, images, data recipes—or something entirely different. Bring a starting version, a function that proposes changes, and another that evaluates them. Meta-Evolve explores revisions and keeps the best measured result.

You can improve the method itself, too: revise an agent’s instructions, a search strategy, or a generation recipe, then measure the results it produces.

Start building API reference

docs.title: An improvement loop in Python
docs.text:
Start with a parser that reads 4m as four seconds. Propose a correction, check both versions, and keep the better result.

From the parser walkthrough

result = meta.improve(
    seed=SEED,
    # This example returns a handwritten correction.
    # Replace it with a function that asks an agent or LLM for new candidates.
    proposer=propose,
    evaluator=evaluate,
    trials=1,
)

Your proposer can generate revised code, a hypothesis, a plan, or another candidate. The evaluator measures how well it meets your objective.

2/6 → 6/6 checks passed

Four minutes now returns 240 seconds. Retrieve the selected source with result.best().value.

docs.title: Add an artifact domain
docs.text:
Add an artifact domain when candidates need their own Python type, validation rules, and stored representation. Here, a Recipe holds ordered instructions. You will improve a short tea recipe, reject a wrongly typed proposal, and save and reopen the selected value without changing Meta-Evolve itself.

All revisions are handwritten and graded by Python. No model, API key, checkout, or earlier notebook is needed. Plain strings and numbers already work with the built-in domains; they need no custom codec.

Piece Purpose in this example Recipe The value the proposer and evaluator receive RecipeCodec Converts that value to stored data and back Registry Makes the codec available to a run Task(artifact=Recipe) Declares which kind of value this task expects

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Open a notebook with Python 3.12 or newer. Download the package ZIP into its working folder, then copy the Python blocks into cells in order. Restart the kernel if your notebook asks.

For hosted notebooks, upload the ZIP through the file browser; %pwd shows the working folder.

%pip install ./meta-evolve.zip

docs.title: 2. Define what a recipe is
docs.text:
Recipe is an immutable tuple of nonblank strings. Its constructor accepts a list or tuple of steps, including an empty one. A bare string is rejected so "boil water" cannot accidentally become a sequence of individual characters. __new__ constructs the tuple; __slots__ = () prevents extra instance fields.

KIND names the meaning of the value; REPRESENTATION names its stored shape. Together they select a codec. These are declarations on your type, not base classes you must inherit from. We use tuple because it already preserves order and prevents in-place edits.

import meta_evolve as meta

class Recipe(tuple):
    KIND = "recipe"
    REPRESENTATION = "json-steps-v1"
    __slots__ = ()

    def __new__(cls, steps=()):
        if not isinstance(steps, (list, tuple)):
            raise TypeError("steps must be a list or tuple")
        if not all(isinstance(step, str) and step.strip() for step in steps):
            raise ValueError("every step must be nonblank text")
        return super().__new__(cls, steps)

recipe_seed = Recipe(("boil water",))
print(type(recipe_seed).__name__, tuple(recipe_seed))
# Output:
# Recipe ('boil water',)

An incomplete recipe is still a valid value. Whether it contains useful steps in the right order belongs to the evaluator, which we will define below.

docs.title: 3. Teach Meta-Evolve how to store it
docs.text:
A codec translates between your Python value and a payload, the plain data stored for that value. encode returns the steps as a plain tuple; decode rebuilds a Recipe, running its validation again. Both methods must be deterministic and perform no I/O. Meta-Evolve computes content identity from the payload; the codec does not create IDs.

Raise TypeError or ValueError for values or payloads that do not fit the format. interfaces=() declares no shared consumer interface for this example.

class RecipeCodec:
    kind = Recipe.KIND
    representation = Recipe.REPRESENTATION
    interfaces = ()

    def encode(self, value):
        if not isinstance(value, Recipe):
            raise TypeError("recipe tasks require a Recipe value")
        return tuple(value)

    def decode(self, payload):
        return Recipe(payload)

codec = RecipeCodec()
payload = codec.encode(recipe_seed)
restored = codec.decode(payload)
print(type(payload).__name__, payload)
print(type(restored).__name__, tuple(restored))
# Output:
# tuple ('boil water',)
# Recipe ('boil water',)

This round trip preserves the steps and restores their type. decode is also the payload validation entry point; there is no separate validate method.

docs.title: 4. Register the codec
docs.text:
Registry.register_artifact_type registers the codec under its (kind, representation) pair. Pass this registry to experiments that use Recipe. Built-in pairs cannot be replaced: a different stored meaning needs a new pair so old data keeps its interpretation.

recipe_registry = meta.Registry()
recipe_registry.register_artifact_type(codec)

docs.title: 5. Define improvements and independent grading
docs.text:
The proposer returns a new Recipe, first adding steeping and then serving. The evaluator gives one point for each correct prefix: boil water; boil then steep; boil, steep, then serve. It returns the fraction correct, from 0 to 1. Extra arbitrary steps do not earn points just for making the recipe longer.

def propose_recipe(parent):
    if "steep tea" not in parent:
        return Recipe((*parent, "steep tea"))
    return Recipe((*parent, "serve"))

def evaluate_recipe(candidate):
    checks = (
        candidate[:1] == ("boil water",),
        candidate[:2] == ("boil water", "steep tea"),
        candidate[:3] == ("boil water", "steep tea", "serve"),
    )
    return sum(checks) / len(checks)

This checks a tiny written checklist. It does not execute the recipe or judge real-world cooking quality.

docs.title: 6. Run the experiment and inspect the values
docs.text:
Task(artifact=Recipe) chooses the domain. Experiment combines that task with the seed, proposer, search, and registry. Greedy(max_trials=2) allows two proposals, each based on the best recipe so far. meta.run evaluates the seed and revisions; it decodes values before handing them to your functions.

trials() returns the attempts; best().value returns the selected Recipe. Its stored kind and representation identify which codec reconstructs it.

recipe_experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate_recipe, artifact=Recipe),
    seed=recipe_seed, proposer=propose_recipe,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=2), registry=recipe_registry,
)
recipe_result = meta.run(recipe_experiment)
for attempt in recipe_result.trials():
    print(attempt.failure.kind if attempt.failure
          else f"{attempt.metrics['score']:.0%}")
best_recipe = recipe_result.best()
print("Stored as:", best_recipe.kind, best_recipe.representation)
print("Returned type:", type(best_recipe.value).__name__)
print("Steps:", tuple(best_recipe.value))
# Output:
# 33%
# 67%
# 100%
# Stored as: recipe json-steps-v1
# Returned type: Recipe
# Steps: ('boil water', 'steep tea', 'serve')

docs.title: 7. See a wrongly typed proposal get rejected
docs.text:
A plain tuple can contain the right words, but it is not our declared value type. replace copies the experiment with a proposer that forgets to construct a Recipe. The codec's TypeError becomes an invalid_output failure for that attempt. The evaluator never receives the rejected value.

from dataclasses import replace

def propose_plain_tuple(parent):
    return (*parent, "steep tea")

wrong_type_run = meta.run(replace(
    recipe_experiment, proposer=propose_plain_tuple,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=1),
))
failed = wrong_type_run.trials()[-1]
print("Failure:", failed.failure.kind)
print("Has a score:", bool(failed.metrics))
print("Evaluations:", wrong_type_run.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# Failure: invalid_output
# Has a score: False
# Evaluations: 1

Only the seed was evaluated. A valid recipe with poor steps would instead receive a measured low score. A rejected seed stops setup; unexpected codec errors propagate. Failures decoding already-stored data are reported as corruption. The codec contract owns these distinctions.

docs.title: 8. Save and reopen with a rebuilt registry
docs.text:
Storage.durable writes history to disk. Each execution below uses a new folder, so rerunning it keeps earlier saves. The text file remembers the latest folder. The with block closes storage when it finishes.

from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

recipe_location = Path("recipe-runs") / uuid4().hex
with meta.Storage.durable(recipe_location) as storage:
    meta.run(recipe_experiment, storage=storage)
_ = Path("last-recipe-run.txt").write_text(str(recipe_location.resolve()))

Reopening needs the value type and codec, but no proposer or evaluator functions. To try this after a kernel restart, rerun sections 2 and 3, then this cell. Storage.read_only opens saved history; Run uses the rebuilt registry to reconstruct its values. Each folder here contains exactly one run.

from pathlib import Path
import meta_evolve as meta

registry = meta.Registry()
registry.register_artifact_type(RecipeCodec())
location = Path(Path("last-recipe-run.txt").read_text())
with meta.Storage.read_only(location) as storage:
    run_id = storage.runs()[0]
    reopened_recipe = meta.Run(run_id, storage, registry=registry)
    value = reopened_recipe.best().value
    print(type(value).__name__, tuple(value))
    print("Evaluations:", reopened_recipe.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# Recipe ('boil water', 'steep tea', 'serve')
# Evaluations: 3

A registered codec is a live Python object. Custom domains currently support local execution, the default used above. mode="durable-local" rejects them because they lack the verified code manifest needed for resuming execution. Reopening with your registry grants decoding only; it does not make the run resumable. CLI inspection cannot accept a custom registry, so use Python for these saved values.

docs.title: Check your codec when extending the example
docs.text: The published ArtifactCodecTests checks round trips, malformed-payload and foreign-value rejection, repeated-call stability, and independence for mutable values. This guide's codec runs that suite in its tests. See the conformance reference for setup and fixtures, and domain concepts for the naming rules.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Replace the body of propose_recipe with return Recipe((*parent, "stir")) and rerun section 6. All three scores stay at 33%, and the seed stays best. Each proposal is a valid Recipe; none satisfies the missing checklist steps.

Next, apply your own value type, storage format, and evaluator using the same four pieces. The programming model owns the public API; architecture owns the domain and identity rules.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: This owns shipped domain invariants. The roadmap owns scope; current status distinguishes available capabilities from future work under Design. Distributed execution defaults to inline calls; explicit process backends execute work on admitted trusted workers. External SDKs remain user-owned callables at the structural proposer seam.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
Meta-Evolve evaluates proposed successors to immutable, versioned artifacts. The domain meaning does not depend on an artifact kind, model provider, search preset, evaluator implementation, or storage backend.

Task -> Seed -> Proposal -> Successor -> Evaluation -> Search decision
                      \-> typed failure

The public callable path hides kernel ceremony. Durable records retain the facts needed for lineage, accounting, inspection, comparison, and replay.

docs.title: Architectural layers
docs.text:
Public API       improve, Task, artifacts, Session, run/resume, result queries
Application      normalization, coordination, comparison, replay
Domain           immutable identities, outcomes, evidence, budgets
Ports            proposer, evaluator, experience, workspace, storage
Adapters         callables, SDK agents, subprocesses, files, SQLite

Dependencies point inward. Adapters translate external systems at the edge; the coordinator never branches on a provider, artifact type, evaluator, policy, or infrastructure implementation.

docs.title: Identities and lineage
docs.text:
Content identity and occurrence identity are distinct. Equal artifact bytes may appear in different causal positions and therefore retain different occurrence IDs and parent links. Task, run, proposal, trial, evaluation, evidence, decision, and component identities are not collapsed for storage convenience.

Every successor names its parents. Every decision-relevant observation is recorded at a logical time. Durable state is a projection of immutable records, not a mutable branch, workspace, cache, or provider conversation.

docs.title: Authority boundaries
docs.text: Candidate-controlled fields contain only proposed artifact content and declared derivation. Experiment-controlled fields include tasks, evaluators, data splits, seeds, environments, and budgets. Governance controls permissions, admission, visibility, and promotion.

docs.title: Proposal and promotion are separate
docs.text: Search may select a best measured artifact. That selection grants no production authority. A candidate cannot widen its budget, alter hidden evaluation, erase failures, change permissions, or promote itself. Future typed mutation surfaces must preserve this invariant; see the M8 design.

docs.title: Evaluation and failures
docs.text: Evaluation is independent of candidate claims and carries measurements, uncertainty, evidence, environment identity, and exact usage. Invalid output, proposer failure, evaluator failure, timeout, exhaustion, policy violation, and infrastructure failure remain distinct. An outcome without a valid measurement is non-rankable.

docs.title: Budgets and randomness
docs.text: Execution overrides inherit task ceilings and reject explicit widening. Start preparation resolves one effective budget before search binding or commitment; it determines identity and admission, and resume consumes the recorded value. The programming model owns the authoring contract. The coordinator owns seed/successor counts. Author Resources reports convert at existing result-to-record boundaries into count-free Usage before those counts are added; durable accounting shapes are unchanged. Unknown billed spend stays unknown through aggregation and replay; estimates stay evidence. Unverifiable monetary ceilings stop further work while retaining completed results. Experience access has separate bounds. Named random streams and recorded decisions make local trajectories replayable. External providers are reproducible to their transcript and declarations, without guaranteed byte-identical regeneration.

docs.title: Experience
docs.text: Experience is explicit and off by default. Pushed context is policy-selected, bounded, and committed before a proposal; pulled experience is capability-bounded and audited. Declared derivation may cite only authorized, strictly prior observations in recorded order. ProposerContext.evidence reads only the committed selection, with enabled state from the policy declaration. RecentAncestors@1 retains the newest accessible ancestor records; AncestorsOnly@1 retains the oldest. Both preserve canonical order and distinct record/rendering bounds. Lookup neither infers producer authority nor widens access; see the selected-evidence contract. M8.7.3 listing and reads authorize exact prior same-task/run artifact occurrences before a read-only storage edge revalidates and decodes source-tree / utf8-tree-v1; M8.7.4 applies that edge independently to both operands of a canonical library-owned diff. M8.7.5 composes those audited outcomes into one committed Git-neutral manifest, then projects it into disposable external Git metadata for a scoped workspace session. Invalid targets share one opaque denial; missing paths deny atomically. Whole-entry results use cumulative bounds and audit both exhaustion causes. Folding validates committed shape and the mount-owned operation prefix; durable loading checks stored bytes and reconstructs source results and the manifest; replay does no live read. Only successful source observations grant derivation authority. Whole-tree reader operations, semantic retrieval, persistent Git identity, and cross-run access remain unshipped under the source-inspection contract.

docs.title: Workspaces and external execution
docs.text: Repository proposers receive a private mutable workspace from an immutable artifact; successful capture creates a new immutable occurrence, and cleanup precedes commitment. Evaluators own fresh workspaces, commands, environments, hidden graders, and failure translation.

docs.title: Durability and replay
docs.text:
Artifacts and append-only transitions are durable truth. SQLite and filesystem stores preserve committed facts; caches and worker liveness do not. Writes validate each new batch against ephemeral grammar state for the committed prefix. That state and the projection advance only after a successful atomic commit with the expected version. Reopening still validates the full history using the same grammar rules; no cache is persisted or trusted across processes. Reopen is a read-only projection, and a read-only storage handle observes live WAL commits with no write, migration, or execution authority. open_run() owns that handle for a context block, validates one explicit or sole run, and yields a live Run; lexical identities never imply recency. It adds no durable records or execution authority. SQLite may maintain WAL sidecars without changing committed history. Resume first verifies component manifests and the recovery frontier, then performs only missing logical work. Replay never reruns a proposer, evaluator, context selector, or provider. Distributed retries may execute an uncommitted operation again while an abandoned call still runs. Lease and epoch checks enforce at-most-once acceptance; content-derived run IDs never couple execution in independent stores. The store owns the trusted-worker allow-list, and only an operator's command writes it; dispatcher-minted worker- ids need no row and hold generation 1. Revoke bumps a row's generation and marks it revoked; rows are never deleted, and trusting the id again keeps the bumped generation. A revoked worker's lease is stale at the next transactional check, and the sweep opening that run's next broker write frees it with a WorkerRevoked cause. The door refuses an unenrolled or revoked id before Terms, and broker acquire refuses it too. Malformed admission messages refuse their connection; typed store failures still stop the drive. Refusal diagnostics retain a bounded history so rejected connections cannot accumulate input buffers for the lifetime of a host. Run.inspect() derives one immutable aggregate from one replay. Registered proposer manifests cover user source, invocation, evidence views/errors, context construction, and adapter wiring; context-policy manifests cover the factory and selection/rendering module. Incompatible source refuses resume before runner construction, preflight, or work; supported histories stay readable. See the callback contract. Session fixes authority and budget; each step advances the classified frontier to ready or stopped without asking search twice. Lifecycle means Stop, rankability means successful evaluation, and bootstrap remains a trial. Summary and inspection derive lifecycle, rankability, and committed usage from one validated frontier each, including a pending distributed seed evaluation. Recorded usage is independent of policy readiness; failures retain their costs and pending work contributes no estimated charge. Summaries are nondurable views with an optional score; baseline and distinct typed failure counts share the captured frontier, while winner queries and comparisons remain strict. Capture-handle persistence and recorded capabilities do not authorize resume or change durable identity. ArchiveUpdate.member_ids is the authoritative ordered membership; an admission may remove any number of members, and evicted_artifact_id names exactly one or is None. Specialists is a GEPA-style per-key frontier, not a Pareto archive: it derives one winner per configured metric from committed evaluations and samples a metric uniformly to expand that metric's winner, so ownership over more metrics means more selection weight. TreeSearch is an ordinary tree-search@1 SearchProgram, not an archive: a private immutable fold derives one node per materialized artifact occurrence, its visits, and its best-descendant subtree Q entirely from durable trial and evaluation facts, then widens while child_count < ceil(sqrt(node_visits)) or otherwise descends by normalized UCT.

Safe exact-kind presentation reads frozen payloads into bounded inert records; decoded values are never inspected and canonical attachments remain exact. Captured run reports render bounded scalars as text or escaped HTML without storage, codec, component, or decoded-artifact calls. The loopback browser keeps storage on one thread and artifact routes within one snapshot; cached payloads add bounded-LRU memory without a byte copy.

docs.title: Replaceability
docs.text: Introduce a port only when a current acceptance test needs a second implementation. Published conformance suites cover codecs, repository proposers, evaluators, search programs, context policies, workspaces, sandboxes, and typed mutation surfaces; store contracts remain under tests/. Each suite states which laws it does not check.

docs.title: Improve
docs.text: improve() is declaration sugar with no independent durable identity or execution semantics. It constructs Task, bounded Greedy, and Experiment, then enters ordinary local run(). Its objective becomes Task.objectives=(objective,) or inherits the default; context uses the existing Experiment.context boundary without pull access. Equivalent declarations retain identical identity and committed facts at the same revision; handle-specific summary metadata can differ across stores. Its storage may persist local history without implying durable-local reconstruction or resumability.

docs.title: Experiment
docs.text: Experiment is an immutable declaration value, not a new durable record or serialization identity. Positional typed declarations and the source-compatible keyword run() form normalize before validation and enter the same execution path. Storage, mode, and the narrowing call-level budget remain execution overlays. Equality is dataclass equality over the eight fields; it does not promise structural equality for live proposer or registry objects.

docs.title: Functional search
docs.text: @search is a dependency-free adapter over the ordinary SearchProgram boundary, not a second coordinator path. Its callback chooses one opaque seed or incumbent occurrence handle, or stops with a validated reason. A private shared lowerer applies the same envelope and authorized unit trial construction as Greedy; the two retain distinct truthful policy and run identities. Complete immutable decorator configuration flows into SearchSpec and run identity. Durable-local reconstruction remains explicit registration through the existing policy-factory extension. Multiple parents, archives, and population-shaped actions stay on SearchProgram.next().

docs.title: Programming harnesses
docs.text:
HarnessArtifact is the built-in agent-harness domain using harness-manifest-v1. Its v1 schema contains a planner TextParam and a context-policy PolicyParam; their names, component references, interfaces, and surface types are immutable across a successor. Only text or policy configuration may change.

Artifact codecs may structurally expose validate_successor(parents, candidate). Proposal completion invokes it after candidate encoding and before artifact creation. Codecs without the hook retain their behavior. This generic boundary is core-owned, so an honest wrapper may use MutationSurface.apply() while a bypassing wrapper receives the same independent check.

Harness search evaluates development episodes only. Held-out episodes run once for the unchanged baseline and once for the selected harness as seed-only Greedy(max_trials=0) runs. Strict comparison requires equal evaluator, artifact, objective, budget, proposer, search, randomness, context, experience, and immutable harness declarations. It reports promotion eligibility but owns no promotion or deployment authority.

Portable repository episodes digest public source, hidden evaluator tests, process controls, and explicit development/held-out splits. The example-owned evaluator launches fresh isolated inner runs and records complete captured attempts. Resume guarantees begin at a committed outer evaluation; uncommitted inner work may repeat.

The research harness example owns its source-view and citation conventions: evaluator-owned views are evidence, not artifact lineage or selected exports, and usable citations require completed opens in first-exposure order. Those example restrictions supplement the kernel observation ledger without adding authority.

docs.title: Nested improvement loops
docs.text:
PolicyArtifact is the built-in search-policy domain using policy-manifest-v1. Its only mutable values are parent selection (seed or incumbent) and a non-negative voluntary trial limit. Fixed schema-owned names, component declarations, interfaces, allowed domains, tasks, seeds, proposers, evaluators, environments, budgets, split membership, caching, aggregation, and promotion remain outside candidate authority.

CandidatePolicy is the trusted candidate-policy@1 interpreter registered through the ordinary policy registry. Its canonical artifact payload is the search configuration and therefore part of the existing RunId; durable-local reconstruction and resume require no coordinator branch.

Policy episodes are user-owned composition around ordinary runs. Each isolated inner run retains its own events, lineage, evidence, failures, usage, RunId, and evaluator-owned storage location. The existing content-addressed RunId is the sole cache identity. Development may reopen an exact completed run or resume a compatible incomplete durable run. Held-out execution always starts in a new empty namespace. Aggregates are recomputed from outcomes rather than cached separately.

Any failed, incomplete, or missing episode makes an evaluation non-rankable while preserving partial outcomes. Inner trial/evaluation counts remain inner; only token, monetary-spend, and elapsed usage rolls into an enclosing evaluation. Separate seed-only held-out outer runs compare baseline and selected candidate under equal external controls. Comparison reports promotion eligibility without granting promotion authority. See the policy-evolution guide.

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
• Artifacts are immutable; equal content does not collapse causal occurrences.
  • Parent lineage, component identity, randomness, evidence, and usage are explicit.
  • Candidates cannot control evaluation, budgets, permissions, or promotion.
  • Failures without valid measurements are never ranked as low scores.
  • Replay projects committed facts without external execution.
  • Replaceable components enter through ports, never coordinator special cases.

docs.title: When to use Meta-Evolve
docs.text:
Use Meta-Evolve to apply, compose, and evolve improvement methods through a common Python programming model. It is useful when your work spans different artifacts, algorithms, or stages: software optimization, agent development, research procedures, and methods you build for scientific discovery.

You define what can change and how it will be evaluated. The library provides artifact contracts, replaceable components, bounded execution, explicit experience, and inspectable results. The method library identifies runnable implementations and proposed research mappings.

docs.title: Choose a path
docs.text: You want to… Start with Apply a method to your problem Available methods, with setup and implementation scope Build a variant from compatible components Compose a method and compare the method structures Improve the procedure itself AutoResearch or policy evolution Develop a discovery method in your own domain Artifact domains and scientific method mappings

docs.title: Why use a common method framework?
docs.text:
• Reuse work across methods. Keep a task, evaluator, artifact representation, or proposer when a compatible method can use it. The method worksheet makes those boundaries explicit. Full algorithms may need different stage schedules; changing a search preset alone does not implement them.
  • Represent the thing you actually improve. Source trees, skill collections, harnesses, and policy values have different structure and valid edits. Built-in and custom domains give those distinctions a contract without changing the coordinator.
  • Build methods with several stages. The AutoData lab composes generation, two solver conditions, acceptance checks, and recipe rewriting. Its current live integration and explicit Python orchestration demonstrate a bounded mechanism, not a packaged reproduction of the paper.
  • Evaluate an improvement procedure. AutoResearch makes a recipe the candidate and judges it through bounded inner runs. The outer result links the procedure to the outcomes used to measure it.
  • Inspect the evidence and work behind a choice. Recorded experience shows which prior observations were supplied; run inspection retains results and failures. Configured durable storage keeps committed history across processes.

These controls support comparisons without making them fair automatically. Keep datasets, objective meanings, model settings, and resource units comparable, and report actual usage and incomplete runs. Equal evaluation allowances need not mean equal model calls or cost.

docs.title: What do I need to supply?
docs.text:
For the simple callable path, supply a starting artifact, a function proposing revisions, and an independent evaluator. The complete parser tutorial defines all three; routing prompts and harness improvement show other artifacts. improve() adds bounded greedy search; Experiment exposes other search choices. The programming model owns that API.

For a method, follow its walkthrough's setup and stage schedule. Your callables own the model or tool integration, domain execution, grading, and usage reports. No model is bundled. Start with Use your model SDK for provider wiring. If a supplied optimizer already fits your task, its built-in proposal and execution strategy can save you that work.

docs.title: Which tool fits my task?
docs.text: These choices overlap. The guidance below compares authoring responsibilities, not optimization quality. External descriptions come from the linked primary sources; they were not validated by running those systems. The source record dates and scopes each check.

docs.title: Meta-Evolve: apply, compose, and evolve methods
docs.text:
Supply a seed, proposer, evaluator, and limits. The library supplies versioned artifacts, search presets, explicit feedback controls, and inspectable run records. Configure durable storage and reconstructible components when you need persistence and recovery. This suits experiments where you want to replace or study those components; it also leaves you responsible for the proposal strategy, SDK wiring, and grading. The package is Apache-2.0 licensed. Use the method library to choose a starting point and the shipped contract to extend it. Scientific method mappings are Design—not shipped; their proposed algorithms are not bundled implementations.

When an improvement procedure becomes the candidate, evaluation, work limits, and promotion remain outside candidate authority. Search selects a measured result; deploying it is a separate decision. These are experiment contracts: process confinement depends on the execution environment, and an ordinary in-process Python callable is not a sandbox.

docs.title: DSPy: optimize LM programs
docs.text: Supply a DSPy program, a metric, training examples, and model configuration; choose an optimizer. DSPy provides the program abstractions and optimizers for instructions, demonstrations, or model weights, depending on the optimizer. If your application already uses DSPy, its own optimization path is a natural starting point. You still design the program and evaluation data. Using its outputs in Meta-Evolve would require your own integration. DSPy optimizer documentation.

docs.title: GEPA / OptimizeAnything: optimize with selectable engines
docs.text: Supply an evaluator and a seed or objective, plus model/engine configuration and work limits. Supply development and validation examples when optimizing across inputs. OptimizeAnything provides an optimization entry point with selectable engines; the GEPA engine supports reflective proposals and configurable candidate selection. Current APIs also expose custom proposers, saved evaluation records, and engines including autoresearch and meta_harness. It can reduce setup when a supplied engine fits; check the chosen engine's controls and output semantics against your needs. API, configuration, and candidate selection.

docs.title: OpenEvolve: evolve programs
docs.text: Supply an initial program, an evaluator, model configuration, and iteration limits. OpenEvolve provides model-driven program revision, population search using islands and diversity dimensions, and history visualization. Its library entry points can accept inline code; separate files are not always required. Consider it when that program-evolution workflow fits. You still author the grader, prepare its runtime, and choose the search configuration. OpenEvolve's maintained README.

docs.title: Meta-Harness: revise harness programs
docs.text: The paper describes a coding-agent proposer inspecting prior harness code, scores, and execution traces in a filesystem. Applying the method requires a task harness, task data and reward function, model access, and an execution environment. It is relevant when the procedure around a model is what you want to change. This describes the paper's method, not a verified general-purpose installation path. Our Meta-Harness example is a bounded mechanism demonstration, not a reproduction of its system or results. Meta-Harness §3 and Algorithm 1.

docs.title: Self-improving agents
docs.text:
These papers study changes to agents or their improvement machinery. Their mechanisms help identify what a Meta-Evolve experiment would need to supply.

Work What changes and how it is judged Local connection Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM) Agent code is revised and tested; valid self-editing variants enter an archive. Archive management and parent selection stay fixed. Proposed DGM mapping Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM) Branch expansion uses estimated descendant productivity; evaluation allocation is a separate decision. Proposed HGM mapping, including the gap from TreeSearch Red Queen Gödel Machine Learned evaluators can change between epochs with fixed scoring rules; an independent anchor judges replacements. Evaluator governance and its limits

DGM and HGM mappings remain Design—not shipped. Red Queen is a research precedent for the narrower #251 proposal. These connections supply neither runnable integrations nor performance evidence.

docs.title: AlphaEvolve: algorithm discovery
docs.text: DeepMind describes a system combining Gemini-generated programs, automated evaluation, and evolutionary selection. Formulating a problem with an executable quality measure is central to that approach. Its reported discoveries are useful research context; the announcement does not establish a currently available self-service setup or its authoring requirements, so this page makes no access recommendation. DeepMind's announcement.

docs.title: What do Meta-Evolve's guarantees mean for my run?
Does it automatically save results or recover after a crash?
docs.text: Default local runs use in-memory storage. Pass Storage.durable(path) to save committed history for reopening and inspection. Resuming execution additionally requires a supported mode and registered, reconstructible components; persisting ordinary notebook callables does not make them resumable. See saving and recovery.

docs.title: Does replay call the model again?
docs.text: No. Replay reconstructs recorded facts without invoking proposers or evaluators. A fresh stochastic model call can produce a different answer; stored records do not promise identical regeneration. See run history.

docs.title: Is a spending limit a hard cap?
docs.text: No. The engine counts trials and evaluations and aggregates usage reported by your components. A monetary ceiling is enforced after reported charges: a call can exceed it before further work stops. Unknown billed spend stays unknown. The engine cannot verify a wrapper's billing report. See money and enforcement.

docs.title: Can candidate code change its own grader?
docs.text: The declared evaluator, budgets, and promotion rules remain outside candidate authority. However, ordinary local Python execution is not process isolation. Running untrusted code requires an appropriate execution boundary; see the source execution guide.

docs.title: Does it automatically use feedback or run evaluations in parallel?
docs.text: Feedback is explicit and off by default; the feedback guide shows how to supply it. Execution is serial by default; distributed mode supports explicit worker process backends. See execution profiles for supported controls and restrictions.

docs.title: Can I combine it with another optimizer?
docs.text: You can implement a callable that invokes another optimizer and returns a candidate, but that is integration work. Define artifact conversion, aggregate inner usage, handle failures, and keep selection data separate from final checks. No DSPy or OpenEvolve adapter is shipped. Our DSPy, GEPA, and OpenEvolve mappings identify remaining work; similar interfaces do not establish compatibility or reproduce an algorithm.

docs.title: What evidence supports improvement claims?
docs.text:
The parser scores come from independently grading handwritten revisions. They teach execution and selection, not model performance. Historical provider captures are listed with their limits in the evidence index. The release quickstart's live report belongs to #271; no retained report was attached as of 2026-09-16. A negative result is still evidence.

This comparison reports no head-to-head benchmark or broad superiority. Any future live claim must link the retained report and its exact configuration, baseline, failures, resource use, and final evaluation. A small demonstration cannot establish general performance.

For the research question of recursive self-improvement, see the survey and mechanism map.

docs.title: Where do I start?
docs.text: Run the parser tutorial, then replace its starting value, revision function, and measurement function for your own task. Choose a task guide for feedback, limits, or saving; an application for a larger example; or the API reference for parameters and return values.

docs.text:
Check dates and inspected versions appear below. Upstream documentation and main branches can change; these descriptions do not certify a package version. Capabilities absent from a source are unverified, not assumed unsupported. Choice guidance is our interpretation of the documented responsibilities.

docs.title: Trace one run through the kernel
docs.text:
After checkout setup, run the canonical example once and keep its two output lines in view. For a first introduction to the public API, start with the duration parser.

uv run python examples/learn/number_search/main.py

12
[0, 1, 2, 7, 12]

The short script enters one coordinator. The actual order is interleaved:

declaration
  → encode, evaluate, and atomically commit the seed
  → search decision and commit
  → proposal, candidate encoding, and commit
  → independent evaluation and commit
  → repeat until the committed stop decision
  → reopen the committed stream as a read-only Run

No stage branches on “number.” The codec handles representation, the proposer handles mutation, the evaluator handles measurement, and search handles the next decision.

docs.title: Build and serve documentation
docs.text:
From a checkout, build the complete site and serve it locally:

uv sync --locked --group docs
uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict
uv run python -m http.server --directory site

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. A saved documentation build includes its matching package ZIP. Repository collaborators can also download the meta-evolve-docs-<commit> artifact from a successful Docs workflow run on main. The artifact is private and retained for 14 days.

docs.title: Find the responsible component
docs.text:
Use this map to enter the trace at the behavior you want to change. The linked checks exercise specific contracts; the architecture owns the invariants and the programming model owns the API.

Responsibility Source entry Existing checks Declare and execute Experiment, Session Equivalent declarations and budget narrowing Preserve identity and history Domain identities, projection Task/run identity, distinct content occurrences Propose with authorized inputs Execution, proposal facts Proposer context and adapters Measure and account for work Evaluation, usage Evaluation facts before commitment Choose what to try next Greedy Shared search contract and limits Interpret a candidate policy Policy data, trusted interpreter Parent selection and hard budget, incomplete inner evidence Add a domain or integration Domain records, ports, adapters Published conformance suites, codec implementations Commit and reconstruct Coordinator, result views Atomic writes and conflicts Project authorized Git history Source observations, Git projection Mount, disposal, access, and tamper checks

For the integrated author API, follow these focused boundaries:

  • Plain callback invocation and historical invocation checks separate explicit context from ordinary Python defaults.
  • Preset allowance resolution and default-limit tests bind the effective budget once, before recording the policy.
  • Component resources and accounting tests separate reported costs from engine-owned counts. The existing encoding and evaluation boundaries lower these reports into durable Usage.
  • Run summaries check reporting independently of successful winner selection.

docs.title: 1. Declaration
docs.text:
examples/learn/number_search/main.py declares the task, seed, proposer, search preset, budget, and random seed. The root meta.run export reaches application/runtime.py.

runtime.run normalizes either declaration form and drives a Session. session_preparation.py chooses codecs, computes the effective budget, adapts callables, checks capabilities, prepares search, and derives run and task identities. Durable-local validation finishes before the coordinator can write an event.

docs.title: 2. Encoding
docs.text:
Preparation encodes the seed through CodecIndex.encode. A successor stays a Python value while the proposer works. encode_candidate in executors.py converts the returned value to a payload before proposal facts are built.

A codec's TypeError or ValueError means invalid candidate output and becomes a typed failure. Another exception is a codec defect and propagates. Codecs do not choose artifact IDs, parents, scores, or promotion.

docs.title: 3. Proposal
docs.text:
execution.py loads only the committed parent artifacts named by the trial. It builds a ProposerContext from recorded randomness, logical step, objectives, bounded context, and audited experience, then calls the replaceable proposer runner.

proposal_building.py checks usage and derivation authority, then builds the proposal, artifact occurrence, stable IDs, parent links, and provenance. proposal_completion.py commits those facts and drives any dependent evaluation. The proposer supplies content and evidence; it does not mint durable identity.

docs.title: 4. Evaluation
docs.text:
evaluation_execution.py calls the configured evaluator adapter, which decodes the committed artifact. build_evaluation then adds one evaluation charge, enforces effective budgets, creates stable evidence and evaluation IDs, and builds either measurements or a typed failure. The caller commits those facts.

The evaluator is outside candidate authority. A candidate can fail a task and receive a real low score. A broken evaluator, exhausted resource, or infrastructure fault carries no metric and cannot be ranked as poor candidate performance.

docs.title: 5. Search
docs.text:
Session._step drives this local run. A prepared policy reads committed SearchState and returns a decision. The coordinator records it before executing a trial; a stop decision ends the loop. Recovery continues the committed frontier.

Greedy's parent choice and retention rules live in policies/greedy.py, not in the coordinator. This is why BestOfN, Population, and a conforming custom policy use the same execution path.

docs.title: 6. Commitment
docs.text:
coordinator.py funnels every durable fact through commit_batch. It first folds the proposed events on a local projection and checks the same batch grammar recovery uses. Storage.commit then writes events and artifact occurrences together. Only a successful store commit advances the in-memory projection.

batch_envelopes.py builds the same event identities and causation chain for provisional folds and the final commit. Context selections and experience audit facts also use commit_batch, each as a separate one-event batch.

The seed follows the same rule through bootstrap.py: its declaration, occurrence, trial outcome, evidence, and evaluation form one genesis batch. A partial genesis is never a run.

docs.title: 7. Projection
docs.text:
projections.py rebuilds RunProjection by folding the ordered event stream. Replay consumes records; it never reruns the proposer, evaluator, context selector, or search policy.

results.py projects read-only best, trials, lineage, summary, and comparison views. The printed lineage follows committed artifact parent IDs. It omits rejected 16 because that occurrence is not an ancestor of the winning 12.

docs.title: When the procedure becomes the candidate
docs.text:
The two similarly named directories have different roles. policies/ contains search implementations such as Greedy. policy/ contains a PolicyArtifact and its trusted CandidatePolicy interpreter. The artifact declares parent selection and a voluntary trial limit; it cannot raise the enclosing budget.

In policy evolution, the outer proposer changes that data. The outer evaluator runs bounded inner experiments using the interpreter and captures their outcomes. Both levels use the same runtime and have their own identities and work counts. The candidate-policy checks show how parent selection changes lineage while the hard budget stays fixed.

Other methods choose what inner evidence to retain and which usage to forward. Compare policy evolution and AutoResearch before assuming that a saved outer run contains every inner history or total cost. The meta-evolution concept explains what further reuse and evidence would be needed to study recursive improvement.

docs.title: When the proposer uses Git
docs.text:
GitHistoryView asks the experience interface for authorized source observations. application/source_history.py builds their manifest; adapters/git_projection.py turns it into disposable Git metadata outside the candidate workspace. The proposer can inspect that view with ordinary Git commands during its session.

Artifact occurrences, evaluation references, and causal records remain framework data. Git commits represent only the permitted projection and are removed when the mount is disposed. The Git history checks exercise log/show/diff, cleanup, access declarations, and tamper rejection. The experience guide owns the read grants.

docs.title: Check source changes
docs.text:
From the repository root after checkout setup, run the same source checks as CI:

uv run --locked ruff check src
uv run --locked mypy

Ruff checks shipped Python sources for unused imports (F401) and undefined names (F821). Declare intentional re-exports explicitly with __all__ or from module import name as name. Run the relevant behavior tests from the component map above for the code you change.

Mypy checks application host interfaces in the source roots listed in pyproject.toml. Imported modules retain their types; diagnostics are limited to those roots. tests/typing/host_contracts.py checks the concrete coordinator against each host protocol. Add new host modules to the configured roots and include their implementation assignments in that file. Runtime conformance, transaction, and authority tests remain part of uv run pytest.

docs.title: Authority
docs.text: In proposal_building.py, list the fields copied from proposer output and the fields minted by core. Explain why moving artifact ID creation into the proposer would let a candidate overwrite history.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text: Change only random_seed in a temporary number-search run. Predict which run identity changes and which task identity stays fixed. Then find both inputs in session_preparation.py and run_support.py.

docs.title: Lineage
docs.text: Sketch the parent IDs for attempts 1, 6, 11, 16, and 12. Explain why two artifact occurrences with equal payload bytes still need distinct IDs.

docs.title: Budgets
docs.text: Account for the example's six evaluations and five successor trials. Identify where the seed is charged, where proposal usage is checked, and where evaluator usage is checked. No component may widen the effective budget.

docs.title: Typed failures
docs.text: Classify these outcomes: a candidate violates the task, a codec rejects the candidate type, the grader crashes, and a proposer exceeds its resource grant. Only the first can be an ordinary low score.

docs.title: Replay
docs.text: Read commit_batch beside replay_run_projection. Name the shared fold and grammar checks that keep “committed” equivalent to “recoverable.” Explain why replay must not ask the proposer for the same candidate again.

docs.title: Comparison validity
docs.text:
Use the CLI walkthrough to compare Greedy and BestOfN. Then list the declarations that must match before the winner is meaningful. A displayed winner is not evidence when task, evaluator, initial artifact, budget, proposer, or hidden component configuration changed.

Continue by purpose: compose a method, add an artifact domain, or follow a linked invariant test into its implementation. The harness guide teaches the current example; historical evidence retains the earlier design rationale.

docs.title: Durable trust
docs.text: What a durable store is trusted to be, and what its integrity checks do and do not prove. Split out of architecture, which owns the invariant this page explains.

docs.title: Nothing in a durable store is authenticated
docs.text:
Event ids derive from position — stable_id(EventId, "event", run_id, sequence) — not from content. Content digests are unkeyed SHA-256 over the JSON the writer supplied. Artifact digests hash that payload. There is no MAC, no signature and no key anywhere in the library.

Every check is therefore a self-consistency check, and self-consistency is exactly what someone who can write the file satisfies: they recompute the digests along with the edit.

docs.title: So the checks detect corruption, never tampering
docs.text:
Read them as answering "was this written correctly", never "was this written by someone entitled to". What they genuinely catch:

  • a truncated or partially applied write
  • a half-applied schema migration
  • a store written by an older library version, or by a foreign writer
  • a store whose artifact blobs and occurrence rows have drifted apart

That is worth having, and it is the whole of what is claimed.

docs.title: Why there is no check that reaches outside the record
docs.text:
There was almost one. run_id_for derives a run's id from its declaration, and the run id is what the caller opens by — so requiring a recorded genesis to still derive its own id would be the one check whose reference value does not live in the bytes under suspicion. It was built, reviewed, and reverted, and both reasons are worth keeping:

  • It bought nothing. The check needs the policy's identity key, which no registry-less reader can re-derive, so the key had to be recorded — and a run predating that field has to be skipped. That skip is a field of the same record, so blanking it walked past all four checks. The switch was as forgeable as everything else, which is this page's whole point.
  • It cost a false verdict. run_id_for folds in the context and experience specs, but a local-mode run commits those as separate batches after genesis. A run interrupted between them can never re-derive its own id, so every reader reported a perfectly good store as corrupt. Measured, not theorised.

The second reason is the general one: an id derived from the whole declaration cannot be re-derived from a prefix that legitimately lacks part of it. Any future attempt has to answer that before it answers forgery.

docs.title: What would change the claim
docs.text: A keyed MAC over event envelopes and occurrence rows, with the key held outside the store. That brings key management, rotation, what a keyless read does, the browser and read-only paths, and a migration for every existing store. It is a milestone of its own and no slice has claimed it.

docs.text: Choose something you want to improve. Each walkthrough takes you from a starting artifact to a measured result, with setup and runnable code on the page. For help changing one part of an experiment, use the task guides.

docs.title: Implementation Plan
docs.text: This page owns current package responsibilities and technical staging. The roadmap owns scope and acceptance; the programming model and architecture own shipped contracts. Historical implementation recipes are retained in pinned evidence.

docs.title: Staged package shape
docs.text:
Build only seams needed by the current gate. Existing packages divide by responsibility, not by levels of evolution:

Package Responsibility application Author declarations, shared preparation, execution, queries and recovery. domain Immutable durable records, identities and domain invariants. ports Narrow contracts required for replaceable components. adapters Callable normalization, artifacts, storage, workspaces and external integration. policies / policy Search/context implementations / candidate-policy interpretation. harness Declared mutable harness surfaces and their value semantics.

Use the contributor code tour for source/test owners. Do not pre-create destination modules or parallel evolution/RSI runtime packages.

docs.title: SoL-Pi: harness efficiency experiment
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. The roadmap gate owns scope, sequence, and acceptance. Keep the first implementation under examples/research/sol_pi/, using existing callable, artifact, evidence, and storage seams; create that directory only when implementation begins.

  • Start with validated Text JSON containing only declared mechanism settings. Keep runtime/model identity, pricing inputs, task splits, evaluator code, permissions, and budgets in experiment-owned declarations. Later code evolution can use an allowlisted SourceTree with independent validation.
  • Use one narrow runner boundary with deterministic and opt-in Pi implementations. Pin the upstream extension and run each evaluated configuration in a fresh isolated workspace/session. Runtime tool and conversation handling belongs there; Meta-Evolve's ContextPolicy selects inter-proposal evidence.
  • Keep capability filtering, nondominated retention, and deterministic final choice in an example-owned selection component. Use ordinary SearchProgram extension points if retention must guide parent choice; add no coordinator branch, built-in Pareto preset, or change to compare_harnesses semantics.
  • Publish measured outcomes through EvaluationResult, detailed call and cache observations through evidence, and counted costs through Resources. Include reducer and compaction calls; preserve incomplete accounting explicitly.
  • Record selection inputs, dispositions, and the frozen winner beside the committed run evidence. Reuse durable history for replay and the existing harness example's separation of development from later evaluation. Keep upstream runtime dependencies optional and outside the core package.

docs.title: SIFT: judge-guided agent evolution
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. The roadmap gate owns sequence, scope, and acceptance. Keep the sequential implementation under examples/research/sift/; create it only when implementation begins.

  • Represent editable agent code as an independently validated SourceTree. The shipped HarnessArtifact text/configuration surfaces do not express arbitrary agent-code changes. Reuse proposer workspaces and independent evaluator execution, with benchmark and model dependencies outside the core.
  • Keep comparison orchestration and immutable decision snapshots example-owned. Use a custom SearchProgram for rank-based sampling only after proving that its inputs reconstruct from committed observations. If the existing search view cannot expose those inputs, compose local runs through an explicit experiment-owned driver retaining run and artifact-occurrence references; do not hide mutable archive state in callbacks or call a live judge in next.
  • Derive the win matrix and Bradley–Terry strengths from retained pairwise records. Recompute rankings without rewriting earlier evaluations. Publish actual measurements through EvaluationResult, observations through evidence, and incurred resources through Resources; retain decision snapshots beside run history when existing records cannot represent them directly.
  • Keep the sequential driver synchronous. Neither Session.step() nor current distributed cohorts provide evaluation-only scheduling or speculative expansion. A later runtime proposal must define staged evaluation identity, pending-node eligibility, provisional estimates, priority changes, completion ordering, recovery, and budget settlement before asynchronous work begins.

docs.title: Milestone 11: trusted distribution
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. The full trusted-worker system remains the active runtime work. M11.0–M11.4 are Shipped, including explicit process backends alongside default inline execution and trusted-worker administration. The roadmap owns supported policies, count-only ceilings, excluded experience and remaining slices. The M11 design owns state transitions; the verification record retains source revisions, regression evidence, and the separate stack integration checks, and the administration record retains M11.4's.

Work, lease and worker state live outside the run event stream so clock-driven renewals cannot change policy-observed versions. Durable enqueue/acceptance and the authorizing logical batch commit atomically. Budgets are derived from committed facts, not an independent mutable accounting ledger. Cohort width is part of policy identity, not an execution overlay; retries keep distinct work attempts under the same logical trial.

The batch grammar validates one batch; the stream grammar validates interleaved trial-keyed ordering. Decision transitions derive the cohort boundary once, and the ordinary writer uses a cohort of one. PolicyDecisionMade.cohort_base is omitted at its default to preserve old bytes. Derived evaluation disposition keeps owed, terminally skipped and allocation-overrun states distinct so replay can both reject forbidden evaluations and accept historical overages.

M11.3's durable prerequisites resolve inputs before claiming, renew inline calls and fence each dispatcher commit. A recorded deterministic completion failure ends its item on recovery; other failures retain bounded retry behavior. Calls may overlap after an aborted drive, but only one result is accepted. InputsUnavailable is the root exception for ordinary artifact read failures; it keeps retryable input faults separate from InvalidDecision.

Cross-process claims and Duplicate/Stale submission use the existing dispatcher settlement path. Completion-stage causes determine recovery without adding a poison flag. Worker processes authenticate and compare fingerprints at admission, then reconstruct executors from the recorded start. Transport admission reserves identity before accepting a connection; reconnect retains unanswered completed results across socket failures. These responsibilities stay in distributed, outside coordinator policy decisions and durable domain records.

Trusted-worker administration (#203) keeps the allow-list in the store, behind schema 5, and writes it only from the operator's workers verb, outside application/ and distributed/; the host is handed a reader's lookup. Fault/load tests (#204) and the reserved examples/research/trusted_workers/ demonstration (#205) remain later slices. Durable accepted outcomes and promotion stay authoritative; liveness and queue estimates may be ephemeral. Worker-process placement adds no further root API, paid concurrency or distributed experience.

docs.title: Author API revision
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. Publication remains #319's gate; the selected source changes are Shipped. The release handoff and roadmap own integration, compatibility and version policy. The implementation continues through shared preparation, existing callable adapters, immutable snapshots and verified manifests.

Do not build a legacy invocation engine or weaken source verification to continue old runs. Read historical records independently of execution; migrate storage only through the explicit writable path. No new procedure class, count renaming, objective model or export reorganization is selected for 0.2.

docs.title: Milestone 12: contributed and federated network
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. After M11, introduce only the signed manifests, scoped trust and filtered-subgraph exchange required by the federation acceptance gate. Keep redaction, retraction and causal provenance explicit. Do not implement the reserved examples/research/federated_exchange/ before its gate.

docs.title: Interface staging
docs.text: Current replaceability lives in narrow ports and configured component identities. External systems translate at adapters; new storage, evaluators, policies and artifact domains must not require coordinator special cases. Use extension conformance to prove a new implementation; future remote infrastructure does not justify unused interfaces today.

docs.title: What not to build first
docs.text: Do not add speculative modules, custom graph/vector infrastructure, peer-to-peer economies, universal agent communication, unbounded self-modification or learned scheduling without a current acceptance case and baseline. Scientific claims need domain evidence and replication. Operational dashboards and remote execution need their own capability and authority boundary.

docs.title: Near-term definition of done
docs.text: Complete the current roadmap gate, keeping the callable path small, focused tests deterministic, artifacts immutable and external authority intact. Existing contracts, runnable examples and source-generated reference must agree; the repository completion check owns the shared criteria.

docs.title: Pre-milestone API spike
docs.text: Status: Shipped. The historical spike established the callable story. Its pinned findings are provenance; current declarations belong to the programming model.

docs.title: Milestone 1: deterministic in-memory kernel
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Immutable records, narrow ports and sequential execution established domain semantics and the ordinary callable path. Current port signatures come from the API reference.

docs.title: Milestone 2: replaceable search policies
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Search implementations consume common transitions and records. Search reference owns their current declarations; the coordinator stays independent of policy choice.

docs.title: Milestone 3: shared experience
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Audited readers, context policies and observation-ledger validation share the experience contract and causal provenance. No ambient memory is added.

docs.title: Milestone 4: durable local kernel
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Filesystem content-addressed artifacts and SQLite event storage compose atomically. Durable trust and recovery own current reconstruction and migration rules.

docs.title: Milestone 5: executable artifacts
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Source codecs, patch proposers, workspace/sandbox adapters and external graders implement source improvement without domain branches in the coordinator.

docs.title: Milestone 6: SDK proposer boundary proof
docs.text: Status: Shipped. The user calls their SDK inside a proposer/evaluator. SDK reference owns typed results, auditing and hard removal of the old first-party provider adapters; no provider ABC is required.

docs.title: Milestone 7: cross-domain local v1
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Cross-domain examples, CLI, browser and conformance exercise the shared contracts. Historical repairs no longer prescribe the current package layout.

docs.title: Milestone 8: harness evolution
