docs.title: Status vocabulary
docs.text:
Status Meaning Shipped Available in the current source package and covered by its contracts. Experimental/live-only Requires a live integration; each page identifies its offline checks and any captured runs. Design—not shipped A proposal beyond the current implementation boundary.

Shipped guides open with their subject. Experimental and proposal pages show an explicit notice. A historical decision can describe shipped behavior even when it lives here; release publication is tracked separately from source availability.

docs.title: Author API comparison decisions
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The adopted changes are implemented in source; #319 still owns coordinated publication. The comparisons below retain their historical baselines.

September 18, 2026: #314's optional decisions, following the foundation. The executable study and evidence record retain the baselines, assertions, receipts, and limits. These engineering traces establish semantic properties; they are not independent usability measurements.

docs.title: 1. Adopt budget-led preset defaults; retain counting names
docs.text:
The duplicate ordinary allowance is avoidable:

# Historical baseline: repeat 25, or opt into max_trials=None.
task = meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate, budget=meta.Budget(trials=25))
experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=seed, proposer=propose,
                             search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=25))

# Implemented declaration, selected for 0.2.
experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=seed, proposer=propose,
                             search=meta.Greedy())

Both forms still require choosing a proposer, evaluator, and external ceiling. The alternative removes one duplicated amount and the need to know an opt-in sentinel. It adds no public import, callback wrapper, or authority-bearing object. Experiment(search=None) follows the same ordinary Greedy rule.

Selected rule: for Greedy, BestOfN, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch, omitted/None max_trials uses the effective finite Budget.trials. If no finite trial ceiling exists, resolve to the existing finite fallback: 20, or 100 for TreeSearch. Keeping TreeSearch's established fallback avoids an unrelated search change. Explicit integers keep their voluntary-stop meaning; they never widen external authority. improve(trials=20) retains its current small, bounded contract. BestOfK, custom search, and candidate-policy programs keep their own meaning; do not inject an ordinary preset limit into them.

Resolve once in shared preset binding after #315 resolves the execution budget. Persist a concrete integer in search configuration before work; reconstruction uses that recorded integer. No new event, coordinator branch, or storage schema is needed. Exact policy manifests changed; historical replay remains supported.

Evidence: with a 25-attempt task budget, the baseline bare Greedy performed 20 attempts; the adopted default performed 25. This is an intentional default change, not a claim of an algorithmic improvement. Explicit equivalent configurations produced identical histories. Zero, two, and unbounded task allowances were exercised across all five presets; failed proposals still terminate when only evaluation/token ceilings exist. Custom search stopped at one attempt and BestOfK at its own two-attempt limit. Wide cohorts remain refused locally; the separate serial distributed capture establishes their admitted recovery path.

Migration: write an explicit old limit to preserve an old declaration's work amount. max_trials=None without a finite task/run ceiling changes from an error to finite fallback; document this alongside bare-default changes. Keep existing stop-reason precedence when budget and voluntary limit coincide.

Retain Budget.trials, Usage.trials, improve(trials=...), max_trials, and Run.trials(). The experiment did not establish a benefit sufficient to rename all of them together. Teach that attempts exclude the seed, the history includes its bootstrap record, and evaluations include authorized seed evaluation.

docs.title: 2. Retain ordered objectives
docs.text:
# Retained public form: primary objective first.
meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate,
          objectives=(meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=2), meta.Minimize("cost")))

# Compared alternative, isolated in the study.
primary_task(evaluator=evaluate, objective=meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=2),
             metrics=(meta.Minimize("cost"),))

The alternative makes primary intent explicit but adds another keyword and a factory; it still needs both metric directions, required-measurement rules, and primary-only search semantics. No wrapper or required author decision disappears. Keeping Minimize under a keyword called metrics also needs an explanation that it configures alternate queries, not mixed-direction search.

Both declarations selected quality 2 and cost 0 under the same history; scalar evaluation, threshold stopping, missing required metrics, and Specialists were checked. Specialists still uses the primary direction for its metric frontiers. Neither spelling establishes Pareto optimization. Retain the tuple and teach its ordering beside the declaration. No migration or new durable identity is needed; a future objective change requires new evidence and a new issue.

docs.title: 3. Adopt resource-only component reports
docs.text:
# Historical SDK result and nested forwarding; no longer the current contract.
meta.ProposalResult(candidate=candidate, usage=meta.Usage(tokens=7, spend_micros=None))
meta.EvaluationResult(metrics=metrics, usage=inner.usage().without_counts)

# Implemented authoring surface, selected for 0.2.
meta.ProposalResult(candidate=candidate, usage=meta.Resources(tokens=7, spend_micros=None))
meta.EvaluationResult(metrics=metrics, usage=inner.usage().resources)

The adopted design introduces one immutable Resources(tokens=0, spend_micros=0, wall_seconds=0.0) value. It has no trial/evaluation fields. Run/domain Usage retains its current counts and serialized meaning; Usage.resources projects the three resource dimensions. Rich author returns use Resources; plain candidate, scalar, and mapping returns remain direct. Keep structural/kernel outcome records on their existing Usage boundary.

Normalize Resources to zero-count Usage once at the adapter boundary. Rich result construction must reject engine-count fields rather than silently give components the impression that those counts are authoritative. Preserve all current value validation and failure accounting. The study converts explicitly only because it runs against 0.1; authors must not need to_usage() wrappers in the shipped alternative. Migrate rich Usage returns in the same release; retaining durable/domain Usage does not imply retaining two author conventions.

This adds one public type but removes two irrelevant component fields and makes the nested projection state what it returns. Both SDK and nested policy evaluation need that distinction. It does not remove the author's decision about which work to charge. Retained inner history must not charge again; forward inner resources plus the evaluator's own resources exactly once.

Evidence: two SDK proposals retained 14 tokens with unknown spend; two billed failures retained 10 tokens and 6 micro-USD with only the seed evaluation. Resources rejected a trial-count constructor argument and preserved unknown spend through aggregation. Policy evolution retained ten inner stores while its development outer run recorded two attempts, three evaluations, and 14 tokens. Resource projection equalled the existing count-stripped total.

Keep spend_micros=0 as known free and None as unknown. The frozen old histories retain both unknown-spend cases, including refusal of further work under a monetary ceiling. Summed elapsed work is not wall-clock duration or hard preemption. #321 added integrated coverage for fresh/resumed resource conversion, partial failures, overages and unknown spend.

docs.title: 4. Retain Experiment; do not add Improver in 0.2
docs.text:
# Retained reuse.
other = dataclasses.replace(experiment, task=other_task, seed=other_seed)

# Compared alternative: one extra object, with the same external authorities.
procedure = Improver(proposer=propose, search=search, context=feedback)
other = procedure.experiment(task=other_task, seed=other_seed,
                             experience=grant, registry=registry)

The sketch groups proposer/search/feedback selection. Task, independent evaluation, hard budget, seed, access grant, random seed, and registry remain explicit outside it. It does not remove their required decisions or turn live callables into serializable candidate data. Freezing an outer object does not freeze its functions or mutable registry.

Reusing across two tasks/seeds produced equivalent results using both forms. The study then reconstructed each real declaration through the sketch while running the actual methods: 15 ordinary runs in AutoResearch, 13 in policy evolution, and 15 in ACE, per comparison side. Values, counts, failures, lineage, budgets, selected evidence, and retention agreed. Independently allocated storage paths were normalized explicitly; that is not an assertion that every storage-bearing event byte is identical.

The class did not remove the existing recipe interpreter in AutoResearch or the policy-suite/episode protocol in policy evolution. ACE still required development, search, consolidation, and final checking. Its 14 wrapper sessions included six during search; the fixture bills zero resources, so equal zero resource totals do not prove that those extra sessions are free in a live run. AutoResearch retains score summaries of inner work; policy evolution retains inner histories; ACE retains search history plus in-memory phase outcomes. Do not flatten those distinctions into a generic run result.

The requirement for demonstrated simplification in two compositions was not met. Retain Experiment and explicit Python orchestration. Teach the conceptual procedure as composition of existing values; data-only candidate configuration still selects permitted behavior through trusted interpretation. No new core class, registry placement rule, serialization, or coordinator is authorized.

docs.title: Integration disposition
docs.text:
Issues #315–#317 implemented the foundation. The adopted comparisons shipped in separate children under #313: #320, preset allowances and #321, component resources. Issue #318 integrated examples, imports and one migration guide; #319 will release them together. Ordered objectives, procedure objects, count renames, root-export pruning, and changing the default meaning of unknown spend are closed as retain current behavior for 0.2, not unresolved requirements that block the release.

Keep ordinary imports at the root and advanced APIs in their existing namespaces. The study needed Specialists from meta_evolve.policies; hiding ordinary declarations behind additional namespaces did not help any journey. Preserve strict Run.compare() controls: a different-proposer scientific study needs its own explicit protocol, not a weaker comparator.

docs.title: Author API foundation decision
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The adopted source contracts are implemented; coordinated package publication remains #319’s separate gate.

Decision date: September 18, 2026. This is #314's foundation handoff under #313. The programming model now owns implemented behavior; this record retains decisions and release treatment. The roadmap owns release scope and policy. The evidence record identifies both installed baselines and the historical captures. The separate comparison decisions finish the optional review.

docs.title: Foundation contracts
docs.text:
Slice Frozen decision Implementation owner Partial ceilings Execution overrides inherit every omitted/None dimension; explicit widening raises ValueError before work or committed run facts; zero is a real ceiling. #315 Plain proposer callbacks Parent positional; framework input only through named keyword-only context. Normal configuration defaults stay Python defaults; no probe calls or retry after body TypeError. #316 Registered invocation Automatically verify framework binding and dispatch source with the proposer implementation; refuse incompatible resume before any component work. #316 Run reporting Extend RunSummary with lifecycle/rankability/stop reason; optional score and empty winning lineage when nothing ranks; one coherent snapshot. #317 Selection/comparison Winner queries remain strict. Comparison requires two measurements; an absent score is neither a tie nor a losing score. Preserve controls and error precedence. #317

The programming model owns callback binding, per-dimension budget rule, comparison controls, and error cases. These are decisions, not open recommendations. Implementation can refine private seams without changing the public rules; a changed rule needs a recorded decision.

The callback distinction is by selected role. The explicit structural port still receives .propose(parent, context). Preserve declared-runner precedence, structural versus callable-object selection, wrapped registered references, validation hooks, and exact context identity. The binding/dispatch dependencies must cover all these routes while retaining the user's declared dependencies. Do not hash the entire library or ask users to register its own adapter code.

The digest experiment establishes that a new dependency changes the manifest of an unchanged callback, and that the existing resume verifier refuses it before work. It is not a replacement for #316's actual adapter integration and route tests. Do not weaken source verification to make old runs continue.

docs.title: Reporting and command outcomes
docs.text:
Situation Summary run / resume CLI exit Successful inspect exit Complete, rankable; seed may still win Measured score and selected lineage 0 0 Complete, unrankable Score None, empty winning lineage, retained costs 1 0 Incomplete, rankable Measured score, incomplete lifecycle, no stop reason Same rankability rule if rendered 0 Incomplete, unrankable Score None, incomplete lifecycle, retained costs Same rankability rule if rendered 0 Missing/corrupt history or execution error Existing typed error; no fabricated summary Existing domain-error exit Existing domain-error exit Invalid command usage Argument error 2 2

Do not claim the execution commands return normally after every interruption. The table defines rendering of a valid returned result; execution exceptions keep their existing behavior.

The distributed capture adds a required case: admitted genesis before seed evaluation. It is a valid incomplete, unrankable history. In the captured pre-change runtime, inspect() and usage() raised SearchNotStarted there. Issue #317 now derives committed usage without requiring projection.search_state; summary, inspection and usage agree. The historical capture reader uses validated replay for this state and identifies that limitation. Pending work is not completed usage.

docs.title: Release treatment
docs.text:
The selected boundary is one coordinated 0.2.0 release, subject to #319's final version/publication check. There is no mandatory intermediate compatibility release. The user explicitly authorized revising the former through-1.x promises. The following inventory determines what this release actually changes:

Surface Disposition in 0.2 Migration run(task=..., seed=..., proposer=...) Retain; typed Experiment is the documentation default. No forced rewrite. Dictionary CLI factories Retain with the existing deprecation warning. Returning Experiment remains preferred; no removal is scheduled by #314. Positional inferred callback context Replace with explicit keyword-only opt-in for plain callables. def propose(parent, *, context); review optional ctx/_context and variadics manually. Structural proposer port Retain. Do not rewrite adapter methods as ordinary callbacks. Whole-budget override interpretation Replace with partial restrictions. Omitted fields inherit; some previously rejected calls now execute. Winner-dependent summary Replace with reportable unrankable outcomes. Check rankability / primary_score is not None; migrate direct dataclass construction. Preset allowance defaults Replace, as specified by the comparison decision. Set explicit max_trials=20 (100 for TreeSearch) to retain the old voluntary limit. Rich component resource reports Replace their author-facing resource value with Resources; retain run/domain Usage. usage=Resources(...); forward inner.usage().resources. trials, history methods, objectives, Experiment Retain. No counting rename, Task rewrite, or Improver migration. Existing root/advanced imports Retain; add Resources with its implementation. #318 organizes discovery by author role; no export-count target. SearchProgram.next() / functional search / BestOfK Retain their extension and algorithm contracts. No unrelated coordinator or policy migration.

No unrelated public spelling is removed just because a breaking release is available. The adopted comparison changes were implemented by #320 for preset defaults and #321 for resources.

docs.title: Compatibility evidence and handoff
docs.text:
Seven physical schema-4 stores capture old complete and interrupted runs. The matching installed runtime resumed every case with identical final events and usage to uninterrupted execution. The #297 reference package read all seven unchanged and refused every resume before work because exact policy/context source changed, despite those package changes being docstrings only.

Supported old histories remain readable. Supported schema migrations are explicitly writable operations on a copy, never a read-only side effect. An old callback's unchanged source is insufficient evidence of invocation compatibility. Resume requires compatible verified components and, where the execution mode requires it, the recorded environment.

Issues #315–#317 implemented these contracts; #318 integrated their migration and import journey. The linked verification records retain the source evidence. #319 owns integrated tests, fresh installs, release artifacts, and the deployed docs check.

Decision #314 neither publishes the package nor demonstrates M11 concurrency or RSI.

docs.title: Author API release verification matrix
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This page specifies the checks for the #319 release plan. It is an implementation checklist, not a record that a 0.2.0 package has passed. Reuse the maintained CI/Docs workflows and existing tests; add a test only for an uncovered distribution or release contract.

docs.title: Candidate and artifacts
docs.text:
Every receipt identifies the release source commit R, chosen version, clean source state, dependency lock hash, and resolved build/tool environment. Use SHA-256 for each wheel, sdist, documentation source ZIP, and retained docs archive. Record package source file hashes separately from archive hashes.

Required artifact checks:

  • Wheel and sdist agree on distribution name/version, Requires-Python, dependency/extra metadata, CLI entry points, README content type, license, and project URLs. Inspect rendered README links outside GitHub's context.
  • Core imports need no optional browser or provider package. Installing the browser extra supplies its actual dependencies and retains required templates, JavaScript, CSS, and py.typed in the installed distribution.
  • The sdist rebuilds outside the repository without .git, untracked files, checkout imports, or files absent from the archive. Its rebuilt wheel installs the intended same code/resources as the release wheel.
  • Source ZIP contents and package source match R; do not equate its bytes or hash with the differently structured sdist. The existing deterministic ZIP content check remains in force.
  • Installed meta_evolve.__file__ resolves inside the selected environment's non-editable installation. Report importlib.metadata.version("meta-evolve") and package file hashes; equal version strings alone do not establish equality.
  • Inspect expected archive contents, including optional package data. Do not use a build that accidentally includes local credentials, caches, or work directories; building a clean tracked revision supplies this boundary.

docs.title: Proposed environment coverage
docs.text:
The release owner must select and record the support matrix before claiming support. The existing >=3.12 metadata is an installation constraint, not proof that every future interpreter and platform has been tested.

Environment Proposed required evidence Ubuntu, repository-pinned Python 3.12 Existing full deterministic suite, compile step, five canonical examples, Docs workflow, and separate wheel/sdist installs. Ubuntu, Python 3.13 and 3.14 Separate wheel/sdist core, CLI, history, and browser-extra smoke checks. Add full runtime/profile coverage before claiming the same full-suite assurance as 3.12. macOS, Python 3.12 Separate wheel/sdist smoke plus relevant existing host/confinement checks; retain actual outcomes rather than treating Ubuntu results as macOS evidence. Other interpreters/platforms No new certification from this gate without corresponding evidence. Preserve explicit runtime capability refusals.

This is a proposal, not a new supported-platform declaration. If a smaller matrix is selected, narrow the claims explicitly. Installer success does not prove confinement, timeout enforcement, or multiprocess support. Serial distributed execution remains the only implemented distributed regime.

docs.title: Installed-package smoke
docs.text:
Run these in separate fresh wheel and sdist environments with working directories outside the checkout and no checkout PYTHONPATH. Copy the small required example/fixture inputs explicitly; do not let the test runner import the source package through its own development installation.

Check Expected outcome Core import and metadata Correct version/origin, expected public and namespaced imports, no browser/provider dependency needed for core work. First parser loop Credential-free callable example performs its declared attempts; seed/evaluation counts and selected value match the maintained example. Partial budget Sparse tightening preserves other ceilings; explicit widening refuses before work. Callback input Keyword-only context works, ordinary optional configuration retains defaults, positional framework context gives its migration error. Rich resource reports Resources is accepted, author Usage rejected with a useful error, nested resource projection preserves unknown spend and engine-owned outer counts. Summary and CLI Failed/incomplete runs remain reportable; score absence differs from zero. CLI run/resume/inspect exit and stream behavior match the migration contract. Durable history Create a registered run, reopen it in a fresh process, and resume an interrupted copy with the same verified environment/source. Browser extra Templates/static assets are present; the existing read-only browser path renders the installed run without acquiring write/execution authority. Documented downloads Maintained extracted parser/prompt and reference examples run with the installed interpreter. Simulated SDK cases retain usage/failure behavior without paid calls.

Use the existing META_EVOLVE_LESSON_PYTHON mechanism for downloaded lessons where applicable, and retain its proof of no checkout imports. A narrow shared smoke script is sufficient for new wheel/sdist coverage. Keep packaging tool dependencies out of the runtime library dependency set.

docs.title: Historical compatibility
docs.text:
Read frozen originals; perform resumptions and writable schema operations only on disposable copies. Record before/after file hashes and serialized facts. Keep fixture component source and import identities frozen.

Existing evidence Release assertion tests/fixtures/api_v01/stores and test_api_v01_history.py All seven captures remain readable: completed, failed, optional context/inherited limits/feedback, variadic, unknown spend, unknown capped spend, and pre-bootstrap serial distributed history. pre_315_budget_override and test_run_budget_override_history.py Historical effective budget and facts remain intact; current partial/full equivalent declarations agree; incompatible old source refuses. pre_316_invocation and test_proposer_invocation_history.py Changed invocation is detected for unchanged optional/variadic callback source, with no component calls or new facts on refusal. v3_durable_run, existing schema and read-only tests Supported old schema reading/migration follows the existing capability boundary. API migration does not make schema upgrades a read-only side effect. Current registered resume, interruption, resource, and distributed tests Same verified runtime continues exactly from recorded work; defaults and budgets are not recalculated and counts/costs are not duplicated.

The broad historical test permits verified continuation or an explicit mismatch so it can also run against its original package. A release receipt must pin the actual expected outcome for R; it must not pass merely because any refusal occurred. Record which manifest or environment check refused the run.

Current integration can encounter changed policy source before changed callback wiring. Preserve the separate direct proposer-manifest assertion so policy drift does not mask an untested invocation change. Do not edit recorded manifests to force a desired error order.

The 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 version change can itself alter the distributed environment fingerprint, which includes installed distribution versions and package source. An expected historical environment refusal is different from a current-runtime resume regression. Test same-package execution/resume in a stable environment; installing test tools or extras between those steps can legitimately change the recorded environment too.

Keep old environments/source artifacts reconstructible from retained hashes and patches. Do not regenerate old stores using the release implementation, replace source digests, or suppress environment verification.

docs.title: Runtime and authority coverage
docs.text:
Run the maintained suite on R; use these owners to investigate a failure, not as a second permanently copied command inventory:

Concern Existing starting points Partial ceilings and resolution test_run_budget_overrides.py, test_run_budget_override_resume.py, test_experiment.py, test_session.py Context and manifests Callable adapter/contracts, proposer seam, invocation history, manifest and source-verification tests Summary/query coherence test_run_summary_records.py, test_run_summary_snapshots.py, inspection, comparisons, CLI and browser tests Preset allowance test_preset_defaults.py, test_preset_budget_inheritance.py, policy manifest and cohort tests Physical resources test_component_resources.py, normalization, monetary/unknown-spend, nested policy and method-specific accounting tests Composition and authority Policy evolution, AutoResearch, ACE, experience grants, lineage, workspace, and conformance tests

Require factual cost and lineage preservation across failure/recovery; no candidate may change external caps, evaluator/private data, access grants, or promotion. Search selection is not deployment authority. Do not flatten method stages or describe AutoResearch's outer-only accounting as total inner spend.

docs.title: Documentation and public installation
docs.text:
Before publication, build strictly from R and execute the maintained rendered, route, source-extraction, downloadable-example, and installed-SDK checks. Revisit changed installation/version text, long signatures, migration links, code copying, and narrow layouts. Reuse #318's observations for unchanged surfaces with source provenance; do not relabel its old review as a new review.

After publication, check the real public artifacts:

  • Index version and each file hash equal the retained release artifact; install the pinned public version from a fresh environment with cache/checkout sources excluded. Force a source install separately rather than accidentally selecting the cached wheel. Preserve dependency provenance.
  • GitHub tag resolves to R; release assets/notes identify the same version and package bytes. Preserve the documented old-run compatibility restrictions.
  • Public .source-commit equals R; the Pages build names the recorded docs repository commit. An HTTP success alone is not revision verification.
  • Public install/start-here, API reference, 0.2 migration, durability and component-resource routes load. Download the actual source ZIP and compare its hash, package metadata, and source manifest to the candidate build.
  • The independent verifier required by the release-owner process records their own environment, public installation commands, result, and limitations. Automated checks and a familiarized internal walkthrough do not replace it.

docs.title: Evidence receipt and stop conditions
docs.text:
Keep a small machine-readable receipt plus a readable verification record. No new public model or release service is needed. Required receipt fields:

Group Retained data Candidate Version, tag, source SHA, clean/patch state, lock/source hashes, build tools and metadata Artifacts File names, archive SHA-256 values, package-file manifest, build/CI artifact IDs and retained locations Verification OS/Python/install source, package origin, exact commands, results/counts/skips, logs and hosted run links Compatibility Frozen fixture hashes, read outcomes, actual resume/refusal reason, event/call-count evidence and current-runtime recovery Publication Index URLs/hashes, GitHub release/tag, docs source/deploy commits and Pages result, downloaded public ZIP hash Acceptance Release-scope decision, residual limits, final publication authorization, independent verification and issue closure links

A failing required job, missing public artifact, hash/revision mismatch, missing applicable acceptance, or unexplained compatibility outcome prevents closure. Do not downgrade checks to warnings, silently add skips, or infer a waiver from earlier local passes. Rerun affected gates after a fix; a new distribution must receive fresh installed-package verification before publication.

docs.title: Verify and publish the author API release: plan for #319
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 18, 2026 for #319, under #313. This plans the coordinated 0.2.0 package release. It does not publish a package, create a tag, change package metadata, deploy documentation, or certify the broader MVP.

The roadmap owns the acceptance gate; the foundation and comparison decisions own the selected API. The release checks below own the concrete verification matrix. Use the current programming model and architecture for shipped meaning.

docs.title: What is already complete
docs.text:
Inspected September 18 Evidence and implication Clean main at 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267 PR #324 merged the integrated API. Select a later release commit after version/packaging changes; this is the planning baseline. #314–#318, #320, and #321 are closed Their native issue states establish that #319 is the remaining API child. The parent body's older unchecked boxes are stale, not evidence of missing source work. Hosted CI and Docs passed on that main commit Runtime run and Docs run. These are baseline passes, not passes for a future version-bumped candidate. Public docs identify the same source Remote docs commit 8cf9810d864aeaf7c07b9945ebda5667f0a2bf00, successful Pages build, and the public .source-commit identify 1607afbb…. The adjacent local docs checkout is older and must not be used as the publication baseline. Package metadata and lock still identify 0.1.0 The version was intentionally held until this gate. Integrated source and published package availability are separate facts. No GitHub releases; no v0.2.0 tag found Recheck all matching release/tag forms immediately before release. No version has been reserved by this plan. Public PyPI project JSON returned 404 This is an inventory observation, not proof of name availability, account ownership, or upload authority.

The #318 verification record already covers the six authoring journeys, supported historical reads, fresh source-ZIP installation, and desktop/narrow rendering. Preserve it. Its local full run reported a process-cleanup failure followed by a passing sandbox rerun; the linked hosted main runs subsequently passed. Do not rewrite the earlier observation as a clean local full-suite pass.

The selected release keeps Experiment, ordered objectives, existing counting names and imports, keyword run, and dictionary CLI factories. It ships partial budget restrictions, explicit callback context, winner-independent summaries, budget-led preset defaults, and Resources. No Improver, new coordinator, concurrent worker implementation, or further API redesign belongs to #319.

docs.title: 0. Set the release scope and publication ownership
docs.text:
Recommended scope: a focused 0.2.0 author API release, with the full MVP tracked separately. This scope choice is awaiting Salah's response at plan preparation. It is not inferred from the pre-1.0 compatibility reset.

There is a real overlap with existing release work:

Owner Relationship to #319 #268 — MVP scope Requires completion of M11 concurrency, live-workflow evidence, environment claims, and independent acceptance beyond this API revision. Remains open. #272 — Distribution verification Owns wheel/sdist installation, browser assets, matrix CI, and a repeatable publishing procedure. Implement/reuse this seam rather than create a competing packaging system. #276 — Publication Names Salah as final acceptance/publication owner, Quancore as procedure owner, and Bhasker as independent post-publication verifier. Retain these responsibilities unless explicitly revised.

Before upload, record whether this is the narrow API cut or the full MVP and which existing acceptance requirements apply. If the narrow cut is selected, record that scope explicitly in the release-owner handoff; leave incomplete MVP issues open and make no concurrency/live-quality claim. If the full MVP is selected, #319 can prepare the distributions and verification but publication waits for that release's remaining gates. Do not silently waive them.

Confirm the exact PyPI project/version, publication account, and supported environment matrix with the existing release owner. GitHub administrator access was verified for both repositories; it does not establish PyPI ownership. Use the proposed matrix in the checks page as a concrete starting point.

docs.title: 1. Add the missing distribution and publication seam
docs.text:
Only ci.yml and docs.yml currently exist. Runtime CI tests the checkout; Docs CI verifies an installed source ZIP. Neither builds, validates, and tests both release distributions or uploads to PyPI. No existing release workflow or standalone publishing procedure was found in the source checkout.

Extend the existing CI packaging responsibility with a small, deterministic installed-package smoke entry point. It must work against an interpreter and artifact supplied by the caller, outside the checkout. Reuse examples and history checks; do not invent another acceptance framework.

Use one reviewed publication workflow or the existing owner's equivalent repeatable procedure. Keep build/verification separate from the upload step. The upload consumes the exact artifacts already checked, with the same hashes; it must not rebuild a different wheel or follow a moving branch.

For GitHub Actions, prefer a protected publication environment and PyPI Trusted Publishing, with OIDC permission confined to the upload job. This avoids a long-lived package token in the repository. Pin reviewed action/tool versions when implementing. See PyPI's publishing instructions.

If this is the first PyPI upload, configure and verify the appropriate pending publisher for the actual repository, workflow, environment, and account. A pending publisher does not reserve a project name; recheck before upload. See creating a project through Trusted Publishing. If access is missing, finish build/checks and the concrete handoff; identify the account/configuration action needed instead of improvising another index.

TestPyPI is optional for rehearsing the upload mechanism. It neither satisfies public-PyPI verification nor establishes ownership of the production name. Publishing remains an explicit later release action, never a side effect of ordinary PR tests or a docs build.

docs.title: 2. Prepare and freeze one release candidate
docs.text:
Use a focused release-preparation PR after the packaging seam is usable:

  1. Set pyproject.toml to the selected release version and update its own distribution entry in uv.lock. Review any unrelated dependency movement.
  2. Validate metadata, Python requirements, license, README rendering and links, CLI entry point, extras, and source/docs/issue URLs. Add missing public project URLs where needed; keep unrelated packaging cleanup out of scope.
  3. Replace current-install guidance that says the package still reports 0.1.0 in the migration/status pages. Preserve 0.1.0 inside historical captures, source patches, and dated evidence. Do not globally replace version strings.
  4. Prepare release notes from the existing migration guide: five changes, retained forms, externally owned authority, supported environments, and read-versus-resume limitations. Existing deterministic examples do not become live-model evidence in the announcement.
  5. Merge/reconcile the preparation and identify a clean, immutable commit R. Record the exact lock and source tree. Build all final artifacts from R.

R is a plan symbol, not a literal git ref. A source/version/docs change after freezing it creates a new candidate and invalidates affected evidence. A later verification-record commit can describe R; it must not silently move the tag or be substituted for the tested source in publication.

docs.title: 3. Build and verify the distributions
docs.text:
Build the wheel and source distribution through the declared Hatchling backend using a recorded toolchain. Record the resolved build backend as well as uv, Python, and runtime/test dependencies: the current unbounded hatchling build-system requirement is not pinned merely because uv.lock is recorded. Use a scoped build constraint if needed for reproducibility.

Validate both archives' metadata and included package resources. Install the wheel and sdist separately into clean environments, forcing the source path for the latter. Rebuild from the unpacked sdist outside git to prove it contains what its backend needs. Verify the package origin and installed source files, not only the reported version. Wheel/sdist compression need not be byte-identical to one another; their installed code and intended resources must agree.

Build the documentation source ZIP from R too. It is a third distribution route and must match the same package source/metadata, but its hash and archive layout are distinct. Preserve the deterministic ZIP test already owned by docs/hooks/entrance.py and test_lesson_downloads.py.

The checks page specifies fresh-install smoke cases, historical compatibility, supported profiles, and evidence fields. Run the maintained full runtime and Docs workflows on R; baseline passes on 1607afbb… cannot substitute. Reuse one successful result per exact revision and required environment rather than rerunning identical suites without cause.

docs.title: 4. Assemble the release handoff before publication
docs.text:
Produce one reviewable packet containing:

  • Commit R, version, proposed tag, final wheel/sdist/source-ZIP hashes, build-tool versions, source manifest, and exact installed-package receipts.
  • Hosted runtime, packaging-matrix, and Docs run links for R, with actual pass/fail/skip counts, reasons, supported environments, and residual limits.
  • Historical read/resume outcomes and explicit negative invocation/environment checks. Retain evidence that refusal performed no component work or new facts.
  • Release notes, rendered candidate docs, immutable documentation archive, public-index/project configuration, and the exact upload/deployment procedure.
  • The chosen narrow/full release scope and the existing owner's final claims and publication decision, plus the independent verification handoff.

Keep durable evidence beyond the existing 14-day Docs artifact retention. Attach receipts/checksums and necessary logs to the release or a maintained evidence record. Temporary /private/tmp paths alone are not release evidence that another contributor can retrieve.

The existing #276 explicitly says “Salah retains final acceptance and publication authority.” Prepare the complete packet first; request any still missing publication decision against these concrete artifacts. If Salah has already authorized the exact publication in the implementation session, retain that authorization rather than asking again. Planning #319 alone is not upload authorization.

docs.title: 5. Publish the exact artifacts and matching documentation
docs.text:
After the applicable acceptance and publication decision:

  1. Recheck tag/version/name availability and that R and artifact hashes match the approved packet. Create the version tag at R and prepare a GitHub release with the reviewed notes and assets using the selected procedure.
  2. Upload the verified wheel and sdist; record the actual index response and compare the index's file hashes. Do not rebuild between verification/upload.
  3. From a clean environment and outside the checkout, install the exact version from the public index, including a source-install check. Verify public asset hashes, metadata, imports, quickstart, CLI, saved history, and browser extra.
  4. Publish the reviewed GitHub release with its verified assets and notes. Keep staged release/docs material separate until the index check succeeds.
  5. Build/deploy docs from R, or use the verified R artifact. Update meta-evolve-docs/.source-commit to R; preserve the static repo's hosting files and README. Inspect its actual remote head first: the local sibling checkout observed during planning was stale.
  6. Verify the Pages build, public marker, migration/reference/install routes, and downloaded ZIP hash/metadata/source. Test real public responses, not just the deployment job or local files. Record source and docs commit IDs.

The current docs deployment is a separate static repository served from its main branch root through GitHub Pages. Reuse that arrangement; a new hosting service or cross-repository deployment framework is unnecessary. A moving homepage cannot retain all version-specific evidence, so keep the tagged source and reviewed docs archive available with the release.

docs.title: 6. Stop, recover, and close honestly
docs.text:
Failure point Required response Before upload: tests, metadata, permissions, or claims incomplete Keep artifacts staged. Fix the owning problem; create a new candidate if source changes. No tag or package claims imply a pass. Ambiguous/partial upload Inspect the public index before retrying. Account for each file/hash; do not blindly upload a rebuild or mark the release complete. Public install or asset mismatch Stop announcement/docs advancement, retain evidence, and use the approved correction/yank procedure if necessary. A fix requires a new published version; do not replace bytes behind an existing version/tag. Package works but docs deployment fails Keep #319 open, report the package/docs split, and redeploy the same reviewed documentation artifact. Do not conceal the successful package upload by calling the whole operation rolled back. A later defect affects saved runs Preserve old distributions and history. Reverting a package/docs pointer does not migrate stored facts or make an older runtime safe for newer stores.

Completion requires both public artifacts and matching docs, recorded fresh installation and compatibility evidence, and the independent verification required by the selected publication process. An automated smoke run cannot be reported as Bhasker's independent acceptance.

Update #319 and #313 with the evidence and reconcile their stale checklists. Close the API parent only after all selected children and publication gates are complete; leave broader #268/MVP issues open unless their own gates are met.

docs.title: Implementation slices
docs.text:
Slice Deliverable Exit A — Scope and packaging seam Record release cut/matrix/ownership; implement missing #272-compatible distribution checks and reviewed publication procedure. Wheel and sdist checks are reproducible and hosted; public-index configuration is known. B — Release preparation Version/lock/metadata, current install guidance, release notes, final candidate and staged assets. Exact R passes runtime, Docs, packaging, and historical checks; complete handoff ready. C — Authorized publication and verification Upload those assets, public-index installs, GitHub release, R docs deployment, independent handoff and closure record. All public artifact/revision/hash links and required acceptance evidence are retained.

These are review boundaries within #319, coordinated with #272/#276. They do not require a new family of speculative issues or additional runtime redesign.

docs.title: Fixed evaluation: plan for #352
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 21, 2026 for #352, D8 under #343. The dependency #351 is open. Its help-assistant lesson and verification record are present in the working tree; Salah's review and publication remain outstanding. Planning can overlap; acceptance follows the dependency order.

The implementation verification records the delivered lesson, installed Jupyter runs, and remaining review.

The programming model owns the API and refusal contract, the architecture owns authority, and the M8 acceptance record and implementation boundaries describe the existing harness mechanism. M11 remains the runtime build boundary. This work teaches shipped behavior.

docs.title: Reader outcome
docs.text:
Answer: “What stops a proposed change from changing the test instead of improving the answer?” Reuse D7's help assistant, password/invoice notes, and three fixed questions. Readers should point to the editable instruction, the protected checks, a permitted mistake, and a retained refusal before learning the broader ownership terminology.

Use one bounded run, one evaluator, and three proposed revisions. Keep the starting exact-match instruction and the same two supported worker behaviors. The second revision deliberately restores exact matching after the first revision broadens it; its missed polite question is an ordinary measured error.

Record Proposed change Expected measurement Evaluator called? Starting version Match exact questions. 2/3 checks Yes Allowed improvement Planner value becomes Match topic words. 3/3 checks Yes Allowed regression Planner value returns to Match exact questions. 2/3 checks Yes Forbidden declaration change Rename the planner surface to evaluation_checks, with a proposed always-pass rule PolicyViolation; no score or successor artifact No

The last proposal attempts to redefine what the editable field means. It does not obtain or modify the actual evaluator. Show the proposed renamed field beside the original declaration and the unchanged HELP_CASES; do not describe this as executing a replacement grader or protecting against arbitrary Python.

Expected work: three proposal attempts and three evaluations, including the starting version. The refused attempt adds one proposal and zero evaluations. Three questions within one evaluator call are three checks, not three accounted evaluations. The best measured instruction remains topic matching, even after the regression and refusal. Use no satisfaction threshold that would stop the demonstration after reaching 3/3.

docs.title: Enforce the actual boundary
docs.text:
Use the existing meta_evolve.harness.HarnessArtifact, with TextParam and PolicyParam. Schema v1 requires both planner and context-policy parameters; show both definitions. Explain that both values are declared mutable, although this example only exercises the planner value. Do not claim that this artifact declares a planner-only allowlist.

The permitted proposals can use HarnessMutation and HarnessArtifact.apply. For the forbidden proposal, deliberately bypass that convenience method and construct a successor with dataclasses.replace: change planner.name to evaluation_checks and its value to an always-pass instruction. The core's generic successor-validation hook calls HarnessArtifactCodec.validate_successor after encoding and before creating a successor artifact. It rejects the changed declaration with PolicyViolation and changed_declarations=("planner.name",) before evaluation.

This distinction matters: apply(HarnessMutation("evaluation_checks", ...)) instead returns InvalidOutput for an undeclared surface. That helper is convenience, not the authority boundary. Keep the main three-case demonstration on the core refusal; an existing helper test or a short explanation can cover the other failure kind without a fourth required case.

Use Task(artifact=harness.HarnessArtifact, ...), Experiment, and run(). improve() does not select this artifact codec. Declare a three-attempt allowance and up to four evaluations, permitting the seed and every proposal if all were admitted; the refusal leaves one evaluation unused. Use bounded Greedy search so the third attempt still has the successful instruction as its parent. Reset the authored proposal sequence when the run cell is rerun.

Keep notes, cases, evaluator callable, objective, and budget outside the candidate. The worker must interpret instruction text and return actual answers; the evaluator must retain question, expected answer, actual answer, and pass/fail evidence. Never assign quality from a revision label. Derive the displayed scores, failure reason, selected instruction, and counts from the returned run records. Display the failed record's lookup so readers can locate it again and inspect its .id, without treating a content duplicate as the same occurrence. This keeps the transcript readable without pinning an opaque identifier across package revisions.

State the limits beside the result:

  • This is a deterministic in-process simulation. Declaration validation supplies no process, filesystem, or Python security isolation.
  • The refusal protects immutable harness declarations on the normal proposal path. The actual checks remain experiment-owned; arbitrary malicious Python could access notebook globals and is outside this demonstration's protection.
  • Preventing this forbidden edit does not prevent all exploitation of an imperfect metric. Broader specification-gaming research stays in #216.
  • A path-valid SourceTree does not enforce a file allowlist. This notebook needs no source-tree variant, confinement setup, provider, or new framework.

docs.title: Notebook and page
docs.text:
Add one complete canonical source at examples/learn/harness_authority.py. Adapt D7's small worker and fixed cases directly, with no runtime sibling imports or hidden helper definitions. The page and downloads must use this source's snippet sections; avoid a second hand-maintained notebook program.

Target five required cells, including installation, each below 40 lines:

Cell Visible contents 1 Shared Python 3.12+ installation cell and fresh-kernel guidance 2 Imports, fixed notes/cases, and the complete two-instruction worker 3 Typed seed, both surface declarations, and evaluator with retained checks 4 The three explicit edits and proposer that returns the next successor 5 Reset sequence, declare/run experiment, inspect outcomes, protected checks, selection, and exact counts

Use readable definitions rather than compressed statements to fit the limit. Count output comments as cell lines too. If the full inspection is too large, keep the first measured result within five cells and make any additional required inspection cell explicit in the evidence; do not hide setup to meet the count. Prefer fitting all three outcomes within the five-cell target.

Put the example early in docs/concepts/authority.md, retaining its URL, keep-authority-where-it-belongs, ownership explanation, and promotion section. Preserve existing useful heading fragments. Add a D7 link next to its statement that the fixed checks stay outside the revised configuration; distinguish the plain mapping there from this typed declaration.

After the result, give one small “Change and predict” exercise: replace the forbidden edit with a permitted planner-value change and rerun. It should reach evaluation and use the fourth evaluation, even if its answers are wrong. Choose a non-no-op instruction relative to the current best parent. This makes the difference between admission and quality observable.

docs.title: Implementation slices
docs.text:
1. Prove the source and behavior. Implement the self-contained example, obtain the four retained outcomes above, and add focused regression checks before polishing the page. Keep src/ unchanged.
  2. Deliver the notebook. Include its source sections in the authority page; add the D7 link. Register authority-boundaries.ipynb and harness_authority.py with docs/hooks/entrance.py's existing generation paths. Use the existing concept navigation rather than a new guide hierarchy.
  3. Verify delivery. Add tests/test_authority_notebook.py and tests/test_authority_downloads.py, authority standalone coverage in tests/notebook_lesson_support.py, and their selections in the existing Docs workflow, including the isolated installed-package job.
  4. Rehearse and hand off. Execute the complete visible notebook, inspect the rendered page and executed output, and write docs/project/authority-lesson-verification.md from actual measurements. Record remaining dependency, audit, and publication gates explicitly.

No new artifact type, mutation framework, SDK adapter, coordinator branch, research study, automatic promotion, or public API change belongs to this work. Link canonical contracts rather than duplicating their signatures or changing their shipped status to describe a documentation delivery.

docs.title: Acceptance checks
docs.text:
• Execute the exact displayed cells: retained scores are 2/3, 1, 2/3, followed by policy_violation with empty metrics and no successor artifact/evaluation. The successful topic-matching version remains selected.
  • Instrument evaluator entry in a focused test: only the seed and two admitted revisions enter it. Prove the forbidden successor reaches the core check, rather than returning a manually constructed failure from the proposer.
  • Assert exact aggregate usage and per-attempt count changes. Confirm the second revision has its own artifact occurrence and parent link even though its content returns to the starting instruction.
  • Snapshot the fixed cases, notes, evaluator declaration, budget, and original harness declarations; verify they remain unchanged through every attempt. Every retained evaluation must use the same expected answers. Also cover direct component/interface declaration replacement with the existing harness regression suite.
  • Exercise the documented permitted replacement for the forbidden edit: evaluations rise from three to four; ordinary poor answers remain measured. Changing an expected answer as the experiment author changes the score in a separate control, proving the checks actually determine the measurement.
  • Whole-notebook and final-cell reruns reset the sequence and reproduce the outcomes without StopIteration or prior notebook state.
  • Check source, rendered Python cells, and generated notebook parity; visible definitions; cell lengths/counts; download links; and retained page anchors. The authority page contains a text diagram, so filter Python blocks rather than assuming every HTML pre is an executable cell.
  • Run downloaded Python, notebook cells, and rendered copied cells against a fresh noneditable install outside the checkout, with package-origin checks, no repository imports or provider keys, and no runtime network access.

Run those focused tests, existing harness artifact/notebook/download tests, standalone lesson checks, concept/navigation/route checks, and the strict MkDocs build. Use the existing META_EVOLVE_LESSON_PYTHON mechanism for tests against that build's downloads/meta-evolve.zip; ensure the workflow's -k selection actually includes the new installed-package tests.

docs.title: Evidence and closure
docs.text:
Retain the rendered page, executed notebook, clean copied-cell transcript, source revision and any dirty patch, archive hashes, installed package origin, installation command/receipt, Python and OS/kernel, required cell count, setup/run/total time, controls, and manual interventions. Exploratory notebooks and audit artifacts belong under gitignored notebooks/352-authority/. Keep the committed verification record concise and link its evidence.

Verify Jupyter and Colab independently before claiming support. D7's local Jupyter result is useful precedent, not evidence that D8 ran on either platform. Separate the exact-build install from a rehearsal of the public installation URL, whose package may lag. Do not borrow D7's timings, hashes, or test totals.

Salah's review is required before issue closure. Publication and the independent newcomer gate retain their existing owners under #343/#274. This plan does not close the dependency, publish documentation, or start participant outreach.

docs.title: Planning basis
docs.text: Inspected source: 9077011776a9b3cf6d2df57e798288e58a9c486c, with substantial existing documentation changes. Read #352, #351, and #343, the canonical contracts, D7's source and delivery evidence, the harness model/codec, and tests/test_harness_artifacts.py plus notebook/download coverage. A read-only Python feasibility run confirmed the 2/3, 1, 2/3 sequence, core PolicyViolation naming planner.name, three attempts/three evaluations, and the same result after resetting the sequence. These became the lesson's acceptance targets. The linked implementation verification now records the notebook, rendered, installed-package, and timing evidence and its limits.

docs.title: Harness lesson: plan for #351
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. This is the planning record; the live verification identifies the implemented lesson and its remaining capture gate.

docs.title: September 21 revision: a standalone live lesson
docs.text:
The user approved a seven-cell live adaptation, following Feedback Descent and EvoSkill, and required the notebook and copied documentation to be independently usable. This extends the earlier fixture-only lesson scope below. M11 remains the runtime boundary; the live example uses shipped callable and harness interfaces.

examples/research/meta_harness/main.py owns the visible declarations. Its SDK, grading, phase, and display modules remain example-local. A generated notebook and page share all seven cells; setup fetches a content-addressed, verified archive containing every support file. No checkout or companion upload is needed. The original study and its verification move together to the deterministic reference page and retain the harness-example.zip download.

Both proposer and worker use actual Claude SDK sessions. Mutations affect only planner text or whether the repository contract enters worker context. Generated repairs run in confined Python children; expected answers stay in the parent. All rankable development occurrences get private checks, selection freezes, and matched held-out runs determine export eligibility. Full receipts reconcile usage. The initial live path is explicitly Experimental/live-only, without claiming full paper reproduction, live resumability, or guaranteed improvement.

Acceptance covers deterministic SDK stubs over real execution, failure and authority boundaries, independently downloaded notebook and copied-page execution, strict rendering and visual inspection, then an authorized live capture. The notebook's first cell must supply all setup, and every code cell stays below 40 lines. The live lesson verification records the delivered reading paths and the remaining live capture.

docs.title: Earlier fixture lesson plan
docs.text:
Prepared September 20, 2026 for #351, D7 under #343. Its dependency #347 is closed. This plan changes the teaching path using shipped behavior. The programming model, architecture, milestones, and implementation plan retain their ownership. M11 remains the runtime build boundary; no runtime, SDK, or research expansion is needed for this issue.

The implementation verification records the delivered notebooks, executed results, and remaining review.

docs.title: Reader outcome and decisions
docs.text:
Readers should be able to identify the editable instructions, the worker's separate answer or repair, the fixed evaluator, and the stopping limit. Use D1's sequence and captions from docs/_includes/evolution-levels.md: change instructions/settings → run the same worker → independently test its output → retain the best measured settings. The starting settings can win.

Keep two explicitly connected examples:

Route Editable value Work being judged What it demonstrates Introductory help assistant One instruction in a plain mapping Returned help answers Instructions are measured through behavior; five required cells, no credentials or supporting imports Existing Meta-Harness study Typed planner text and context configuration Repository repairs executed against independent tests Governed edits, confinement, separate selection/final phases, accounting, and eligible export

Both workers and proposers are deterministic fixtures. The help assistant is a simulation, not a repository-repair agent or the research fixture. The advanced study executes real bounded repair/test processes, but does not reproduce the paper or establish general model improvement. State those limits beside results. Use only Shipped, Experimental/live-only, and Design—not shipped for status, following the existing convention for shipped lesson openings.

docs.title: 1. Shorten the introductory notebook
docs.text:
Maintain one complete source at examples/learn/harness_help.py, with snippet sections included by docs/guides/harness-evolution.md. Generate its notebook and Python download through the existing entrance hook. Keep every code cell below 40 lines; aim for fewer than 80 readable Python lines before the result.

Use {"planner": "Match exact questions."} as the seed. Keep both password and billing notes fixed outside the candidate. Preserve the existing three questions: reset password, please reset password, and download invoice. The single proposed instruction, Match topic words., changes the polite password answer from a missing-note response to Open Settings > Password. The expected measured result becomes 2/3 → 3/3, derived from actual answers. This replaces the old two-change 1/3 → 2/3 → 3/3 fixture; do not reuse its transcript or claim that the new score measures the same starting configuration.

Required cell Visible contents 1 Shared direct-install block, Python 3.12+, fresh-kernel instructions 2 Import, plain seed, fixed notes, complete assistant, and three fixed cases 3 Evaluator calling the assistant and retaining each question, actual answer, expected answer, and pass/fail 4 Handwritten proposer returning a new mapping with the changed instruction 5 improve(..., trials=1), measured starting/selected checks, changed answer, selected configuration, counts, and direct reuse

Show one proposal attempt and two evaluations, including the seed; explain that the declared attempt limit stops this run. Print observations from retained evaluation evidence instead of assigning scores to instruction names. Preview or reuse calls outside the run are not additional accounted evaluations. Reusing the selection on please download my invoice demonstrates adoption by the caller, not a held-out quality claim or deployment.

The main exercise sets trials=0: the starting configuration remains selected, the polite password request remains unanswered, and there is one evaluation. Also explain that changing an expected answer or adding an unseen phrasing can expose the simulation's limits. The evaluator stays independent of proposed instructions; unsupported instructions produce an evaluation failure with no score, while a completed wrong answer is an ordinary measured mistake.

Remove the initial HarnessArtifact, component fingerprints, expanded Experiment, held-out comparison, and export setup from the short notebook. Link to their concrete use in the advanced study after the first result. Ordinary mappings do not inherit typed harness mutation validation, resumability, or compare_harnesses/export_harness support. In particular, do not preserve the old typed no-op rejection test as a claimed mapping guarantee.

Preserve the guide URL and published fragment IDs. Old fresh-check/export anchors should lead to short, meaningful explanations and links to the matching advanced sections, rather than an unrelated next-step list.

docs.title: 2. Lead the research page with the actual repair
docs.text:
Open docs/research/meta-harness.md with the existing arithmetic example:

Observation Starting harness First revised harness Planner instruction Make a conservative change while preserving the interface. Diagnose requested behavior and repair arithmetic operations. Worker output in math_ops.py return value - 1 return value + 1 Independent check increment(3) == 4 fails The same check passes

Explain that the fixed worker interprets these instructions through authored Python branches. The instruction does not receive a score by itself: the worker produces source, and a fresh independent workspace executes the check. This first edit changes aggregate development quality from 0.0 to 0.5 across two repair tasks. A later context-setting edit reaches 1.0; keep it as a short continuation of the full study rather than a second prerequisite explanation.

Sources of truth for this example are flagship_declarations.py, fixture_responder.py, evaluation_core.py, and development_evaluation.py under examples/research/harness_evolution/. Derive/check the displayed instruction, repair, and measurement against their executed evidence.

Order the page as: concrete repair and two-level explanation; supported-runtime setup and result; mechanism worksheet and explicit typed declaration; diagnosis and citations; private selection, held-out comparison, accounting and export; paper comparison and evidence. Preserve the paper citation and the existing distinction between this bounded typed-surface study and Algorithm 1.

Keep short source excerpts where they explain a guarantee. Replace the supporting-source: harness directive and the full development-function dump with links to the complete source directory and existing harness-example.zip. Preserve the complete-supporting-source anchor as a useful source/download section. Essential expanded declarations remain visible, not hidden behind a new notebook helper.

Retain the existing study unchanged wherever possible: development diagnosis and authorized source reads; citation validation; private checks of all rankable occurrences; a frozen selection; matched seed-only held-out baseline/candidate runs; typed failures; separate inner/outer counts and resource roll-up; decision retention/replay; and export eligibility. Private selection may differ from the development winner. Exported settings are available for the user to adopt; neither selection nor export grants deployment authority.

Keep stopping conditions concrete: development allows two revisions, three evaluations, 100 fixture tokens, and 30 seconds, and may stop on satisfaction. Each private or held-out candidate has a seed-only evaluation with 40 fixture tokens and ten seconds. Print the phase report's actual usage and ceilings; inner proposal/evaluation counts remain separate from outer counts.

docs.title: 3. Supply an honest advanced notebook route
docs.text:
Generate downloads/meta-harness-repair.ipynb from the research page using the existing notebook exporter. Use visible Python setup/download/run cells and the existing complete archive; keep run_flagship as the execution owner and the existing CLI as the alternative terminal route. The introductory download is downloads/harness-improvement.ipynb, with downloads/harness_help.py as its canonical source download.

The advanced sequence is:

  1. Explain Python/OS requirements before setup. A small stdlib check rejects unsupported Python or platforms; a supported OS alone is not sufficient.
  2. Install the matching package directly and visibly download/extract the complete example into a fresh directory. No manual ZIP upload or checkout is required. Record matching archive hashes/revision for the audit.
  3. Before any study work, run a real confinement canary with the example's existing confinement_policy.launcher. Create a decoy in a protected output_root, pass that root to the launcher, and keep the allowed workspace separate. Confirm the parent can access the decoy, the child can read/write its own workspace, and the child cannot read/write the decoy. Show all definitions. Launcher failure must fail the check, not count as denial.
  4. Visibly import and call the downloaded study's existing run_flagship, which owns registration and all three phases. Print its report and inspect the retained first planner revision and episode-capture repair/check pair; do not rerun episodes to manufacture a separate demonstration. Locate the selected export. Explain fresh output directories versus compatible resume.

Use macOS with working sandbox-exec, or Linux with the example's required Landlock ABI 3 or newer. A failed canary stops before repair/proposal work with an actionable diagnostic. Do not disable protection or add a fallback runtime. No advanced Colab badge/support claim without an actual successful hosted run; a verified supported local Jupyter route satisfies the advanced requirement. The introductory notebook still requires fresh Colab and Jupyter verification.

The notebook exporter does not expand catalog source-function comments. Keep web-only explanatory excerpts within its existing web-only markers, with source links retained in notebook prose; executable notebook cells must be complete. Do not introduce another source renderer or duplicate the study.

docs.title: M11 trusted-concurrency design
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This page is the subordinate design record for #10. The milestone roadmap owns status, order, gates, and exclusions. The implementation plan owns technical staging and package boundaries. The distributed direction owns the longer arc through M12. This record owns vocabulary, the consistency model, the durable rules concurrency changes, and the compatibility promises.

Nothing here makes a name importable or an invariant implemented.

Longer than the other design records, deliberately: the rules below are one interlocking set — the outstanding-work definition, the decision barrier, the evaluation disposition and the reservation fold are four readings of the same predicate, and splitting them across pages would hide that they must agree.

docs.title: What distributed start refuses
docs.text:
The milestone roadmap owns the scope statement. This record owns the refusals that enforce it: seven configurations, each a CapabilityError naming its reason: six checked at start before any claim or lease, and the environment fingerprint, which is checked when a worker is admitted, before it can claim. Single-process resume ships in M11.2: prepare_resume admits a distributed run (session_preparation.py, mode not in ("durable-local", "distributed")) and re-runs admission against the recorded values, with Session.drive() rolling the epoch over as the explicit recovery step. There is no Dispatcher.resume. What stays M11.3's is the CROSS-PROCESS re-read: the "Re-read on resume from" column below describes a worker rejoining a run another process is driving. Admission turns on a declared capability, never a named preset — checking for a specific policy by type would be the policy-specific coordinator branch the constitution forbids.

Refused Reason A declared context policy Pushed context binds a fact to an exact stream position, and its cutoff is strict where pull's is inclusive. A declared experience access Pull experience appends audit facts synchronously from inside the proposer, behind stream-global guards. A policy without the cohort capability The capability is a declared width and a producer, and only BestOfN declares the width. Greedy chains strictly, so each parent is the previous result and a generation has nothing to draw from. BestOfK is the natural second — _cohort_parent already freezes an incumbent for a whole cohort of k — but it neither declares a width nor produces a generation, which is #201. A finite token, wall-time or spend ceiling The shipped presets hand each trial the run's whole measured allowance — bind copies the declared token and wall-time ceilings, and narrow adds the remaining spend at decision time — so a second cohort member, computed from the same base where nothing is yet settled, has nothing left to allocate. Zero is refused with the rest; the budget section owns why. A custom codec Codecs carry no manifest; durable-local already refuses them. A worker with the wrong codec is worse than one with none. A component not declaring retry_safe Automatic retry of unsafe work is dishonest. Determinism is not required: that is durable-local's rule, for M4's interrupted-equals-uninterrupted guarantee, which a distributed run does not claim. An environment fingerprint mismatch See environment fingerprint. Compared when a worker process is ADMITTED, against the dispatcher's current build; on resume a run's recorded fingerprint is compared with the current one and a difference is reported, never refused (AD6).

Every restriction is a refusal, never a silent degradation. Paid concurrency needs conservative per-trial allocation of measured dimensions, which M11.0 opened as #206 and which the measured-ceiling refusal above stands in for until it lands.

docs.title: Vocabulary
docs.text:
Four identities, none collapsed. The identity concept already establishes that equal bytes in different causal positions stay different occurrences; a work attempt is a third axis and folds into neither.

Term Meaning Identity Trial The logical experiment. Unchanged. Derived from its decision. WorkItem One deliverable unit. At most two per trial: proposal and evaluation. Stable from the trial and the kind. WorkAttempt One worker's bounded attempt at a work item. The work item and an ordinal, unique in the work table. Worker A trusted execution identity with declared capabilities and capacity. An operator-supplied id plus a monotonic generation.

docs.title: Execution terms
docs.text:
What runs work, and how its failures divide. None of these is an identity.

Term Meaning Worker process The operating-system process that hosts one Worker and connects to the dispatcher. It runs one call at a time: capacity is one, fixed by the worker protocol. Admission The handshake that authenticates a worker process against the run's shared key, checks that an operator-named worker is enrolled and trusted and that its declared capabilities meet the run's requirements, and then checks that it runs the same build and resolves the same components. It happens before that worker can claim anything. Reattachment A worker reconnecting under its own identity and resending the result nobody acknowledged. It preserves ACCEPTANCES, not work: a lease is rebound only inside the epoch that issued it and only while its old connection is still registered, and any other resend is answered Duplicate or Stale from the store. Enrolment An operator's entry for a worker id in the store's allow-list, made with workers add and holding the capabilities that worker declares. A dispatcher's own minted ids need none. Revocation An operator's withdrawal of a worker's trust: its generation moves on by one and its row is marked revoked. It is installation-wide, reaching every run in the store, and a lease issued at the old generation is stale at the next transactional check. Capability match At admission, every key in the union of the run's component work_requirements must be declared by the worker at a value with the same canonical bytes. Extra keys are allowed. Executor What runs a component on a work item's resolved inputs and returns its result, holding no coordinator, storage, clock or broker. Attempt failure Input resolution or the executor raised, outside the escaping set. The attempt is released and the retry bound decides. Completion failure A fault after the component returned: building its facts, validating them, or committing them. Its cause is recorded and it propagates; the dispatcher does not run the component again, and once the lease ends the recorded cause decides whether a later drain may. Input resolution The store reads that resolve a work item's inputs before its component is called. Submission A worker presenting a work attempt's result under the lease that attempt was issued. Never an enqueue. Duplicate submission A submission at a completed work item by its accepted attempt, with a token that proves. Answered with the stored acknowledgment. Stale submission A submission at a work item this run holds, whose lease no longer authorises it: the item was never leased to it, has ended, was completed by another attempt, or its lease is superseded, fenced or expired. Refused, never a contract violation. Stale reason The one precondition a stale submission failed, from a closed set: not leased, ended, superseded attempt, other worker, stale generation, unproven token, prior epoch, expired. Expiry is recognised even after it has been swept, from the token verifier the row keeps, so a lease that ran past its deadline reads expired either way. When several hold, terminal rows are checked first, then the epoch, then the worker's current generation, then the row's lease. Submission status What a submission would be answered, read without acting on it: live, duplicate with the stored acknowledgment, or stale with its reason. Advisory; the acceptance inside the committing transaction decides. Endpoint One backend as the dispatch loop sees it: the inline helper thread, or one worker connection. Every endpoint speaks the same dispatch messages. Transport failure A connection that breaks the protocol, or breaks. Its leases are released with cause WorkerDisconnected, the connection is closed, and the others continue. Dispatcher supersession A second dispatcher's rollover of the run's epoch, after which every commit and broker write the first one attempts is refused with DispatcherSuperseded. Exclusion, not failover: nothing decides which dispatcher should win.

docs.title: Semantics settled in M11.2
docs.text:
Four questions the vocabulary above left open. Each was answered because two adapters had answered it differently, and the shared contract suite could not see the disagreement.
