Aim for four required cells to the first measured table, each below 40 lines:

  1. Install the package from the documentation build's source ZIP.
  2. Download and extract that build's complete systems example automatically.
  3. Import the downloaded example and verify real confinement, with an actionable explanation if the runtime or extraction location is unsuitable.
  4. Run the maintained study and display the compact measured comparison.

Keep code inspection, detailed phase results, failure controls, accounting, and replay after that result. Publish the actual required cell count and elapsed setup/run time. This optional study has its own runtime requirements; the introductory five-minute result remains separate.

Confinement discovery alone is insufficient. Use the existing launcher for a small standard-library probe in a temporary workspace: verify that Python starts and that reading the downloaded protected workload file is denied. Confirm that file exists and is readable by the trusted notebook first, so a missing file cannot masquerade as successful protection. Handle launch denial, timeout, an unsafe path, and unavailable facilities before calling the study. This diagnostic is setup work, outside study evaluations and scenario counts. Prefer a visible cell over a new runtime abstraction.

The extraction layout matters: confinement.REPOSITORY is derived from the example's ancestors. Extract into a dedicated notebook working-directory child outside the interpreter installation and Linux readable exemptions such as /tmp and /usr. Keep child workspaces outside the protected download root. Validate canonical paths through the existing confinement checks. Choose a compatible rehearsal directory; retain the current allow-list.

Use lesson_notebook() to export the page's visible cells as downloads/systems-optimization.ipynb. Regenerate and execute the existing docs/notebooks/systems_optimization/systems_optimization.ipynb from that export, preserving its established evidence URL. Check cell-source equality between page, download, and executed notebook. Mark illustrative candidate source as nonexecuted excerpts so it does not become extra setup cells. Keep table rendering in the shared visible cells, with no second study driver or notebook renderer. Keep downloads and installation from one documentation build; retain their hashes and source revision for audit.

docs.title: Data and behavior to preserve
docs.text:
• run_example() retains development search, post-search selection, final comparison, decision persistence, and replay in their existing order.
  • Read tables from decision.development, decision.selection, and decision.comparison. Resolve the final selected source through its recorded identity and the run's artifacts. search.best() is not necessarily the post-search winner.
  • Display typed failures and absent comparisons explicitly. A failed attempt has no invented metric. Preserve cleanup even if a run or notebook cell fails.
  • Keep simulator execution, candidate surfaces, workload separation, policy identities, accounting, and evaluator independence intact. Presentation changes need no coordinator branch, new public API, or new artifact domain.
  • Preserve source-manifest verification. Editing an identity-bearing example module, even its comments, requires regenerating affected captured digests.

docs.title: Acceptance checks and evidence
docs.text:
Extend test_systems_optimization_notebook.py, test_catalog_examples.py, test_lesson_downloads.py, and the existing research/navigation checks. Replace assumptions that setup is the first run cell or that every saved output is byte-identical when installation logs/timings are variable; keep exact checks for deterministic study results. Test visible behavior rather than specific explanatory sentences.

The focused checks must prove:

  • The archive is complete, preserves relative paths, and matches maintained files. A fresh noneditable installation runs the downloaded notebook outside the checkout without PYTHONPATH or earlier notebook state. Assert package and example import origins. On Linux, ordinary pytest /tmp extraction is unsuitable for this example; provision a compatible isolated location.
  • Notebook cells and the displayed measurements agree with a fresh governed run. Table rows cannot mix workload phases. All replay checks still pass.
  • Changing the two-worker comparison from <= to >= changes observed measurements. Reuse the existing wrong-comparator candidate as the control, and retain invalid-schedule/off-surface typed refusals as failure evidence.
  • Unsupported enforcement stops before study execution with a useful remedy; successful capability detection followed by failed launch is covered too.
  • A missing or unrankable final comparison renders without a score or crash; output-directory cleanup still runs on exceptions.
  • A strict documentation build and rendered-link checks cover the notebook, source archive, source links, optional program navigation, and advanced study.

Run the affected notebook/download tests and existing systems-optimization measurement, failure, confinement, accounting, decision, and replay tests. Retain a rendered page, executed notebook, copied-cell transcript, source revision and dirty-state qualification, archive hashes, installation origin, OS/kernel/Python details, setup/run times, cell count, and manual interventions. Record Jupyter and Colab outcomes separately. Agent rehearsal supplies execution evidence; Salah's audit and the separate newcomer-review gate retain their owners.

docs.title: Planning evidence
docs.text:
Inspected working tree: 9077011776a9b3cf6d2df57e798288e58a9c486c, with existing documentation edits. A fresh fixture run on Python 3.12.13/macOS 26.6.2 reproduced the numbers above, development/selection/final evaluation counts of 9/5/2, scenario counts of 13/15/4, and all eleven replay checks.

The outer tool sandbox refused nested sandbox-exec with “Operation not permitted”; running with approved local process permissions succeeded. This supports testing actual launch in preflight. It does not establish hosted notebook compatibility. A fresh installed-download notebook rehearsal and actual Colab check remain implementation acceptance work.

docs.title: Scientific direction
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This is a retained design record. The programming model and project status identify shipped behavior; proposals below do not extend those contracts.

Meta-Evolve may eventually represent hypotheses, protocols, datasets, simulations, analyses, claims, replications, and retractions as typed artifacts. That direction does not make software evaluation equivalent to validated science.

Scientific use requires explicit provenance, preregistered or otherwise governed evaluation, uncertainty, leakage controls, independent replication, negative results, and human/institutional authority. Model-generated novelty or an improved benchmark score is evidence only within the declared experiment.

Training views, semantic retrieval, learned search, and model-weight updates must be derived from immutable authorized records. They cannot become an unrecorded source of experience or retroactively alter a historical decision.

Current shipped semantics provide useful ingredients—immutable artifacts, typed failures, evidence, budgets, causal lineage, and replay—but do not ship a scientific artifact domain or make generalization claims.

docs.title: Future search policies
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This is a retained design record. The programming model and project status identify shipped behavior; proposals below do not extend those contracts.

Meta-Evolve currently ships deterministic Greedy, BestOfN, BestOfK, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch presets. The ideas below are roadmap direction, not importable names or accepted semantics.

docs.title: Pareto and quality-diversity archives
docs.text: Multi-objective archives would need explicit dominance, constraint, tie, capacity, and admission decisions. Quality-diversity additionally needs a versioned behavior descriptor and deterministic binning. Archive membership must be replayable from recorded evaluations rather than recomputed under a new definition.

docs.title: Islands and migration
docs.text: An island design must distinguish artifact identity from island membership. Migration is a recorded search decision, not artifact copying or Git history. Timing, topology, migrant selection, admission, and random streams must remain deterministic at the logical level.

docs.title: Other bandits and tree allocation
docs.text:
TreeSearch ships fixed progressive widening, best-descendant backup, and deterministic UCT descent; it does not imply the broader allocation ideas below are importable names or accepted semantics. Any other allocation policy may use uncertainty, cost, or upper-confidence estimates only when their observations, update rule, and random choices are explicit. Retry delivery must never become an extra logical trial.

No future policy may erase failed outcomes, widen budgets, inspect hidden evaluation, or require a coordinator special case.

docs.title: Trusted-worker administration: plan for #203
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. This page preserves the September 21, 2026 planning snapshot for the implemented M11.4 trusted-worker administration slice, and states below what was built where that differs from the plan. The broader M11 milestone remains Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 21, 2026 for #203, the fourth M11 slice, after M11.3 merged. This page is the record a reader resolves the decision labels AD1–AD7 and PD1–PD8 against: source docstrings across the slice cite them by name rather than restating the argument. PD6 and PD7 share their labels with M11.3's farewell and one-live-process-per-id rules, which host.py, admission.py and worker_identity.py cite too, so source names these as "the worker-administration plan's PD6".

The verification record identifies the commits, the checks run and the mutations that did not redden a law. The roadmap owns scope and acceptance; the programming model owns the public API; architecture owns invariants; and the implementation plan owns technical boundaries. The M11 design supplies the subordinate admission, lease and reattachment rules, and is the page a normative sentence belongs in. The command-line guide owns how an operator uses the result; storage and recovery owns the schema step.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: An operator decides which external workers a store trusts, what each declares it can do, and can withdraw that trust while a run is live — with every refusal landing before a lease, and a withdrawn worker's live lease dying at the broker's next transaction.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• The store: schema 5, one new validated table trusted_workers, the v4 → v5 rung, and read-only opening of schema-4 stores.
  • Domain, port, adapters: the trusted-worker record, the trusted-worker port with its SQLite and in-memory adapters, and the generation check plus the revocation sweep inside both work brokers.
  • Admission: the trust lookup and capability match in the host handshake, the registration's generation, and a per-connection guard on an unexpected raise over unauthenticated bytes.
  • Dispatch: what the dispatcher and the loop do when a worker turns out to be revoked — at a claim, and at a stale answer.
  • Operator surface: the meta-evolve workers verb, Storage.trusted_workers(), and the environment row on resume.
  • Record and docs: the design record's new section and fixes, the command-line and durability guides, status wording, this page, and a verification receipt.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Multi-host transport and TLS, autoscaling, priorities, preemption.
  • Per-kind routing — a worker serving only evaluations — and multi-call worker processes, meaning capacity above one. Both are recorded as deferred rather than built.
  • Worker respawn. "Replacing a dead worker is administration" stays true and stays unbuilt.
  • A structured, dimension-wise environment fingerprint.
  • The concurrent renewal-versus-expiry and over-capacity race tests, which belong to #204's harness.

docs.title: AD1 The registry is a validated table in the store; schema 5; v4 stays readable
docs.text:
The store schema version moves 4 → 5, with a rung that creates trusted_workers. A read-only open accepts a v4 store by validating it against the v4 shape, and its registry reads as empty. A validated table behind a version bump was chosen over schema_meta rows or an unvalidated side table so that an older binary REFUSES a v5 store rather than silently ignoring its revocations. Installation-level means per store: the table carries no run_id.

An already-open older process cannot keep writing. The version check runs only at open, so a dispatcher started before an in-place upgrade would hold the v4 store, with the old code in memory, while the new command line migrates it and revokes a worker. Schema 5 therefore carries a BEFORE UPDATE and a BEFORE INSERT trigger on work_items whose body calls a no-op SQL function registered on every writable connection before any schema work. SQLite resolves a trigger body when a statement is prepared, so a connection that never registered the function cannot write that table once the migration commits; its reads still answer. Every lease-bearing write touches work_items, so the old dispatcher's next broker transaction fails whole as a typed durable-store error and the run resumes on the new build. An exclusive-access migration was rejected: leaving WAL fails while any other connection is open, it leaves a check-then-migrate window, and it would refuse the upgrade for a harmless read-only browser.

One creator, two callers. A fresh store runs no rung — it is built from the current definitions and stamped — so the trigger DDL is defined once and executed both from the rung and from the current-definitions pass that every writable open runs. Both triggers are validated by the exact definition text SQLite's catalog records for them. For a stamped store that validation runs before the definitions pass, so a stamped v5 store missing a trigger is corruption rather than something an open quietly repairs.

The read side is its own port. A reader offers get and all; the authority adds trust and revoke. Every store hands out the reader, and only the writable one also answers for the authority, so mutation is structurally absent from what anything that merely reads the allow-list holds — including a dispatcher's, where the connection underneath could write — rather than refused at call time. Listing opens a store read-only, so it never migrates one and works while a dispatcher holds it.

docs.title: AD2 Operator allow-list; revoke bumps the generation and marks the row
docs.text: An operator-supplied id needs a TRUSTED row to be admitted or to hold a lease. A revoke is generation + 1 together with status revoked, so a revoked worker's reconnect loop meets an authenticated terminal refusal instead of being re-issued the new generation. Re-trusting keeps the bumped generation. Rows are never deleted: the generation is monotonic for the life of the store.

docs.title: AD3 Dispatcher-minted ids need no row
docs.text: Ids in the reserved worker- namespace are the dispatcher's own: generation 1, and not revocable — to stop them, stop the dispatcher. The dispatcher therefore never writes the registry, the record's "operator authority only" stays literally true, and ordinary runs add no rows. An operator row under the reserved prefix is refused.

docs.title: AD4 Capabilities match at admission, against the run as a whole
docs.text: The row carries the worker's operator-declared capabilities: an opaque string-keyed mapping, shaped like a component's work requirements. At admission the host refuses — authenticated, terminal, before any lease — a worker whose capabilities do not satisfy the union of the run's component requirements, key by key. Every admitted worker can then run every item, which is already the invariant M11.3 relies on. There is no capacity column: the record rejects a worker capacity field whose only legal value is one.

docs.title: AD5 No new stale reason
docs.text: A lease whose generation is not its worker's current one — or whose worker's row is revoked or absent — is STALE_GENERATION, already in the closed set and already crossing the wire.

docs.title: AD6 Resume never refuses for environment drift; it reports it
docs.text: The recorded fingerprint is one digest over five inputs, so no dimension-wise policy is expressible, and strict equality would refuse every resume after a dependency sync. The property that matters — every worker in one drive runs the dispatcher's build — is enforced at each admission instead. Resume computes recorded against current and says the environment changed since start.

docs.title: AD7 An unexpected raise refuses the connection, not the run
docs.text:
The host handshake refuses the connection, not the run, for any non-escaping exception raised on unauthenticated bytes.

Added 2026-09-25, after review: the host keeps the exception on the Refused it returns, and a spawned run chains it, since the wire names only the type. The trust read types every sqlite3 failure, so a damaged store escapes this guard and stops the run. A worker_nonce must match the workers' 64-character hexadecimal format, because Terms echoes it and is sized at that format. The listener keeps only its latest 16 refusals, bounding retained exceptions and the input buffers held by their tracebacks.

docs.title: Decisions on the shape of the work
PD1 acquire raises, never returns a second kind of None
docs.text: The dispatcher's claim step continues on None, so a None-style refusal would spin the drive. It raises a typed run error instead, which is not a root export and does not escape normalization. The epoch fence still refuses first.

docs.title: PD2 The generation check sits between the epoch and the row
docs.text: The staleness rule's order is: the terminal exemption, unchanged; the epoch; then the presented generation against the one the store honours; then the row, the credential and the deadline. Before the row, because a revoked lease loses its row and a row-first order would report "not leased" or "expired" for a worker an operator had revoked. The honoured generation is keyword-only with no default: a default would be a silent "no authority" fallback. The comparison is written in the staleness module, and domain/work.py gains nothing.

docs.title: PD3 The sweep frees revoked leases and authors the cause
docs.text:
The expiry sweep in both adapters returns a LEASED row whose generation is no longer honoured to READY at the next broker write, clears the verifier as rollover does, and writes the revocation cause under the existing first-writer-per-attempt rule. A revoked credential then authorises nothing, and the cause survives a dead dispatcher: rollover, a restarted drive's first write, runs the same revocation arm before it frees the other prior-epoch leases (added 2026-09-25, after review found rollover freed such a row with no cause). The cause constant lives in the domain, because adapters cannot import application code.

A revoke is installation-wide. The registry has one row per worker for the whole store, so revoking a worker frees every live lease it holds in every run in that store, each with a spent attempt and the revocation cause.

docs.title: PD4 trust may widen a trusted worker's capabilities; narrowing or changing one is refused
docs.text: On an already-trusted id, trust with the same capabilities is a no-op, and with a superset — every existing key kept at a canonically equal value, new keys added — it updates the row at the same generation: a larger set cannot invalidate an admission that already matched, so declaring one more capability costs no lease. Dropping a key or changing a value is refused, because an admission that matched may depend on it. On a revoked row, trust sets it TRUSTED at the kept, bumped generation and replaces the capability map wholesale — that is the only path by which a map is narrowed, and it is what "revoke it first" means. The superset rule is keyed on the row's status, never on the row's presence: rows are never deleted, so a presence rule would make narrowing impossible. A second revoke does not bump twice, and revoking an id nobody enrolled is refused, because a typo must not report "revoked".

docs.title: PD5 The host gets a lookup, never the port
docs.text:
A host admission carries a lookup that reads through a reader's get and nothing else, in a field named lookup, never trust. The evidence:

  1. The store hands out a reader: test_the_allow_list_a_store_hands_out_is_a_reader_whatever_it_may_do, on durable and read-only stores.
  2. A drive supplies a reader factory. The listening host calls it when opening, before creating a key or listener; a spawned backend leaves it unused. It never asks for trusted_worker_authority (test_trust_lookup_handoff.py).
  3. mypy types trusted_workers() as TrustedWorkerReader, which has no trust or revoke. Types cannot tell a reader's get from a writer's, since TrustLookup is a bare Callable, so the handed lookup's provenance rests on (2).

2026-09-25: acceptance evidence reworded from a directory AST ban to the laws above; the rule is unchanged.

A host is spawn-policy or operator-policy by construction: the admission refuses minted ids together with a lookup, and refuses neither, so "no lookup, so everyone is admitted" cannot be built. A spawn-policy admission carries no lookup at all and answers generation 1 without consulting one.

docs.title: PD6 Conflicting requirements are not an eighth start refusal
docs.text: Two components declaring one key at different values is valid inline and with spawned workers: neither matches work requirements against a worker. That field's only reader compares it for equality — host against worker at a handshake, recorded against supplied on every resume — and both stay byte-identical. It is unsatisfiable only under every-worker-runs-everything, so the listening host refuses it when it opens, before the rollover. Both seven-row start-refusal tables stay untouched.

docs.title: PD7 Equality is type-strict
docs.text: Capability values are compared as canonical payload bytes. Python equality would let 1 satisfy True, and existing tests already declare boolean capabilities.

docs.title: PD8 Drift rides Run, not RunSummary
docs.text: A run summary promises capabilities without verifying compatibility to resume, and feeds the inspect, compare and browser goldens. Drift is therefore a method on Run, and the command line prints it as one extra row only when there is drift, so every existing resume output stays byte-identical.

docs.title: Two pull requests
docs.text: Both planning passes found the same thing: operator-named ids already take real leases, so broker enforcement without the door would abort a listening drive, and the door without broker enforcement would make revoke a lie. They land together.

docs.title: The first: registry and revocation
docs.text:
An operator can enrol and revoke, and it is enforced at the door, in every broker transaction, and in the dispatch loop. What it built, where that differs from the plan above:

  • The schema-5 DDL, the v4 → v5 rung and the write guard live in one new module, adapters/sqlite/schema_v5.py, rather than growing schema.py. The read-only shape map holds exactly the versions it has a shape for, 4 and 5.
  • The table's key is worker_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL: in SQLite a TEXT primary key does not imply NOT NULL.
  • A store answers through two capability Protocols, not one. Storage.trusted_workers() returns a reader — a distinct object with no trust and no revoke, on every kind of store, including a writable durable one — and Storage.trusted_worker_authority() returns the writable port and is declared by the durable strategy alone. One method name would have answered True for a read-only store under a structural check, so the writable half is a name a read-only store does not have; and the reader is a separate object rather than the port under a narrower type, because a host is handed one bound get (PD5) and a get bound to the port would carry revoke on its __self__. The writable store's reader reads the live table over the store's own connection, so a revoke made through the authority, or by an operator's command on another connection, is visible at its next get.
  • Placement. decide_trust and decide_revocation live in ports/worker_registry.py beside the Protocols, so the two adapters cannot drift on a rule. The store capabilities are Protocols of their own there, not a method on WorkTransactor, whose capability is its one method: a strategy with a broker and no registry would stop satisfying it. The workers verb is the top-level worker_administration.py, not part of cli.py (at its length ceiling) or of distributed/, since the operator writes the allow-list and the dispatcher and the transport only read it. The diagnosis rule moved into each adapter's work_diagnosis.py to keep the lease and ledger modules under the length guideline.
  • The door's generation read raises the handshake's own refusal rather than returning a sentinel, because there is no number that means "no". It is read at the Hello before the build comparison, and again just before the reservation.
  • The SQLite generation read lives once, in the submission classifier that renewal, status and acceptance already share, rather than being copied to three callers whose whole job is to agree. The in-memory ledger is handed the answer by the broker that holds the registry.
  • The diagnosis precondition split in two: whether the attempt is still undiagnosed, and whether the caller's credential authorises a diagnosis. The sweep asks only the first — a stored lease carries a digest, not the secret — and the in-memory ledger's held lease does carry the secret, so one shared rule would have passed there and refused in SQLite.
  • The sweep clearing the verifier has no law of its own. Planting "keep the verifier" leaves every law green, because the cause write already refuses a later diagnosis and every other path meets the generation check first. It is kept because the record requires it and because it is one statement shared with release and rollover.
  • Answering a revoked holder also RELEASES the item it was holding. Settler._answer sends the answer; then, when holds_a_revoked_credential says it names the connection's own credential, it calls fail_attempt (even when the send failed) and raises the TransportFailure that closes the connection. The answer is best effort: a close can drop what the socket had not taken, and the door's refusal tells the worker anyway. That broker write's opening sweep is what frees the row and records WorkerRevoked, so the cause fail_attempt passes goes unused. The answer is classified by a read, which by contract moves nothing, and the binding that would have carried the lease into the loop's own release is dropped before the outcome is settled — so without that release the row stays LEASED with nothing bound to it, which the dispatcher refuses by name rather than waiting out. PD3 is still where the freeing happens; the refusal is what makes a write happen at all on that path. A refusal from that release is not swallowed: DispatcherSuperseded and DurableStoreError are facts about the run, they outrank failing one connection, and they end the drive.
  • A workers list or workers revoke pointed at a path holding no store exits 1, the existing mapping for a refusal from the library, not 2. workers add CREATES the store and exits 0, because an operator enrols the workers a run will use before that run exists. Exit 2 is reserved for a malformed or reserved id, which a parser type refuses in the domain's own words before any store is opened.
  • An unreadable trust row stops every run its worker holds a lease in. A trusted_workers row the decode refuses is DurableCorruption — never skipped, because skipped as absent it would free a lease nobody revoked, and skipped as trusted it would honour an authority nothing can read. The revocation sweep that opens a run's broker writes reads the row of each worker holding one of that run's leases, so while the damaged worker holds a lease in a run, every write in that run stops until the row is repaired, whoever asks. So does anything that looks that worker up by name: its own claims, workers list, and the door, which stops any listening run the worker connects to. A run it neither holds a lease in nor connects to never reads the row and keeps writing, since the sweep is scoped to its run. Kept, lawed and documented rather than softened: a lease's authority is not something a store may read past.

docs.title: The second: capabilities and the record
docs.text:
An operator can declare what a worker can do and have it matched at admission; a resume in a changed environment is reported; and the design record carries its own worker-administration section. What it built, where that differs from the plan above:

  • The unexpected-raise guard is the last arm of the host handshake's advance: a raise the handshake did not expect on bytes a peer chose refuses that one connection, unauthenticated, naming the exception type and never its message, while anything a run must stop for still stops it.
  • The matcher is worker_capabilities.py, a top-level module (about 110 lines, not the estimated 75) beside the workers verb that writes declarations, not in manifests.py, which answers whether the code is the same and is at its length budget. It holds the union of a run's requirements, and the first key in sorted order a declaration misses or declares at a different value. Its admission and command-line laws live in tests/test_worker_capability_admission.py and tests/test_cli_worker_capabilities.py rather than in the matcher's own module, which holds the pure-function table.
  • The door matches capabilities inside the same call that answers the generation, so trust and capabilities always come from one registry read, at both reads. The listening host computes the run's requirements once when it opens, before the key file and the port, so a run with conflicting requirements writes neither.
  • Writing commands report their transaction's resulting row, including the generation and the full declaration for add. They do not infer whether the command changed anything from a separate read, which could race another operator. worker_administration.py passed 300 lines when --capability arrived; the review round's trim brought it back under.
  • The plan's "skip the shared freeze" mutation stays GREEN: a declared value is also frozen by the SQLite encoding and compared by canonical bytes, so any one of the three is masked by the other two. The command-line array law goes red instead under "the command line takes arrays and objects as literal text".
  • The drift row is printed after the drive, so a resume that raises shows only its error. Stale M11.2 text calling the fingerprint "recorded, never compared" was also rewritten in domain/components.py, beyond the two files the plan named.
  • The identity evidence is tests/test_workers_mint_no_identity.py. Three of its mutations go red through the replay fold's own refusal rather than the law's assertion — a second guard in the domain, recorded rather than hidden.

docs.title: Laws
docs.text:
Each law goes red under a named mutation, and where a law could pass for a weaker reason the neighbouring case that rules it out is named with it.

  • Registry, against both adapters with a completeness guard: insertion at generation 1; an identical trust is a no-op, a superset widens at the same generation, and a narrowed or changed value is refused — a triple, because an always-overwrite registry passes the first two alone. A read-only store's reader has no trust or revoke attribute, is empty below schema 5 and table-backed at 5. A revoke bumps by exactly one and marks the row, read back through get rather than from the return value; a second revoke does not bump; an unknown id is refused with no tombstone; re-trust keeps the bumped generation and the status is asserted; rows never vanish; the reserved prefix is refused using an id the grammar accepts, or the grammar would refuse it for the wrong reason. SQLite also: survives a reopen, sees a second connection's revoke, leaves the row unchanged when the commit tears, and reports a damaged row as corruption.
  • Broker, one contract tuple over both adapters: an absent, revoked or wrong-generation operator id is refused with rows equal before and after, and a reserved worker then claims that same row, so the queue was not merely empty; a reserved id needs no row and the registry is still empty afterwards; a superseded epoch is answered first; after a revoke through the authority, renewal, submission status, acceptance and release all refuse with the stale generation while the deadline is still ahead; the swept row is READY with the revocation cause and its attempt still spent; the terminal exemption still answers duplicate; revoking one worker leaves another's lease live; and one revoke frees that worker's lease in each run in a two-run store, at that run's own next write. Plus a differential sequence across both adapters, a torn sweep, and the precedence cases.
  • Wire: three enrolled ids revoked through the real port exhaust an item, which ends as an infrastructure failure naming the revocation at the last attempt; a re-enrolled worker resending a lease from before its revoke is answered and stays connected; an idle revoked worker is failed at its next claim with attempts unchanged.
  • Admission: unenrolled and revoked are refused authenticated and terminally, before the run's terms cross; a revoke landing between the Hello and the manifests is caught by the second read; a host with a minted policy and a lookup, or with neither, cannot be constructed; a spawn-policy handshake admits its minted id at generation 1 against an empty registry.
  • Real processes, because command-line code has escaped a green suite in this repository by never being launched: every exit code of the verb, through a real process as well as through main(argv). A worker nobody enrolled exits 2 saying it is not enrolled, while the run's rows stay NON-EMPTY, ready, unspent and on the same epoch and the port stays open — the emptiness matters, because an all(...) over an empty work table is true — and then, enrolled through the real verb, the same run finishes. A revoke delivered as a real command while a worker is inside its call sends that worker back to the door, where it exits 2 saying it was revoked, while the item it held completes on another worker under the same trial with two attempts and the revocation recorded against the first. Each worker waits on a release marker of its own: one shared marker lets the run reach its stop and close the port before the revoked worker is back at the door, after which it would back off forever. A worker declaring the wrong capability exits 2 naming the key and both values, at no cost to the run.
  • Schema: each frozen capture opens writable and lands at 5 with an empty table and unchanged events; a read-only open of a v4 store leaves it untouched; a v5 store without the table is corruption. A raw connection opened on a v4 copy before the migration — standing in for the older process — is refused on update and on insert into work_items once another connection has migrated the store, and can still read. The trigger lifecycle has one law per caller: a freshly created store holds both exact definitions, a migrated one holds both, and a stamped store with a trigger dropped by hand is corruption.
  • Capability matching: declared equal to required is admitted; a superset is admitted; a missing key is refused naming the key; a differing value is refused naming both values; 1 does not satisfy a required True; nested maps, arrays and nulls compare; empty requirements admit anything, which is the control; and two components requiring one key at different values is refused when the listening host opens, with rows ready, attempts unspent and the epoch unchanged.

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
• Every runtime refusal the record's admission table names has a law asserting the refusal leaves rows ready, attempts unchanged and the epoch unchanged. Unenrolled, revoked and capability mismatch are also shown with real processes. The two structural rows cite the laws that already close them: the codec by the start and resume refusals, capacity by the handshake pin and the broker's capacity inequality.
  • After a revoke through the registry — never by editing a lease — renewal, submission status, release and acceptance all refuse with the stale generation in both adapters, and the process law shows the item completing on another worker under the same trial with two attempts.
  • An item exhausted by revocations ends as an infrastructure failure whose exception type is the revocation cause, and nothing new enters the closed wire error map.
  • An older process that held the store open across the migration cannot write work_items afterwards, and a read-only store exposes no trust or revoke.
  • The frozen schema-4 captures stay byte-identical and open read-only; inline and spawned-worker runs stay byte-identical in events and work rows, with the registry empty; and a host is handed a lookup that reads only through a reader, by PD5's three pieces of evidence.
  • Existing listening-mode tests pass after enrolling their ids, with no assertion weakened.

docs.title: Worker processes: stabilization plan for #353
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. This page preserves the September 21, 2026 planning snapshot for the implemented M11.3 worker-process slice. The broader M11 milestone remains Design—not shipped.

Prepared September 21, 2026 for #353, the third M11.3 slice. At preparation, the scope was to finish the existing implementation and prepare it for another review. The issue states and branch heads below describe that dated baseline, not the current GitHub state.

The verification record identifies the implemented revision, regression evidence, and completed checks. It also tracks the subsequently authorized push/merge integration separately, including the new #341 settling-lease regression; the baseline checks do not validate a later base revision automatically.

The roadmap owns scope and acceptance; the programming model owns the public API; architecture owns invariants; and the implementation plan owns technical boundaries. The M11 design supplies the subordinate admission, lease, and reattachment rules.

docs.title: Inspected baseline — September 21, 2026
docs.text:
Item Observation and consequence PR #353 Draft; changes requested on 170e4a26b8401b6d6560d9b18b459cac60595791. Three inline findings remain the initial repair scope. Base PR #341 Open draft targeting main, head f48e04f6ffd231f9d9b6db9ce2f77cf7a68de7b1; changes requested and merge conflicts reported. Settle its review and integration before landing #353. Stack ancestry The inspected #353 head includes that #341 head and current main 9077011776a9b3cf6d2df57e798288e58a9c486c. Its description's promise to inherit the base fixes is older than the source. Verify the fixes instead of implementing them twice. Parent #202 Closed, while its body still leaves #341/#353 unfinished. Reconcile tracking with integrated acceptance; issue state alone is not proof of completion. Evidence The review reports three isolated reproductions on this exact head. The PR's earlier full-suite claim is historical; this planning pass ran no runtime tests. Hosted checks were still in progress when inspected.

The local main working tree contains unrelated in-progress documentation and example changes. Implementation should use an isolated checkout of the PR, preserving that work. Recheck branch heads and reviews when execution starts.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Preserve the existing spawned-worker and listening-host entry points, one lease per worker process, shared settlement path, and explicit reconnect behavior. The required change is three bounded fixes with regression coverage, followed by integration and documentation verification.

Keep admission before spawned-run epoch rollover; authenticate before sending run details or lease secrets; build executors from the recorded start; retain at-most-once acceptance and store-authoritative Duplicate/Stale answers. Reconnect must preserve acknowledgment recovery without promising recovery of an old live call across epochs. Failures retain their existing domain meaning.

Worker respawning, capacity above one, durable worker administration, a general load-testing framework, paid-budget admission, distributed experience, TLS implementation, and the full M11.6 example remain outside this repair.

docs.title: 1. Refuse malformed authentication envelopes locally
docs.text:
Finding: malformed MAC aborts the dispatcher.

In distributed/handshake_envelope.py, validate the MAC's type, ASCII encoding, and SHA-256 hexadecimal format before comparison. Translate malformed peer input into the existing handshake refusal, without quoting supplied payloads. Keep MAC verification before body decoding. Do not broadly catch application exceptions and relabel them as authentication failures.

Acceptance:

  • Drive the real host handshake with the reported non-ASCII MAC, plus wrong type, wrong length, and non-hex variants; each returns Refused.
  • A pending-admission/dispatcher regression proves another valid worker can still join and perform work after a malformed peer is refused.
  • Existing wrong-key, nonce, frame-bound, and verify-before-parse tests pass.

docs.title: 2. Preserve results through write-side connection loss
docs.text:
Finding: worker exits before retaining its result.

In distributed/worker.py, retain Completed and its lease before attempting transmission. If encoding or frame validation converts it to CompletionFailed, clear the pending result before transmitting that replacement. Only completed results participate in the existing acknowledgment/reconnect path.

Route socket OSErrors through Lost(holding, run_id) for reads, initial pulls, initial resends, outcome writes, and subsequent pulls. Keep this boundary specific to transport operations: protocol violations, encoding failures, and component interrupts must retain their existing classifications. In distributed/worker_process.py, ensure the connected socket closes when serve() returns or raises. Reuse the existing reconnect loop; retain its backoff on connect/admission failures without adding a new retry policy.

Acceptance:

  • With a socketpair and explicit synchronization, close the host while the evaluator is running, then release the evaluator. The worker returns Lost carrying the exact result and lease; the evaluator was called once.
  • Fail the first pull, a resend repeatedly, and a pull after acknowledgment. Pending state is preserved only while a completed result remains unanswered.
  • A failed fallback write after an unsendable result retains no completed result. Attempt failures, completion failures, and interrupts remain distinct.
  • Exercise the real external-worker reconnect path: preserve incarnation, advertise the held lease, resend before pulling, recover the answer, and exit on Goodbye. A spawned worker still exits when its dispatcher is lost.

The adjacent cross-run probe confirmed that the handshake filters advertised leases by issuing run, while the caller passes its pending result to serve() unconditionally. The repair therefore also refuses a newly admitted session whose run differs from an unanswered result's issuing run, before sending that result or pulling new work. It closes the socket and reports both identities; it neither discards the result silently nor relabels it. An idle worker with no pending result may still join another run. This bounded addition preserves the same identity invariant as acknowledgment recovery.

docs.title: 3. Reserve worker identity at final admission
docs.text:
Finding: overlapping handshakes admit duplicate identities.

Keep ownership in the existing HostAdmission, HostHandshake, and listener handoff. After manifest and held-lease validation, recheck identity and reserve ownership before sending Admitted. The reservation must be visible before another handshake advances in the same PendingHandshakes.advance() batch. Rechecking a live map populated only after the batch does not satisfy this.

Preserve same-incarnation reconnects, the live-owner rules, and minted IDs' single-admission rule. Any temporary reservation belongs to its connection; refusal, disconnect, timeout, host shutdown, or failed handoff releases only that reservation. A successful handoff transfers ownership to the existing live-endpoint tracking. Add no durable registry or coordinator special case.

Acceptance:

  • Stage two real handshakes with the same worker ID and different incarnations: both Hellos pass before either manifests message completes. Admit exactly one.
  • Repeat through the production pending-handshake batch. The refusal must not release or steal the first worker's healthy lease.
  • Retain legitimate same-incarnation reattachment and stale-owner replacement; refuse overlapping reuse of a minted worker ID.
  • Abort between reservation and handoff; later legitimate admission succeeds, and cleanup cannot erase another connection's ownership.

docs.title: 4. Verify the integrated slice and align its claims
docs.text:
Make each defect a separate reviewable fix with a regression that fails on the inspected head. Then restack as needed after #341 is settled and rerun against the resulting commit. Verify #341's settling-lease protection, completion-failure subclass round trip, and guarded exception formatting remain intact.

Use existing handshake, worker-answer, reattachment, host, process, cleanup, CLI-signal, cohort, liveness, and broker suites. Preserve real-process proofs: simultaneous execution in distinct processes; worker termination during proposal and evaluation; dispatcher termination and resume; duplicate acknowledgment after restart; deterministic cohort barriers; exact accepted count accounting. Use explicit synchronization instead of timing assumptions for new regressions.

After focused checks pass, run the integrated deterministic suite, Ruff, mypy, source compilation, canonical CI examples, strict docs build, and experiment 17's no-provider dry run. Record exact source commits, commands, outcomes, and any skipped process capabilities. A dry run proves its declared contract, not live provider quality or complete paid-spend accounting.

Align programming-model.md, architecture.md, milestones.md, implementation-plan.md, project/status.md, the CLI guide, and the M11 design. At the inspected head, the API describes opt-in processes while architecture still says execution is serial and the status page implies distributed mode alone starts processes. State the actual distinction: default inline execution versus explicitly selected process backends. Keep the broader M11 gate open until its remaining slices pass. Do not repeat signatures outside their owner.

The planning completion gate was three demonstrated repairs, preserved base behavior, passing checks on the integrated commit, consistent availability claims, and a fresh review of that exact revision. The later authorization to push, merge, and reconcile GitHub tracking is recorded in the integration verification.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
After the duration parser or live SVG example, change one part of the loop at a time. Define what better means, give the proposer useful feedback, and learn to read and keep the result.

Each guide includes its own setup and runnable notebook cells. Follow the path below, or jump to the part you want to change.

The parser and SVG examples use the same components:

Component Duration parser Live SVG Artifact Parser source SVG source Proposer Revises the parser Revises the drawing Evaluator Checks expected answers Grades the rendered image Feedback Failed cases Visual critique Selected result Retained parser Retained drawing

docs.title: Follow the learning path
docs.text:
The first five guides use the same duration parser and handwritten revisions, so you can see each change without model calls. The final guide uses a small branching example to make the search decision visible.

  1. Define what better means. Write the evaluator and choose which measurement determines the winner.
  2. Give the proposer feedback. Record failed checks and use them to guide a revision.
  3. Inspect results and failures. Trace the selected version and understand unsuccessful attempts.
  4. Set limits and stopping conditions. Bound the work and stop when the result is good enough.
  5. Save and reopen a run. Keep the history, restart Python, and reuse the selected source.
  6. Choose what to try next. Compare revising the best version with exploring another branch.

docs.title: Connect your model
docs.text: Ready to replace a handwritten proposer with your agent? Use your model SDK shows request wiring, results, and usage in a routing example. If you have already connected your agent in SVG, continue with whichever guide you need above.

docs.title: Extend an experiment
docs.text:
You want to… Guide Represent, validate, and save your own value type Add an artifact domain Assemble components into a method Compose a method

Upgrading an existing experiment? Follow Migrate to 0.2. For tool choice, read When to use Meta-Evolve. The concepts overview explains the roles; the API reference documents their contracts. For a complete application to adapt, explore the examples.

docs.title: Local run browser
docs.text: Inspect saved runs, view artifacts and their differences, and compare results in an optional local browser. It reads Storage without changing history or executing experiment components.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
Install the optional dependencies, then point the command at an existing durable store:

uv sync --extra browser
meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --port 8000

Runs using a custom artifact codec can reconstruct it through the ordinary experiment-module convention:

meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --module experiments.my_run

The optional module is loaded only after browser dependencies are available. Only its experiment().registry enters the browser reader; proposers, evaluators, policies, sessions, and execution are never invoked. Without the module or codec, the run is an ordinary actionable codec-unavailable 422 state rather than corruption.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The host is fixed to loopback and the server uses one worker. The browser has no write, run, resume, cancellation, promotion, or deletion controls. It has no authentication. Loopback binding limits its intended scope; it is not a claim that the application is safe to proxy or publish remotely.

The pages are complete server-rendered HTML. Search, detail, comparison, lineage tables, and navigation work with JavaScript disabled. A small same-origin script only polls committed stream versions and reloads after facts change. A complete run page with a stable version carries no polling attributes at all; only the catalog and incomplete or unstable pages poll.

docs.title: What appears
docs.text:
The catalog is ordered lexicographically by content-derived run ID; it makes no chronological claim. Cards show task identity, lifecycle, rankability, policy, the primary objective and available score, artifact kind, and usage. Search filters those recorded fields.

A detail page follows the recorded story: overview, declaration, lineage, trials, evidence and failures, recorded artifact history, and decision timeline. The SVG lineage diagram has a semantic table containing the same parent edges. The history table preserves recorded occurrence order without calling it time, keeps occurrence identity separate from content digest, and offers one explicit diff choice for every parent.

Artifact pages show identity, parents, bounded specialized presentation, exact canonical attachment, and every available parent diff. Text, source trees, skill sets, canonical Python values, harnesses, and policy artifacts have fixed views. A custom kind receives deterministic canonical-payload text and an explicit no-specialized-view notice. All content originates in the frozen payload; decoded ArtifactView.value is never read, stringified, or passed to templates. Evidence URIs remain inert text, never links.

Direct-parent diffs support Text, SourceTree, and SkillSet. They identify added, removed, modified, and unchanged files and label added, removed, and unchanged lines textually as well as visually. A file whose content is identical on both sides reports its unchanged status without lines and consumes none of the shared diff budgets. Foreign-run views, non-parent edges, and incompatible families are refused with 422. Multi-parent occurrences never acquire an arbitrary default parent.

Bounds apply in this order: lexicographic path sorting; first 100 entries; 64 KiB UTF-8 per retained preview document; 256 KiB aggregate preview input; 64 KiB per diff side and 256 KiB aggregate diff input before invoking the diff algorithm; then 4,000 output lines. Final partial and omitted states remain visible. Canonical downloads are not truncated.

Comparison always receives an explicit ordered pair and invokes the public Run.compare() contract. It reports score, usage, winner or tie, and the three declaration flags. Incompatible or unrankable pairs remain visible as typed refusals; the browser does not pre-filter candidates or turn failure into a score.

docs.title: Replay and caches
docs.text:
One dedicated thread creates Storage.read_only(), performs every listing, version query, inspection, and comparison, and closes the handle. Route handlers and Starlette's general threadpool never receive it. This preserves SQLite connection affinity while concurrent HTTP requests queue safely.

The first catalog request performs one validated replay for every discovered run. It keeps one lightweight card per run, stamped with the exact run_version it observed and replaced when a newer version appears, plus a 32-entry LRU of full inspections. Comparisons use a separate 32-entry LRU keyed by the ordered IDs and both exact versions. Eviction discards only derived views, never durable facts. Inspections retain each frozen payload beside the decoded object, without eagerly storing an additional serialized byte copy; payload-heavy runs therefore consume proportionally more memory inside the bounded LRU. A comparison cache miss pays the public API's full multi-replay cost.

Before replay, the reader polls exact versions. Exact hits avoid replay; completed cached runs are not polled again. Catalog polling still calls Storage.runs() to discover additions and checks versions of incomplete runs.

Inspection reads a version before and after replay. A mismatch is retried once. If commits continue, the valid inspection snapshot is served without a version label or cache entry. Comparison is stricter: both versions must remain stable across the complete public comparison. A second mismatch returns retryable 503 rather than presenting a mixed observation.

docs.title: Failures and safety
docs.text:
Unknown or concurrently missing runs and artifact occurrences return 404. Comparison and diff refusals and codec capability gaps return escaped 422 pages. Transient store failures and unstable comparisons return 503. Corruption and unexpected defects return a safe 500 without a traceback or durable detail. A corrupt or codec-unavailable run becomes an isolated catalog error card so healthy runs remain reachable.

Store-open and schema failures happen before the server binds and use the ordinary CLI domain-failure path. Responses include a restrictive content security policy, nosniff, no-referrer, and frame-denial headers. These defenses do not expand the browser beyond its local, unauthenticated scope.

Raw artifact responses use application/json, nosniff, and Content-Disposition: attachment with a digest-derived filename. The bytes are the current digest encoding, canonical-payload-v1, not a native artifact export and not an unconditional promise for every future durable format.

docs.title: Manual visual review checklist
docs.text:
For changes to browser templates or CSS, review the catalog, run, artifact, diff, refusal, truncation, and codec-unavailable fixtures with JavaScript disabled at both fixed viewports:

  • desktop: 1440 × 900;
  • mobile: 390 × 844.

Record completion in the PR. Check heading order, landmarks, skip link, visible keyboard focus, native controls, textual status labels, contained wide tables and preformatted text, single-column mobile layout, and reduced-motion mode. The browser does not provide screenshot automation.

docs.title: Migrate execution budget overrides
docs.text:
For the complete upgrade path, start with Migrate to 0.2.

Execution budgets now inherit omitted task ceilings. This is the #315 source change in the Author API revision, whose working release target is 0.2.0. The package version and hosted documentation release remain separate integration work; this page describes the implemented behavior. The programming model owns the current contract.

docs.title: Tighten only what changes
docs.text:
Given a task with Budget(trials=4, evaluations=5), an execution can now pass Budget(evaluations=2). The resolved allowance is four trials and two evaluations. Previously this partial override raised ValueError because its missing trial dimension was treated as removing the task ceiling.

Execution override Effective allowance or outcome None or Budget() Four trials, five evaluations Budget(evaluations=2) Four trials, two evaluations Budget(trials=None, evaluations=2) Four trials, two evaluations Budget(trials=0) Zero trials, five evaluations; seed-only work Budget(evaluations=0) Seed admission raises BudgetUnavailable Budget(trials=3, evaluations=6) Explicit widening raises ValueError

The same rule applies to tokens, billed micro-USD, and reported elapsed time. Where the task has no ceiling, an override may introduce one. Explicit None cannot remove a task ceiling; changing that authority requires a different task declaration. A standalone Budget still uses None to mean no ceiling.

Existing valid full overrides and dataclasses.replace(task.budget, ...) calls remain valid. Empty or sparse overrides that formerly failed can now execute work; update tests or callers that relied on that rejection. Invalid explicit widening still fails before proposer/evaluator calls or committed run facts. Storage construction and seed encoding retain their earlier validation order.

The complete example below applies this restriction. Inspect result.inspect().declaration.effective_budget to see the resolved limits; the sparse request itself remains unchanged.

import meta_evolve as meta


def increment(parent):
    return parent + 1


task = meta.Task(evaluator=float, budget=meta.Budget(trials=4, evaluations=5))
experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=0, proposer=increment,
                             search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=None))
result = meta.run(experiment, budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=2))

print(result.inspect().declaration.effective_budget)
print("Proposals:", result.usage().trials)
print("Evaluations:", result.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# Budget(evaluations=2, trials=4, tokens=None, spend_micros=None, wall_seconds=None)
# Proposals: 1
# Evaluations: 2

Run it with python examples/learn/budget_overrides.py, or use the reference case.

docs.title: Existing runs and accounting
docs.text:
There is no store migration. Runs record the effective budget, and resume uses that recorded value. A partial override and its fully specified equivalent produce identical facts and identities; they cannot create separate runs in the same store. A previously rejected override has no run history to migrate.

Search presets retain their own defaults and stopping rules. Seed evaluations, failed-work costs, unknown spend, and post-call resource enforcement retain their existing accounting semantics; see evaluation and budgets.

Historical resume still requires matching registered components and source manifests. The #315 resolver alone preserved built-in manifests on its merge baseline. The integrated callback and reference changes intentionally alter source verification; old histories remain readable, but continuation requires matching source. The verification record identifies the isolated #315 baselines, and callback migration explains the subsequent boundary.

docs.title: Migrate proposer context
docs.text:
For the complete upgrade path, start with Migrate to 0.2.

Status: Shipped. This is the source implementation of #316, part of the coordinated pre-1.0 revision. The package remains version 0.1.0 until that release is published. The programming model owns the callback contract; this guide explains the transition.

docs.title: Make framework inputs explicit
docs.text:
Previously, the plain-callback adapter preferred two positional inputs whenever they bound. That made def propose(parent, factor=2) receive a context object as factor, and rejected the explicit keyword-context spelling.

Before:

def propose(parent, context):
    return parent + context.rng.choice((-1, 1))

After:

def propose(parent, *, context):
    return parent + context.rng.choice((-1, 1))

If context was unused, remove that argument entirely. Update direct Python callers too: propose(parent, context=context). No change is needed to the ordinary parent-only path.

Existing spelling New behavior and action f(parent) Receives the parent only. f(parent, *, context=None) Receives actual framework context, regardless of the default. f(parent, factor=2) factor stays 2; it is ordinary configuration. f(parent, context=None) Preparation raises TypeError; make context keyword-only or remove it. f(parent, ctx=None) or _context=None Receives parent only; the alias retains its default. Review manually if it previously used inferred context. f(parent, *args, **kwargs) Receives no extra arguments. Explicitly add keyword-only context when needed. f(parent, required) Preparation raises TypeError; bind configuration in a wrapper or partial. Uninspectable plain callable Wrap it in an inspectable callback or implement the explicit structural port.

The parent can be positional-only or itself named context. An additional positional parameter named context is reserved and rejected. Parameter annotations and aliases do not opt in. Invalid signatures fail before seed evaluation, validation hooks, or committed run facts. Callback exceptions remain typed failures under the existing failure rules; the framework never retries a body to discover how to call it.

Local bound methods, callable objects, decorated callables, and partials use their effective inspect.signature. If a partial still exposes keyword-only context, the framework supplies it even if the partial prefilled that keyword. Use a wrapper that hides it when you intend a fixed argument:

def configured(parent):
    return existing_function(parent, fixed_settings)

This is a signature pattern, not a complete runnable example. Durable registered wrappers must be plain module-level functions with declared source dependencies; local convenience does not make a closure or partial durably verifiable.

docs.title: Keep explicit adapter interfaces
docs.text:
These contracts are unchanged:

  • A structural object's .propose(parent, context) method receives two positional inputs, with the existing .propose(parent) convenience.
  • ProposerRunner.execute(parents, context) remains the explicit runner port.
  • PatchProposer owns its (tree, context) callback interface.

Normal execution chooses a declared runner first, then a structural .propose method, then a plain callable. Invalid runner metadata does not fall back to another route. A callable's valid configured .component preserves identity while retaining the plain-callback argument rule.

An explicit CallableProposer(obj) or local ComponentRef retaining a callable chooses its callable side, even if it also has .propose. Passing obj.propose as a plain callback therefore differs from passing obj as a structural object. Review the entry route before editing an adapter's method signatures.

docs.title: Registered runs and history
docs.text:
The registry now automatically includes framework binding, invocation, and registered adapter wiring in every registered proposer manifest. Continue to declare your own source dependencies. Evaluator manifests gain no invocation dependency from this change.

All pre-cutover registered proposer manifests differ, including parent-only callbacks whose behavior did not change. An unchanged function is insufficient evidence: an optional or variadic function could receive different arguments. Resume raises CapabilityError before runner construction, preflight, or new work. Policy factory setup may still execute while resolving manifests.

Use Storage.read_only(...) and Run(...) to inspect supported old histories. Continue unfinished runs with their matching package and component environment. Do not edit recorded manifests, backfill hashes, or treat a fresh run as a continuation. When intentionally changing component behavior, version the component and start a new run. Run IDs do not incorporate source manifests; an identical ID does not prove implementation equivalence, and an existing run cannot be overwritten.

The verification record covers captured old runs, same-runtime recovery, and migrated examples. Final package and hosted-site publication belong to #318/#319.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Run two improvement experiments, compare their results, and reopen their recorded history from the terminal. The walkthrough uses deterministic local examples and requires no model credentials.

docs.title: Run and compare
docs.text:
From a checkout, install the package with uv sync --locked. This offline example needs no credentials. Its artifact is a number; the proposer changes that number, the evaluator measures distance from a fixed target, and only search changes between the two declarations.

The first factory fixes the target at 12, starts at 0, and permits eight successor attempts. Greedy keeps the best measured parent; BestOfN always proposes from the seed. Feedback is omitted and named randomness uses seed 35.

Complete experiment modules

experiment.py:

"""A CLI experiment module: one ``experiment()`` factory and nothing else.

This is the whole convention. The module defines its components and returns a
typed ``meta.Experiment``; importing it starts no run, opens no storage,
and prints nothing. The command line supplies the infrastructure it owns:

    meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/experiment.py --storage ./store

``examples/learn/number_search/main.py`` is the same search written as a script.
A script is not an experiment module: importing one runs it. That difference
is exactly what this file exists to show.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import meta_evolve as meta


TARGET = 12
MOVES = (-2, 1, 5)


def propose(parent: object, *, context: object) -> object:
    """Take one random declared move away from the parent."""

    return parent + context.rng.choice(MOVES)


def score(candidate: object) -> float:
    """Higher is better; reaching the target scores the maximum 0."""

    return -abs(candidate - TARGET)


def experiment() -> meta.Experiment:
    """The factory the command line calls. Plain callables, so this module
    runs under the default ``--mode local``. See ``resumable.py`` for the
    registered-component shape ``--mode durable-local`` requires."""

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=score,
            objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=0),),
            budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=9, trials=8),
        ),
        seed=0,
        proposer=propose,
        search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=8),
        random_seed=35,
    )

best_of_n.py (keep beside experiment.py):

"""The comparison variant: the same experiment under a different policy.

``meta.Run.compare`` refuses two runs that do not declare the same task,
initial artifact, budget, and proposer, so a comparable variant has to reuse
them rather than restate them. This module therefore uses
``dataclasses.replace()`` on ``experiment.py``'s declaration to change exactly
one field — the search policy:

    meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/best_of_n.py --storage ./store
    meta-evolve compare <greedy-run-id> <best-of-n-run-id> --storage ./store

The sibling import works because the command line appends an experiment
module's own directory to ``sys.path``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace

import meta_evolve as meta
from experiment import experiment as greedy_experiment


def experiment() -> meta.Experiment:
    """Greedy hill climbing swapped for independent best-of-N attempts."""

    return replace(greedy_experiment(), search=meta.BestOfN(max_trials=8))

Start with two runs in one durable store:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/experiment.py --storage ./store
# Selected output: score 0; evaluations 6; lineage 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 7 -> 12
uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/best_of_n.py --storage ./store
# Selected output: score -7; evaluations 9; lineage 0 -> 5
uv run meta-evolve list --storage ./store

run imports one side-effect-free experiment() factory returning meta.Experiment and prints the new run's summary. list returns the stored run IDs. Use those IDs next:

uv run meta-evolve inspect <greedy-run-id> --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve compare <greedy-run-id> <best-of-n-run-id> --storage ./store

inspect reports lifecycle, rankability, declarations, attempts, evidence, and decisions, including typed failures. compare first requires a successful measurement from each run, then checks that the task, initial artifact, budget, and proposer declarations are compatible. It reports both runs and their winner or exact tie. The BestOfN module reuses the first module's declarations so only search behavior changes.

For an optional server-rendered view over the same read-only public queries:

uv sync --extra browser
uv run meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --port 8000

The local browser guide documents its fixed loopback scope, exact-version caches, rendering exclusions, and absence of authentication.

The canonical examples/operations/command_line/ walkthrough pins this entire transcript through subprocess tests.

docs.title: Reports and exit status
docs.text:
run and resume print the summary to stdout, including lifecycle, rankability, stop reason, and recorded costs. An absent score or winning lineage prints none. A measured zero is still a score; retaining the seed still ranks. Wall-clock measurements remain omitted from stable text.

Outcome stdout stderr Exit Rankable run or resume Summary Empty 0 Unrankable run or resume Summary with absent score and retained costs Empty 1 inspect of any valid history, including pending seed evaluation Detailed report Empty 0 Compatible rankable compare Comparison Empty 0 Missing/corrupt run, refused comparison, or inadmissible execution Empty Typed error 1 Usage or experiment-module error Empty Error 2

Unexpected defects keep their traceback. The migration guide explains the changed failure report; commands and factory declarations keep their existing inputs.

docs.title: Resume is a declared capability
docs.text:
Create a reconstructable run, then resume it:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py \
    --storage ./store --mode durable-local
uv run meta-evolve resume <run-id> \
    --module examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py --storage ./store
Complete resumable module 
"""The experiment-module shape ``--mode durable-local`` requires.

Same convention as ``experiment.py`` — one ``experiment()`` factory, no
import-time side effects — but the factory registers its components and
returns the registry, so the run is recorded resumable:

    meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py \\
        --storage ./store --mode durable-local
    meta-evolve resume <run-id> \\
        --module examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py --storage ./store

Two modules rather than one because the library requires different component
shapes for the two modes: local mode drives live callables, durable-local
drives registered, source-digestible module-level functions so a resumed run
can verify it is replaying the code that was recorded. The command line does
not choose between them and does not check either — it passes ``--mode``
through and lets ``meta.run`` enforce its own contract.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import meta_evolve as meta


TARGET = 6


def climb(parent: object, *, context: object) -> object:
    """Deterministic and retry-safe: the same parent always yields the same
    child, so replaying it during recovery reproduces the identical candidate.
    ``context`` is unused because this climb has no randomness in it."""

    return parent + 1


def score(candidate: object) -> float:
    """Higher is better; the target itself is the ceiling."""

    return -abs(float(candidate) - TARGET)


def experiment() -> meta.Experiment:
    """Register the components and hand back the typed declaration plus the
    registry ``meta.run`` and ``meta.resume`` both resolve against."""

    registry = meta.Registry()
    proposer = registry.register_proposer(
        "example:climb", "1", climb, deterministic=True, retry_safe=True
    )
    evaluator = registry.register_evaluator(
        "example:score",
        "1",
        score,
        deterministic=True,
        retry_safe=True,
        configuration={"target": TARGET},
    )
    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(evaluator=evaluator, budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=8)),
        seed=0,
        proposer=proposer,
        search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=8),
        registry=registry,
    )

The module registers source-digestible proposer and evaluator functions. On resume, its factory rebuilds the registry and the library verifies the recorded component identities. A local run may use durable storage and remains listable and inspectable, but it is not resumable.

The command line adds no capability rules. It passes --mode to meta.run and lets meta.resume accept or refuse the recorded run. The programming model owns the five report-verb mappings, factory convention, modes, and exit codes.

For a real interrupted-process workflow, continue with the examples/operations/durable_operations/ walkthrough.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text: Run the two commands above, then inspect the IDs printed by list. Compare their parent choices as well as their best scores. These commands report recorded results; a different search policy does not guarantee a higher score. Try resuming the local run: expect CapabilityError. The registered durable-local example can resume; repeating resume after completion adds no work.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
The CLI is a thin translation over the public run and durability contracts.

meta-evolve run MODULE --storage STORAGE [--mode local|durable-local|distributed]
                       [--workers N | --listen ADDR --key-file PATH]
                       [--lease-seconds S]
meta-evolve list --storage STORAGE
meta-evolve inspect RUN_ID --storage STORAGE
meta-evolve resume RUN_ID --module MODULE --storage STORAGE
                          [--workers N | --listen ADDR --key-file PATH]
                          [--lease-seconds S]
meta-evolve compare LEFT_RUN_ID RIGHT_RUN_ID --storage STORAGE
meta-evolve ui --storage STORAGE [--port PORT] [--module MODULE]
meta-evolve worker --module MODULE --connect ADDR --key-file PATH --worker-id ID
meta-evolve workers add WORKER_ID --storage STORAGE [--capability KEY=VALUE ...]
meta-evolve workers list --storage STORAGE
meta-evolve workers revoke WORKER_ID --storage STORAGE

Each verb makes one public call:

Verb Public call Result run meta.run(...) Run ID and summary list storage.runs() Reachable content-derived run IDs inspect run.inspect() Overview, declaration, trials, decisions resume meta.resume(...) Verified missing durable-local or distributed work compare run.compare(other) Compatible comparison and winner

worker is the second long-running exception, beside ui: it makes no run of its own, and serves one that is already listening.

workers is about the store rather than about any run in it: add enrols a worker the store will trust, list reports every enrolment it holds, and revoke withdraws trust. A revoke is installation-wide — it frees that worker's leases in every run the store carries — and list opens the store read-only, so it can be run while a dispatcher is driving.

Writing commands report the state their transaction committed, including the generation and, for add, the complete capability declaration:

shed-1 is enrolled at generation 1 with capabilities {"gpu":true}
shed-1 is revoked at generation 2
leases from earlier generations are freed in every run in this store at that run's next broker transaction

Repeating a command reports the same state. Another operator may act before or after it; the report makes no claim about a separately observed earlier row.

The module's side-effect-free experiment() factory returns Experiment. Dictionary factories remain functional under the pre-1.0 release policy, but each load emits DeprecationWarning naming the module and factory and asking for meta.Experiment(...). Unknown keys and the execution-owned storage, mode, and call-level budget remain usage errors; those overlays belong to the command line and run().

Failures in the RunError hierarchy become concise CLI errors without tracebacks. Unknown arguments, invalid factories, missing runs, capability gaps, and incompatible comparisons fail closed.

The CLI does not add an artifact history, registry, evaluator, or promotion authority of its own. Git may be ingress or egress for source, but durable Meta-Evolve artifacts and transitions remain the experiment record. Inspection includes failures, artifact occurrence identity and digest, evidence, decision rationale, and named randomness. Measured wall-clock values remain omitted so equivalent deterministic runs produce byte-identical output.

docs.title: Worker processes
docs.text:
A distributed run executes inline by default. There are two ways to select worker processes.

The dispatcher can spawn its own:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/best_of_n.py \
  --storage ./store --mode distributed --workers 4

Or it can listen, and an operator starts workers wherever there is capacity. Enrol each worker id in the store first: a listening dispatcher admits the workers this store's operator put on its allow-list, and holding the key file is not authority to claim work.

uv run meta-evolve workers add shed-1 --storage ./store

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/best_of_n.py \
  --storage ./store --mode distributed --listen 127.0.0.1:9000 \
  --key-file ./worker.key

uv run meta-evolve worker --module examples/operations/command_line/best_of_n.py \
