If you already imported Meta-Evolve, restart the kernel after installing. Then run the remaining cells in order.

Archived or offline docs: use the ZIP included with that build. Put meta-evolve.zip in the notebook's working folder (%pwd shows it; hosted notebooks let you upload files), then run %pip install ./meta-evolve.zip instead. Installing from source may still download build tools.

The package ZIP is also included with this documentation build.

Starting source and instructions. SEED reads a duration's number but ignores its unit. CONTRACT tells the proposer what the parser should do.

import meta_evolve as meta

CONTRACT = """Implement parse_seconds(text) for whole-number durations.
Inputs contain a number followed by s, m, or h, such as '30s' or '2h'.
Return the duration in seconds as an integer. Return only Python source.
"""

SEED = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    return int(text[:-1])
'''

Evaluation. evaluate returns the fraction of six checks answered correctly. load_parser executes the source locally; use this evaluator with the reviewed, handwritten code shown here.

CASES = (
    ("30s", 30),
    ("90s", 90),
    ("2m", 120),
    ("3m", 180),
    ("1h", 3600),
    ("2h", 7200),
)


def load_parser(source):
    namespace = {}
    exec(source, namespace)
    return namespace["parse_seconds"]


def evaluate(source):
    parse = load_parser(source)
    passed = 0
    for text, expected in CASES:
        actual = parse(text)
        if type(actual) is int and actual == expected:
            passed += 1
    return passed / len(CASES)


print(f"Starting score: {evaluate(SEED):.0%}")
# Output:
# Starting score: 33%

Revisions. The simulated agent adds minutes support, then hours support.

MINUTES = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    quantity = int(text[:-1])
    return quantity * 60 if text[-1] == "m" else quantity
'''

COMPLETE = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    quantity = int(text[:-1])
    seconds_per_unit = {"s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600}
    return quantity * seconds_per_unit[text[-1]]
'''

Proposer. propose supplies the instructions and current source to the simulated agent. Its response depends on the source, so reruns repeat the same revisions without a hidden response counter.

def agent(message):
    """Simulate source revisions, without a model or a call counter."""
    source = message.rsplit("Current source:\n", 1)[1]
    if source == SEED:
        return MINUTES
    if source in (MINUTES, COMPLETE):
        return COMPLETE
    raise ValueError("This simulation only recognizes the tutorial sources.")


def propose(source):
    message = f"{CONTRACT}\nCurrent source:\n{source}"
    return agent(message)

The Start here walkthrough introduces the starting parser. You can close this section once its cells have run.

docs.title: 1. Allow one proposal attempt
docs.text:
meta.improve() evaluates the seed, then proposes and evaluates revisions from the best version so far. trials=1 limits it to one proposal attempt. The seed evaluation is additional.

The returned run provides the selected measurement through best_trial(), work counts through usage(), and its recorded stop reason through inspect().

allowance_result = meta.improve(
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=propose,
    evaluator=evaluate,
    trials=1,
)
print(f"Selected score: {allowance_result.best_trial().metrics['score']:.0%}")
print("Proposals:", allowance_result.usage().trials)
print("Evaluations:", allowance_result.usage().evaluations)
print("Stop:", allowance_result.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# Selected score: 67%
# Proposals: 1
# Evaluations: 2
# Stop: trial_limit_reached

Every proposal attempt counts, even if it fails to improve the result. A failed proposal can consume an attempt without producing a candidate to evaluate. That is why proposals and evaluations have separate counts.

docs.title: 2. Stop when the score is good enough
docs.text:
meta.Task declares the evaluator and objectives. meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=0.6) means larger scores are better and a score of at least 0.6 is sufficient to stop.

meta.Experiment combines the task, starting artifact, proposer, and search policy. Greedy builds on the best measured version. Its max_trials=3 allows up to three proposals; meta.run() executes that declaration.

threshold_experiment = meta.Experiment(
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=propose,
    task=meta.Task(
        evaluator=evaluate,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=0.6),),
    ),
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
)

threshold_result = meta.run(threshold_experiment)
print(f"Selected score: {threshold_result.best_trial().metrics['score']:.0%}")
print("Proposals:", threshold_result.usage().trials)
print("Evaluations:", threshold_result.usage().evaluations)
print("Stop:", threshold_result.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# Selected score: 67%
# Proposals: 1
# Evaluations: 2
# Stop: objective_satisfied

The minutes revision passes four of six checks, exceeding the threshold. Search stops with two proposal attempts unused. This target is optional: improve() does not declare one automatically. Passing it measures these development checks; assessing unseen inputs requires separate final checks.

docs.title: 3. Put a ceiling on evaluation work
docs.text:
meta.Budget limits allowed work independently of search. Here the task allows two evaluations in total, including the seed. Set the target to 100% so we can see what happens when work runs out first.

limited_experiment = meta.Experiment(
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=propose,
    task=meta.Task(
        evaluator=evaluate,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
        budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=2),
    ),
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
)

limited_result = meta.run(limited_experiment)
print(f"Selected score: {limited_result.best_trial().metrics['score']:.0%}")
print("Proposals:", limited_result.usage().trials)
print("Evaluations:", limited_result.usage().evaluations)
print("Stop:", limited_result.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# Selected score: 67%
# Proposals: 1
# Evaluations: 2
# Stop: budget_exhausted

The seed and minutes revision use both evaluations. The task's ceiling stops search before it asks for another revision, even though the target is unmet and the search policy has remaining attempts. The selected result is retained.

docs.title: 4. Narrow the budget for one execution
docs.text:
Pass budget= to run() for a tighter allowance on a particular execution. Omitted or None dimensions inherit task ceilings, and supplied finite values cannot exceed them. A partial override such as Budget(evaluations=1) retains every other task limit; see the reference example. This call uses limited_experiment from the preceding example but allows only the seed evaluation:

seed_only = meta.run(limited_experiment, budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=1))
print(f"Selected score: {seed_only.best_trial().metrics['score']:.0%}")
print("Proposals:", seed_only.usage().trials)
print("Evaluations:", seed_only.usage().evaluations)
print("Stop:", seed_only.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# Selected score: 33%
# Proposals: 0
# Evaluations: 1
# Stop: budget_exhausted

Each run accounts for its own work. The seed preview in setup and earlier runs are separate from the counts printed by this call.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Change evaluations=2 to evaluations=3 in the evaluation ceiling example and rerun that cell. Both revisions now fit: expect 100%, two proposals, three evaluations, and objective_satisfied.

Then change satisfy=0.6 to satisfy=0.3 in the target score example and rerun that cell. The seed already qualifies: expect 33%, zero proposals, one evaluation, and objective_satisfied. Search never needs to ask the proposer for a revision.

For your own experiment, replace SEED, propose, and evaluate with your starting value, revision function, and independent grading function. Keep the same controls and inspect both usage and the stop reason: an allowance is a ceiling, not a promise that all the work will be used.

docs.title: Other resources
docs.text:
For model calls, components must report their token, monetary, and elapsed-time usage. A budget declaration does not interrupt an in-flight SDK request or guarantee a hard provider spending cap. The budget reference explains enforcement and unknown billed spend. The budget concepts explain work counts and why candidates cannot widen their own allowance.

Next, save and reopen a run so its history and selected source remain available after you close the notebook.

docs.title: Live SDK example: duration parser
docs.text:
For a first run, use the notebook learning path. This guide keeps the full live SDK, execution, accounting, and persistence example.

Meta-Evolve is a declarative Python library for evaluated evolution and meta-evolution over versioned artifacts. You define what can change and how to measure it; Meta-Evolve runs the search and records its history. Start with code, then apply the same loop to a routing prompt.

Use the same pattern for prompts, code, skills, harnesses, and search procedures. The applications overview explains the broader uses.

Status: Experimental/live-only. Offline checks cover the seed, SDK boundary, and saved runs. Live execution requires your OpenAI SDK and API key; no model result has been captured yet.

Suppose a time-tracking tool accepts "90s", but users also enter "1h30m" or "2 minutes". You want to improve the parser while keeping its behavior testable. The candidate is Python source text. A model proposes a replacement; Python checks the replacement against answers that the experiment owns.

Download the three-file parser bundle. All three complete files are also expandable below; no repository checkout or hidden helpers are needed:

File Responsibility parser.py Starting source, subprocess grader, experiment, and saved results parser_cases.py Contract, 40 development checks, and 12 separate final checks openai_client.py OpenAI request settings, output validation, and accounting

docs.title: Define what correct means
docs.text:
The contract supplied to the proposer
CONTRACT = """Implement parse_seconds(text: str) -> int.
1. Accept only nonnegative ASCII integer quantities (0-9).
2. Units: s/sec/secs/second/seconds, m/min/mins/minute/minutes,
   h/hr/hrs/hour/hours; return the total in seconds.
3. Accept one or more quantity-unit pairs, case-insensitive, with optional
   whitespace before, between, or after tokens; repeated units add together.
4. Raise ValueError for everything else: empty input, decimals, signs,
   colon notation, unsupported units, missing quantities/units, or junk.
"""

Units can repeat in any order: "1m2m" means 180 seconds. "01s" means 1 second. Whitespace may separate pairs or quantities and units; it cannot split a number ("1 2s"). Plural spelling does not depend on the quantity. Consume every input completely, including rejecting junk after an otherwise valid pair.

Input Required result Why it matters "1s" 1 Basic seconds "2min" 120 Conversion and abbreviations "1h30m" 5400 Compound duration without spaces " 2 H " 7200 Whitespace and case "0h0m0s" 0 Zero is valid "1.5h" Raise ValueError Decimal quantities are outside the contract "1h junk" Raise ValueError Reject partially valid input

These hand-curated checks cover spellings, compounds, whitespace, case, zero, and malformed inputs. The 12 distinct final inputs are withheld from search and feedback. They remain visible in source for review; separation is experimental discipline, not secrecy from a repository reader.

docs.title: Run the seed check
docs.text:
With the package installed in a checkout, the offline check is python examples/learn/llm/parser.py --dry-run. The standalone setup follows.

Use Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or Linux. Save parser.zip in a new working folder together with the matching source package, open a terminal there, and run:

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip
python -m zipfile -e parser.zip .

The source package is generated with this documentation build. Keep the three extracted files together. The SDK is needed only for the live run below.

The seed supports just s and m, without spaces. It is a plausible incomplete implementation, rather than an intentionally broken program:

Starting artifact · parser.py
SEED = '''def parse_seconds(text):
    """Parse a whole number of seconds or minutes."""
    import re
    match = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9]+)(s|m)", text)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("expected seconds or minutes")
    quantity, unit = match.groups()
    return int(quantity) * (60 if unit == "m" else 1)
'''

Run the real grader with no model requests, SDK installation, or credentials:

python parser.py --dry-run
# Output:
# Dry run: no SDK requests; only the seed is evaluated.
# Seed: 17/40 development cases
# '1s': {'value': 1}; expected 1
# '2sec': {'error': 'ValueError'}; expected 2
# '3secs': {'error': 'ValueError'}; expected 3
# '4second': {'error': 'ValueError'}; expected 4
# '5seconds': {'error': 'ValueError'}; expected 5
# '1m': {'value': 60}; expected 60

The tested output measures this seed: 17 passing checks give a score of 0.425. Correctly rejecting invalid input counts as a pass. The command prints six observations; the evaluator produces one for each of the 40 checks.

docs.title: Assemble the improvement loop
docs.text:
The proposer asks for a revision. The evaluator measures that revision against independent answers. Search chooses the parent and when to stop; feedback supplies the selected parent's already recorded development checks. The starting source is the seed. These roles become the following declaration.

This extracted function comes from parser.py. CONTRACT is shown above; evaluate grades the source, and lesson_identity records the implementation fingerprint. Their complete definitions are expandable on this page.

Experiment and explicit development feedback · parser.py
def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, *, context):
        # The newest case observations belong to the selected parent.
        observations = [record for record in context.bundle.records
                        if record.kind == "evidence" and record.value.kind == "duration-case"]
        latest = max((record.logical_step for record in observations), default=-1)
        feedback = [dict(record.value.data) for record in observations
                    if record.logical_step == latest]
        return client.generate(
            instructions=CONTRACT + "\nReturn only Python source, without Markdown fences.",
            # Evidence contains immutable mappings; JSON needs ordinary dicts.
            input=json.dumps({"source": parent, "development_checks": feedback}, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=evaluate, objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )
Role This experiment Artifact / seed The source string in SEED; each replacement is a new version Proposer propose sends the current source, full contract, and authorized observations to client.generate Task / evaluator and objectives evaluate runs development inputs and returns their passing fraction; Maximize requests a score of 1.0 Search Greedy expands the best measured candidate, with at most three revisions Feedback / experience AncestorsOnly supplies committed ancestor records; the proposer extracts only the selected parent's case observations Result Run provides the selected source, attempts, evidence, and usage External limits Fixed cases, independent answers, child limits, model settings, attempt limit, and storage location

For one revision, Meta-Evolve selects the parent and supplies its recorded observations. Your proposer asks for new source. Your evaluator executes that source in a fresh child process and grades it in the parent process. Meta-Evolve records the artifact and results, then decides whether to expand it next.

The model cannot change the experiment's answers, search limit, or satisfaction threshold. Evaluator feedback reaches the proposer through committed history.

docs.title: Improvement, ties, and regressions
docs.text:
The seed is evaluated before any revision. A perfect seed stops immediately; a revision that passes all 40 development checks also stops the search. Otherwise the loop can try up to three revisions, for at most four development evaluations and three model requests. The 12 final checks use Python only.

A tie keeps the earlier best occurrence. A worse revision remains in history but does not replace the parent used for the next proposal. best().value can therefore return an earlier revision or the seed. A final-check failure never triggers another revision. No live score, improvement, or generalization is promised by these rules.

docs.title: Inspect the grader
docs.text:
This excerpt turns the child's returned values into independent measurements. cases contains the evaluator's expected answers; rows contains the child's observed answers. None in an expected case means it must raise ValueError.

Case grading · excerpt from evaluate in parser.py
    checks = tuple(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="duration-case", data={
        "input": text, "expected": expected, "actual": row,
        "passed": row == ({"error": "ValueError"} if expected is None else {"value": expected}),
    }) for (text, expected), row in zip(cases, rows))
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": sum(check.data["passed"] for check in checks) / len(checks)},
        evidence=checks, usage=usage,
    )

The parent compares actual values with expected answers and sends only inputs to the child. Wrong answers lower the passing fraction; execution faults stay typed:

What happened Recorded result Wrong integer, return type, or exception for an input An observed failed case; the evaluation remains rankable Source cannot be parsed, required callable is absent, or output protocol is malformed InvalidOutput, with no score Source fails during module initialization EvaluatorFailure, with no score Execution exceeds its wall or CPU limit TimeoutFailure, with no score Child output exceeds its limit ResourceExhausted, with no score The evaluator cannot create a workspace or start Python InfrastructureFailure, with no score

Each evaluation uses a new temporary directory and isolated Python invocation. The child gets a minimal environment without OPENAI_API_KEY, a three-second wall limit, a two-second CPU limit, and at most 65,536 bytes of combined output. The parent reads at most that much output and cleans up the process group. Successful evaluations retain case observations; failed executions retain bounded process output when available. Proposal usage survives a later grading failure.

This is trusted development execution. The child can still access the host filesystem and network; a fresh directory and stripped environment are not hostile-code isolation. Use a disposable environment for model-generated source you have not reviewed.

docs.title: Run with a model
docs.text:
Install the optional SDK in the environment from setup, set OPENAI_API_KEY through your usual credential mechanism, and choose a new output directory:

python -m pip install openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
python parser.py --run ./runs/duration-parser-01
# Makes up to three model requests; provider charges may apply.
# Prints each measured score, selected source, tokens, billed spend, and final check.
# Exact scores and token counts depend on the model responses.

The declared model is gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17, overridable by OPENAI_MODEL. The official model page lists this snapshot and Responses support. Requests use a 120-second SDK timeout, zero retries, 4,096 output tokens, and reasoning effort none. The wrapper applies the SDK timeout and retry options. The SDK timeout is not a hard total wall-clock deadline across network phases.

The Responses schema provides input and output tokens, but no exact per-call bill. Total tokens are input_tokens + output_tokens; cached input is already included. Without a billed receipt, the run reports billed spend: unknown and remains usable. A monetary ceiling stops further work if a bill cannot be verified; token and trial bounds still apply. Estimates do not establish a bill, including with API-key login.

docs.title: Understand the result
docs.text:
The live command prints each measured attempt, the selected source, usage, and one separate final check. Seed is the baseline; Revision 1 is the first proposal. Best measured source is the retained winner, not necessarily the last proposal. A typed failure has no score. Development usage excludes the separate final check stored in final.json.

Live capture pending: see evidence and verification. No live improvement or score is asserted here. The seed-check comments above are measured offline output. A future live excerpt must identify its retained records and configuration; live outcomes vary.

docs.title: Keep the work
docs.text:
run_lesson(client, directory) runs the experiment through meta.run with durable storage. Choose a new directory that survives process exit. It saves:

File or directory What you can inspect later configuration.json Model declaration, attempt bound, execution limits, Python version, and implementation digest history/ Committed source versions, evaluations, evidence, feedback, decisions, and usage run-id.txt The run to reopen, including its committed prefix if accounting aborts selected.py The best measured source after a completed search final.json One separate final check, its observations, and its own usage accounting-unknown.json Accounting interruption and any available receipt, if execution aborts

With a saved run at ./runs/duration-parser-01, inspect it in a new process:

python parser.py --inspect ./runs/duration-parser-01
# Prints retained attempts, the best measured source, usage, and the final report.
# Makes no SDK requests and does not execute candidate code.

Local callables support reopening; resuming this local closure is unsupported. An accounting interruption retains committed history and available receipts, without selecting a result or running final checks. Copy a reviewed selected.py into your application to reuse it; selection does not deploy the source.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
In SEED, replace text with text.strip() in the re.fullmatch call and run --dry-run again. Predict the effect before running: the present seed's passing count stays at 17. Whitespace handling alone cannot add the missing full unit spellings or compounds in these development cases. Add a check for " 1s " to see what that change actually fixes. Changing the grader changes the experiment.

In run_lesson, change the default trials=3 to trials=1 to reduce the maximum number of rewrite requests. It need not change the selected source: the first revision may already be sufficient. Keep the final set out of both revision requests and search when adapting this lesson.

docs.title: The same loop, a different artifact
docs.text:
Role Duration parser Routing prompt Artifact / seed Python source Instructions for a response model Proposer Model writes new source Model writes new instructions Task / evaluator and objectives Python executes 40 cases; maximize passing fraction A fixed response model answers 40 tickets; Python grades labels Search Greedy, at most three revisions, stop at 1.0 Same Feedback / experience Selected parent's development observations Same, with ticket responses External limits Child execution and model request limits Request limits also apply inside evaluation

The live routing example applies these roles to a prompt and includes its own setup. To change one component at a time, follow the guide path, starting with your evaluator and its feedback.

docs.text:
The guide path covers these capabilities with handwritten revisions. These retained downloads apply them to this live parser and include their complete runtime source. Each uses the same independent grader and SDK boundary.

Capability Download Inspect results inspect_parser.zip Change search search_parser.zip Compare feedback feedback_parser.zip Add metrics metrics_parser.zip Set a target threshold_parser.zip Bound work limits_parser.zip Reopen history reuse_parser.zip

docs.title: Complete source
Report your own cost
docs.text:
Optional custom cost reporting

The example's OpenAIClient accepts a function or bound method through cost_reporter(response). It receives the raw SDK response once and returns CostReport(usd, kind, source) or None. Save this beside the three runtime files:

run_with_cost.py · an illustrative user price, not OpenAI pricing
from decimal import Decimal
from openai_client import CostReport, OpenAIClient
from parser import run_lesson

def report_cost(response):
    usd = Decimal(response.usage.output_tokens) * Decimal("0.000002")
    return CostReport(usd, "estimated", "my output rate: USD 2 per million, v1")

with OpenAIClient.from_environment(
    cost_reporter=report_cost, cost_reporter_id="my-output-rate-v1",
) as client:
    run_lesson(client, "./runs/duration-parser-cost-01")
# An output of 1,000 tokens reports USD 0.002000 (estimated).
# Input-token cost is excluded by this chosen formula; billed spend stays unknown.

For an API lookup, replace the callback body with your own receipt client:

Callback body · billing_api is your configured client
def report_cost(response):
    receipt = billing_api.lookup(response_id=response.id)
    if receipt is None:
        return None  # Receipt unavailable: keep billed spend unknown.
    return CostReport(Decimal(receipt.usd), "billed", receipt.id)
# A receipt of USD 0.012345 reports 12,345 billed micro-USD in Usage.

CostReport is local to openai_client.py; core has no provider dependency. Use exact decimal strings and give your lookup a timeout. Change cost_reporter_id whenever pricing or lookup behavior changes. A report's kind, raw amount, rounded-up micro-USD, and source are retained as evidence. Only billed enters Usage.spend_micros; estimates remain visible in inspection. A lookup error records cost-reporting-failure and keeps the model result with unknown spend. Inspection reuses committed reports without repeating a lookup.

Empty or incomplete responses retain usage in a typed failure. Missing required token accounting after dispatch raises ExecutionAccountingUnknown; the driver saves available receipt details. A transport failure cannot become free work.

docs.title: Verification and remaining work
docs.text:
The seed check and deterministic tests cover grading, feedback, selection, accounting, and reopening. Offline tests do not establish model performance. Evidence and verification tracks retained live captures and independent review.

docs.title: Live SDK example: routing prompt
docs.text:
For a first run, use the notebook learning path. This guide keeps the full live SDK, execution, accounting, and persistence example.

Status: Experimental/live-only. The loop is tested offline with injected providers. No retained live transcript is available yet; no improvement is promised.

A support inbox needs to send each ticket to billing, account, or technical support. The candidate is the instruction text, not the model's answer. A model proposes revised instructions. To measure them, a fixed response model routes tickets and Python compares its labels with independent expected answers.

This lesson stands on its own. Download the three-file prompt bundle: prompt.py contains the loop, prompt_cases.py contains the policy and cases, and openai_client.py owns SDK requests and accounting. All three files are expandable at the end of this page.

docs.title: Define what correct means
docs.text:
The initial prompt already states the intended policy correctly. Improvement means better measured adherence, not inventing a different routing policy:

Routing policy and starting instructions
POLICY = """Route each support ticket to exactly one team:
billing: charges, invoices, or refunds.
account: identity, access, or account changes.
technical: product malfunction.
For mixed requests, follow the explicitly requested primary action.
If no primary action resolves the tie, choose account before billing before technical.
Return only the lowercase label: billing, technical, or account."""
SEED = POLICY  # Start with the correct policy; improvement is not guaranteed.
Ticket Expected label Reason “I was charged twice. Please refund the duplicate.” billing Requested refund “I lost my recovery codes.” account Restore access “The dashboard freezes.” technical Product malfunction “I cannot sign in, but my priority is a refund.” billing Explicit primary action wins “Reset my password and send my invoice.” account Unresolved tie: account precedes billing

There are 40 fictional development tickets and 12 distinct final tickets. Final checks run once after selection and never enter search or feedback. The full case file is visible for review; separation does not make its contents secret.

docs.title: Install and preview
docs.text:
With the package installed in a checkout, the offline check is python examples/learn/llm/prompt.py --dry-run. The standalone setup follows.

Use Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or Linux. Save prompt.zip in a new working folder together with the matching source package, open a terminal there, and run:

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./meta-evolve.zip
python -m zipfile -e prompt.zip .
python prompt.py --dry-run
# Preview only: prints the policy, six labeled cases, request bound, and configuration.
# No SDK requests; accuracy is not measured.

The package comes from this documentation build; no checkout is needed. Keep all three files together. Unlike the parser's seed check, routing cannot measure a prompt without calling a response model. This preview does not simulate answers.

Selected lines from the real credential-free preview, checked by an automated test:

# Dry run: no SDK requests; accuracy is not measured.
# 'I was charged twice for this month. Please refund the duplicate.' -> billing
# 'I lost my recovery codes. Help me regain access.' -> account
# 'The dashboard freezes whenever I open the chart.' -> technical
# "I cannot sign in, but my priority is a refund for yesterday's charge." -> billing
# 'Please reset my password and send a copy of my invoice.' -> account
# "Please fix the broken export and refund this month's charge." -> billing
# Maximum requests: 163 development + 12 final = 175 (no retries).

docs.title: Assemble the improvement loop
docs.text:
The proposer writes revised instructions using the selected parent's recorded observations. The evaluator asks the response model to follow those instructions and grades the answers. Search selects the next parent and decides when to stop. Feedback is explicitly authorized development evidence.

Experiment and feedback · extracted from prompt.py
def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, *, context):
        latest = context.evidence.latest("routing-feedback")
        if latest is None:
            raise meta.CapabilityError("No routing feedback selected; check the evidence label and max_records.")
        if latest.data.get("prompt_sha256") != sha256(parent.encode()).hexdigest():
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Selected feedback is for another prompt; use RecentAncestors with enough records.")
        if context.evidence.truncated:
            print("Feedback: using the selected report; some context records or rendered text were truncated.")
        return client.generate(
            instructions=(
                "Rewrite the routing prompt to follow this policy. "
                "Return only the prompt.\n" + POLICY
            ),
            input=json.dumps({
                "prompt": parent, "development_checks": latest.data["checks"],
                "development_complete": latest.data["complete"],
                "development_failure": latest.data["failure"],
            }, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=lambda prompt: evaluate(prompt, client),
            objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.RecentAncestors(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )

POLICY and SEED are shown above. evaluate is shown below; lesson_identity fingerprints the implementation. The complete definitions are on this page. This is an extracted function, not an additional program to maintain.

Role This experiment Artifact / seed The policy text in SEED; each proposed prompt is a new version Proposer propose asks client.generate for revised instructions Task / evaluator and objectives evaluate obtains ticket responses and grades their labels; maximize passing fraction, satisfying at 1.0 Search Greedy, at most three revisions after the seed Feedback / experience RecentAncestors; context.evidence.latest("routing-feedback") reads a complete selected report External limits Fixed cases, expected labels, response-model configuration, request limits, attempt bound, and storage

For one revision, Meta-Evolve selects the parent and supplies its authorized history. Your proposer sends that prompt and its development observations to the model. Your evaluator uses the replacement instructions for each ticket. Meta-Evolve records the responses, measurements, and usage, then selects the next parent. The candidate cannot change the answers, response-model configuration, feedback authorization, or attempt limit.

The evaluator reserves routing-feedback for one report containing its checks, completion/failure state, and prompt digest. The proposer verifies that digest against its parent; the label alone proves neither authorship nor occurrence. Disabled context raises ContextDisabled. An enabled policy with a missing or different-parent report raises CapabilityError before any rewrite request. Increase the record allowance or fix the policy/report label, then start a new run.

The truncation notice means records were omitted or rendered text was clipped. A retained structured report remains usable. max_chars does not trim its data or bound the SDK request; the fixed cases and request settings bound this lesson. Rejected siblings are outside the selected parent's ancestry. Keep Experiment here to record the SDK environment and accept budgets; the small callable path needs fewer declarations.

docs.title: Inspect the evaluator
docs.text:
The model returns text; Python grades it. After stripping surrounding whitespace, only the exact expected lowercase label passes. There is no model judge. A wrong label is a measured failure. An unavailable response stops that evaluation with a typed failure and retained known usage, without a misleading partial score.

Independent grading · extracted from prompt.py
def feedback_report(prompt, checks, *, failure=None):
    """One evaluator-owned report, including partial observations after failure."""
    return meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="routing-feedback", data={
        "prompt_sha256": sha256(prompt.encode()).hexdigest() if isinstance(prompt, str) else None,
        "checks": [dict(check.data) for check in checks],
        "complete": failure is None,
        "failure": failure.kind if failure else None,
    })


def evaluate(prompt, client, *, cases=DEVELOPMENT):
    """Measure every ticket, or retain a typed failure without a partial score."""
    if not cases:
        raise ValueError("evaluation requires at least one ticket")
    if not isinstance(prompt, str) or not prompt.strip():
        failure = InvalidOutput(message="expected a nonempty prompt")
        return meta.EvaluationResult(
            failure=failure, evidence=(feedback_report(prompt, (), failure=failure),),
        )
    usage, evidence, checks = meta.Resources(), [], []
    for ticket, expected in cases:
        try:
            response = client.generate(instructions=prompt, input=ticket)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            error.receipt = {
                "request": getattr(error, "receipt", None), "ticket": ticket,
                "completed_usage": asdict(usage),
                "completed_evidence": [evidence_record(item) for item in evidence],
            }
            raise
        usage += response.usage
        evidence.extend(response.evidence)
        if response.failure is not None:
            evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="routing-unavailable", data={
                "input": ticket, "expected": expected, "failure": response.failure.kind,
            }))
            evidence.append(feedback_report(prompt, checks, failure=response.failure))
            return meta.EvaluationResult(
                failure=response.failure, usage=usage, evidence=tuple(evidence),
            )
        check = meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="routing-case", data={
            "input": ticket, "expected": expected, "actual": response.candidate,
            "passed": response.candidate.strip() == expected,
        })
        checks.append(check)
        evidence.append(check)
    evidence.append(feedback_report(prompt, checks))
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": sum(check.data["passed"] for check in checks) / len(cases)},
        usage=usage, evidence=tuple(evidence),
    )

cases defaults to the development set. evidence_record, included in the full script, serializes observations if accounting becomes unknown. Completed response evidence stays available even when a later ticket fails. Its final feedback report then contains only completed checks and a typed failure, allowing a failed seed to be revised without pretending the remaining tickets were measured.

For expected billing, " billing\n".strip() passes; "Billing" and "billing because..." are completed wrong answers. Empty or incomplete model output with known tokens becomes InvalidOutput, without a score. A typed timeout or infrastructure failure from the provider boundary keeps its type. If request seven fails, the first six responses and all known usage survive; the remaining tickets are not silently marked wrong.

docs.title: Run with a model
docs.text:
Install the SDK separately, set your own API key, and choose a new persistent directory:

python -m pip install openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
python prompt.py --run ./runs/routing-01
# Calls the model for both rewriting and ticket responses; provider charges may apply.
# Prints measured attempts, response evidence, selected prompt, usage, and final check.
# Live scores and token counts vary; this is not a captured transcript.

The default model is gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17; override it with OPENAI_MODEL. The shared wrapper uses the Responses API, a 120-second SDK request timeout, zero automatic retries, 4,096 output tokens, and reasoning effort none. The SDK timeout is not a hard total wall-clock deadline across network phases. Configuration stays fixed across candidates and is saved in configuration.json.

The maximum is 163 development requests: 40 seed responses plus 3 × (1 rewrite + 40 responses). The separate final check adds 12 requests, for 175 total, without retries. Early satisfaction or failures can reduce that number. A perfect seed still needs 40 responses to establish its score and 12 final responses; it makes no rewrite request.

Tokens are input plus output tokens; cached input is already included in input. Billed spend stays unknown unless an exact receipt is supplied. Estimates are evidence, not bills. A monetary ceiling stops further work when spend cannot be verified; it is not a provider-side hard spending cap. Missing token accounting after dispatch raises ExecutionAccountingUnknown and retains available receipts. The default has no monetary ceiling; its bound is the request count. A programmatic budget applies to development search, while final usage is separate.

docs.title: Understand the result
docs.text:
The driver prints Seed, each revision, a representative ticket observation, and Best measured prompt. Read the actual label beside its expected label to understand a failed case. Inspect history/ for all retained observations. It also prints a captured RunSummary: baseline and selected measurement, proposals, evaluations (including the seed), typed failures, stop reason, usage, and saved-history location. The report is captured inside the storage block and rendered after it closes. New Run queries still need an open store.

A tie keeps the earlier best occurrence. A regression stays in history and does not become the next parent. A score of 1.0 stops development early. The best prompt may therefore be the seed or an earlier revision. A final-check failure never triggers another rewrite, and final results do not alter development scores.

Live results need evidence tied to code and configuration; one run does not establish generalization or guarantee the same answers on repetition.

docs.title: Keep the work
docs.text:
run_lesson uses durable storage before selecting a prompt. Choose a new directory for each run; an existing directory is refused to avoid overwriting history.

Saved item Meaning configuration.json Model, implementation fingerprint, Python version, attempts, and declared budget history/ and run-id.txt Committed versions, observations, decisions, usage, and run identity requests.jsonl Completed requests, responses, failures, evidence, and usage, including uncommitted calls selected.txt Best measured prompt, if one exists final.json Separate final measurements, responses, failure if any, and usage accounting-unknown.json Available receipts and interrupted phase when accounting is unknown

Open a fresh terminal, activate the same environment, and inspect without a key:

. .venv/bin/activate
python prompt.py --inspect ./runs/routing-01
# Reads retained attempts, responses, selected prompt, configuration, and final report.
# No model calls or new evaluations.

Reopening does not resume the local callables or regenerate model responses. The driver uses meta.open_run(history_path, run_id=saved_id) and closes the owned handle on exit. Missing/corrupt stores and stale IDs keep typed errors. Without a saved ID, only a single run can be inferred; multiple IDs require explicit selection. Lexical ID order does not mean latest. See reopening for the standalone notebook form. If no candidate was successfully measured, there is no selected prompt and no final check. An accounting interruption leaves the committed prefix inspectable. Selecting a prompt does not deploy it.

If accounting interrupts the seed, there may be no committed run or run ID yet; inspection still reads available reports. requests.jsonl has one JSON object per completed call, including rewrites. Read it to inspect every response without model calls. The journal and history overlap: do not add their usage totals together. An interruption during final checking preserves the selected prompt and development history. Load selected.txt as UTF-8 text to reuse its instructions in your own application.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text: In run_lesson, change the default trials=3 to trials=1 and run into a new directory. Predict the upper bound: 40 + (1 + 40) = 81 development requests, plus 12 final requests. The winner may stay the same; fewer attempts do not promise a different score. Keep policy, cases, and model settings fixed when comparing the two runs. Never use final tickets as rewrite feedback.

docs.title: Rehearse offline
docs.text:
From a repository checkout, these tests replace only the provider while running the actual grader, search, accounting, and storage. No fixture is imported by the public lesson:

python -m pip install pytest
python -m pytest -q tests/test_llm_prompt_lesson.py tests/test_llm_prompt_feedback.py tests/test_llm_prompt_persistence.py tests/test_llm_prompt_docs.py
# Offline verification; no API key or model requests required.

These tests exercise improvement, ties, regressions, failures, and final-set separation with synthetic provider responses. Their scores and accounting are not a live transcript. Evidence and verification tracks live captures and independent review.

Driver, evaluator, and experiment prompt.py
"""Improve a routing prompt with model responses and independent Python grading.

Run --dry-run without credentials. See docs/learn/llm-prompt.md for the lesson.
"""

import argparse
from dataclasses import asdict
from hashlib import sha256
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput
from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown

from prompt_cases import DEVELOPMENT, POLICY

SEED = POLICY  # Start with the correct policy; improvement is not guaranteed.


def feedback_report(prompt, checks, *, failure=None):
    """One evaluator-owned report, including partial observations after failure."""
    return meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="routing-feedback", data={
        "prompt_sha256": sha256(prompt.encode()).hexdigest() if isinstance(prompt, str) else None,
        "checks": [dict(check.data) for check in checks],
        "complete": failure is None,
        "failure": failure.kind if failure else None,
    })


def evaluate(prompt, client, *, cases=DEVELOPMENT):
    """Measure every ticket, or retain a typed failure without a partial score."""
    if not cases:
        raise ValueError("evaluation requires at least one ticket")
    if not isinstance(prompt, str) or not prompt.strip():
        failure = InvalidOutput(message="expected a nonempty prompt")
        return meta.EvaluationResult(
            failure=failure, evidence=(feedback_report(prompt, (), failure=failure),),
        )
    usage, evidence, checks = meta.Resources(), [], []
    for ticket, expected in cases:
        try:
            response = client.generate(instructions=prompt, input=ticket)
        except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
            error.receipt = {
                "request": getattr(error, "receipt", None), "ticket": ticket,
                "completed_usage": asdict(usage),
                "completed_evidence": [evidence_record(item) for item in evidence],
            }
            raise
        usage += response.usage
        evidence.extend(response.evidence)
        if response.failure is not None:
            evidence.append(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="routing-unavailable", data={
                "input": ticket, "expected": expected, "failure": response.failure.kind,
            }))
            evidence.append(feedback_report(prompt, checks, failure=response.failure))
            return meta.EvaluationResult(
                failure=response.failure, usage=usage, evidence=tuple(evidence),
            )
        check = meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="routing-case", data={
            "input": ticket, "expected": expected, "actual": response.candidate,
            "passed": response.candidate.strip() == expected,
        })
        checks.append(check)
        evidence.append(check)
    evidence.append(feedback_report(prompt, checks))
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": sum(check.data["passed"] for check in checks) / len(cases)},
        usage=usage, evidence=tuple(evidence),
    )


def experiment(client, *, seed=SEED, trials=3):
    def propose(parent, *, context):
        latest = context.evidence.latest("routing-feedback")
        if latest is None:
            raise meta.CapabilityError("No routing feedback selected; check the evidence label and max_records.")
        if latest.data.get("prompt_sha256") != sha256(parent.encode()).hexdigest():
            raise meta.CapabilityError("Selected feedback is for another prompt; use RecentAncestors with enough records.")
        if context.evidence.truncated:
            print("Feedback: using the selected report; some context records or rendered text were truncated.")
        return client.generate(
            instructions=(
                "Rewrite the routing prompt to follow this policy. "
                "Return only the prompt.\n" + POLICY
            ),
            input=json.dumps({
                "prompt": parent, "development_checks": latest.data["checks"],
                "development_complete": latest.data["complete"],
                "development_failure": latest.data["failure"],
            }, default=dict),
        )

    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(
            evaluator=lambda prompt: evaluate(prompt, client),
            objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1.0),),
            environment={"model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity()},
        ),
        seed=seed, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=trials),
        context=meta.RecentAncestors(max_records=200, max_chars=64_000),
    )


def lesson_identity():
    root = Path(__file__).parent
    return {
        "sha256": sha256(b"".join((root / name).read_bytes() for name in
                                 ("prompt.py", "prompt_cases.py", "openai_client.py"))).hexdigest(),
        "python": sys.version,
    }


def evidence_record(item):
    return {"kind": item.kind, "data": dict(item.data)}


def save_json(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, default=dict) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


class RequestJournal:
    """Retain completed calls even if a later call prevents a history commit."""

    def __init__(self, client, path):
        self.client, self.path = client, path
        self.configuration = client.configuration

    def generate(self, *, instructions, input):
        result = self.client.generate(instructions=instructions, input=input)
        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as journal:
            journal.write(json.dumps({
                "instructions": instructions, "input": input,
                "candidate": result.candidate,
                "failure": result.failure.kind if result.failure else None,
                "usage": asdict(result.usage),
                "evidence": [evidence_record(item) for item in result.evidence],
            }, default=dict) + "\n")
        return result


def show(result):
    for index, attempt in enumerate(result.trials()):
        outcome = attempt.failure.kind if attempt.failure else (
            f"{attempt.metrics['score']:.0%}" if attempt.metrics else "incomplete"
        )
        print(f"{'Seed' if index == 0 else 'Revision ' + str(index)}: {outcome}")
        checks = [item.data for item in attempt.evidence if item.kind == "routing-case"]
        if checks:
            row = next((row for row in checks if not row["passed"]), checks[0])
            print(f"  {row['input']!r} -> {row['actual']!r}; expected {row['expected']}")
    try:
        print("Best measured prompt:\n" + result.best().value)
    except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
        print("No successfully measured prompt.")
    return result.summary()  # Capture while storage is open; rendering needs no handle.


def run_lesson(client, directory, *, seed=SEED, trials=3, budget=None):
    """Save the selected prompt, then perform one final check outside search."""
    root = Path(directory)
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    save_json(root / "configuration.json", {
        "model": client.configuration, "lesson": lesson_identity(), "trials": trials,
        "budget": asdict(budget) if budget else None,
    })
    client = RequestJournal(client, root / "requests.jsonl")
    phase = "development"
    try:
        with meta.Storage.durable(root / "history") as storage:
            try:
                result = meta.run(experiment(client, seed=seed, trials=trials), storage=storage, budget=budget)
                snapshot = show(result)
                selected = result.best().value if snapshot.rankability == "rankable" else None
            finally:
                run_ids = storage.runs()
                if len(run_ids) > 1:
                    raise meta.RunSelectionRequired(run_ids)
                if run_ids:
                    (root / "run-id.txt").write_text(run_ids[0].value + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(snapshot)  # The captured report remains usable after storage closes.
        if selected is None:
            print("Separate final check: skipped; no successfully measured prompt.")
            return result.id
        (root / "selected.txt").write_text(selected, encoding="utf-8")
        from prompt_cases import FINAL

        phase = "final"
        final = evaluate(selected, client, cases=FINAL)
        save_json(root / "final.json", {
            "metrics": dict(final.metrics),
            "failure": ({"kind": final.failure.kind, "message": final.failure.message}
                        if final.failure else None),
            "evidence": [evidence_record(item) for item in final.evidence],
            "usage": asdict(final.usage),
        })
        print("Separate final check:", final.failure.kind if final.failure else
              f"{round(final.metrics['score'] * len(FINAL))}/{len(FINAL)}")
        print(f"Final tokens: {final.usage.tokens}; see final.json for separate usage and evidence.")
        return result.id
    except ExecutionAccountingUnknown as error:
        save_json(root / "accounting-unknown.json", {
            "phase": phase, "reason": str(error), "receipt": getattr(error, "receipt", None),
        })
        raise


def main():
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    modes = cli.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    modes.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="preview policy and cases; no model calls")
    modes.add_argument("--run", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="save a new experiment and final check")
    modes.add_argument("--inspect", type=Path, metavar="DIRECTORY", help="read saved results; no model calls")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    if args.dry_run:
        from openai_client import configuration

        print("Dry run: no SDK requests; accuracy is not measured.")
        print(POLICY)
        for ticket, expected in DEVELOPMENT[:6]:
            print(f"{ticket!r} -> {expected}")
        print("Maximum requests: 163 development + 12 final = 175 (no retries).")
        print("Configuration:", json.dumps(configuration(), sort_keys=True))
    elif args.inspect:
        identity = args.inspect / "run-id.txt"
        run_id = identity.read_text().strip() if identity.exists() else None
        try:
            with meta.open_run(args.inspect / "history", run_id=run_id) as result:
                snapshot = show(result)
        except meta.RunNotFound:
            if run_id is not None:
                raise  # A saved explicit identity must never fall back to another run.
            print("No committed run. No successfully measured prompt.")
        else:
            print(snapshot)
        for name in ("configuration.json", "final.json", "accounting-unknown.json"):
            path = args.inspect / name
            print(f"{name}:", path.read_text() if path.exists() else "not recorded")
    else:
        from openai_client import OpenAIClient

        try:
            with OpenAIClient.from_environment() as client:
                run_lesson(client, args.run)
        except (meta.CapabilityError, ExecutionAccountingUnknown) as error:
            cli.exit(2, f"{error}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
