docs.title: Documentation audit and editorial conventions
docs.text: Lead with improving solutions and the methods that produce them. The use, compose, and evolve journeys connect that idea to implementations and research directions. The complete duration parser teaches the common API; task guides and examples provide next steps. Keep instructions beside code and evidence.

docs.title: Ownership and navigation
docs.text:
Section Reader's question Content owner Start What can I improve, and how do I begin? Homepage overview and First experiment parser walkthrough Guides How do I change one part of an experiment? Evaluation, proposal, search, feedback, limits, storage, and composition Examples How does this apply to my problem? One catalog of maintained runnable examples Concepts Why does it work this way? Explanations under the architecture contract Reference What does this API accept and return? Source signatures, detailed contracts, tools, programming model, and the complete command inventory Development (secondary) What exists, and how do I contribute? Contribution routes, contracts, status, roadmap, research map, design and evidence indexes

The homepage remains accessible through the logo. Order guides as a learning path and link related pages by purpose. Keep historical URLs or explicit redirects when moving their navigation entries. Source repair, integer demonstrations, and evidence notebooks are additional examples rather than competing introductions.

Development links to indexes and canonical overviews; detailed designs and historical notebooks remain accessible at their existing URLs. Examples owns runnable methods and applications, grouped by what changes and how it is judged. The parser's primary next step is live SVG Feedback Descent; adaptation guides, the live parser, and the gallery provide alternatives. Keep one navigation home per page and avoid an automatic footer that contradicts the tutorial's next step.

Open the programming model with the mental model and callable API. Ordinary guides and concepts explain current behavior without milestone chronology; project status and evidence records retain development history. Preserve decision-relevant limitations beside the behavior they qualify. Navigation checks protect reader routes and historical destinations, not an exact submenu layout or leaf count.

The homepage has three blocks: an introduction to broad artifact improvement and improving the method itself, a canonical parser declaration with its measured result, and selected examples. Keep the proposer’s handwritten behavior and its agent/LLM replacement point clear in the shared code comments. Link the primary action to the complete parser tutorial; feature SVG Feedback Descent, EvoSkill, and Meta-Harness in that order, followed by the example catalog. These are a selection, not permanent categories. Keep setup, availability, authentication, and development details on their substantive pages.

The tutorial and README retain installation, every definition, one handwritten revision, independent evaluation, and verified output. The homepage includes only the canonical improve declaration; literal README cells and shared setup are checked against their owners. Execute the excerpt with the canonical definitions and test the full tutorial outside the checkout with the installed package. Keep the notebook export complete and runnable.

The programming model owns the shipped API; architecture owns domain semantics; milestones owns scope and acceptance gates; and the implementation plan owns technical staging. Design records remain subordinate, including records whose decisions later shipped.

docs.title: Comparisons and positioning
docs.text: The comparison explains method reuse, structured artifacts, composition, and evaluating improvement procedures through concrete examples. It answers fit, authoring responsibilities, and next steps. Support external capability claims with versioned primary sources, check dates, and the material actually inspected. Name uncertainty instead of inferring absence; preserve unrelated source dates. Compare complete setup and responsibilities, not call-site argument counts. Qualify storage, recovery, accounting, and execution guarantees beside their benefits. Live performance claims must link retained evidence; tutorial scores remain teaching evidence. Conceptual roles, availability, autonomy, and strength of evidence answer different questions. Keep the survey's attributed autonomy map on its research page. Distinguish empirical evidence, conditional proofs, and bias-relative search guarantees; a practical estimator does not inherit an idealized oracle's guarantees. Keep historical comparison anchors.

docs.title: Method walkthroughs
docs.text:
The gallery at examples.md owns discovery of runnable methods and applications. It shows the editable artifact, evaluation, and a brief execution requirement; the walkthrough owns detailed setup and commands. The complete script inventory lives at reference/example-commands.md. The research map at research/index.md owns proposed mappings and adjacent references under Development. Keep one canonical walkthrough per method and preserve retired catalog URLs through substantive redirects. Keep availability aligned with research/catalog.json; use only Shipped, Experimental/live-only, and Design—not shipped as status labels.

Open every algorithm or method page with a short What it does. and How it works. summary before setup, component tables, or implementation details. Explain the problem, the changing object, and the distinctive mechanism in plain language, so the paper is optional reading. Cite the primary source for research claims and distinguish its method from this repository's adaptation or proposal. For surveys, benchmarks, and infrastructure references, describe their contribution without pretending that each is an optimization algorithm.

Keep that orientation consistent while preserving the method's teaching order: SVG shows drawing and critique; EvoSkill makes direct agent calls before search; Meta-Harness measures a harness through fresh repairs. Preserve captured outcomes and code provenance. Prose-only changes must not invalidate or silently replace live evidence; code changes require the existing capture-validity checks.

SVG is a live walkthrough. Introduce Feedback Descent and link the Stanford blog before setup. Show the ask input/output boundary so readers can use their own agent; explain revise and grade alongside their code. Keep required helpers expanded, optional display code collapsed, and the captured images as supporting evidence. Exercise replacement agents without making billable calls in tests.

After the problem, answer the four method questions: what changes, what generates the change, what judges it, and what is retained? Name fixed controls and actual stages, including search and feedback. Keep exact algorithm scope, complete setup, supported execution, result interpretation, adaptation, and evidence together. Identify whether the candidate is an output, generator, policy, or research procedure.

State which results are returned, persisted, or produced by later calls. Capturing inner histories and forwarding physical usage are explicit choices; nesting supplies neither automatically. The nested-evaluation comparison shows the different policy and AutoResearch boundaries. An outer Run need not capture or resume the whole method.

Implementation scope and evidence are separate from availability. Preserve the distinction between a mechanism fixture, live integration, and a reproduction. A search preset does not establish a complete research method. Scientific discovery belongs in the framework's application scope, while unimplemented scientific methods retain their Design—not shipped status. New method releases update the canonical walkthrough, catalog, source/download links, and evidence together; composition claims point to code showing actual compatible reuse. State authentication and platform needs separately from status. Distinguish live-capable code, offline SDK rehearsal, and a retained live capture, and identify the tested source/package through the existing evidence records. Publish package, support downloads, and documentation as one verified build; a working local download path is not evidence of public availability.

docs.title: Concept conventions
docs.text:
Concepts start with the duration parser. Offer the path: improvement loop → artifacts → meta-evolution → evaluation and authority → experience → deeper semantics. Keep search, history, budgets, failures, identity, domains, and conformance discoverable. Evaluation and authority also appear in introductions.

The loop owns optional base notation; meta-evolution adds the procedure candidate. Link those definitions after concrete examples. They are teaching notation, not new API types or a prerequisite for the quickstart. Diagrams label mutable candidates, fixed controls, and optional feedback. Keep overviews compact; show branching, rejection, and seed evaluation in detailed traces. Use text as well as color and preserve offline readability. Selection may retain the seed; it promises neither a gain nor promotion.

Open each primary page with a plain-language definition, what the reader supplies, and what they can do with it. Explain declaration fields for values such as Task and Experiment, and public methods for active or inspectable objects such as Session and Run. Keep evaluator measurements distinct from the task's evaluation contract. The programming model owns the core-object progression; link there instead of repeating full contracts. Use an example, then link a runnable guide and its owned reference. Concept pages need no full notebook; supplemental scripts name repository setup. Distinguish evaluator and proposer authorship from permission to read evidence. Keep simulated proposals and measured behavior explicit, and use only verified example results.

Use recognizable navigation names and links by purpose. Preserve URLs and heading fragments when retitling; navigation supplies the reading order.

docs.title: Lesson conventions
docs.text:
Make rewritten instructional pages self-contained: purpose, prerequisites, setup, code, expected observations, explanation, and one focused exercise. Links offer optional depth, not missing steps. A discovery page helps readers choose a tutorial; it need not reproduce every tutorial.

The limits guide established the pattern used by evaluation, search, feedback, inspection, and persistence: open with the problem and a short task chooser, then put complete prerequisites in one collapsed section labeled Required setup for a fresh notebook, before the executable task cells. Tell readers to expand and run setup first, then run the examples in order. Folding required setup does not make it optional. Keep the actual change, output, interpretation, and exercise visible. Explain each API before use and link to Start here for the full parser explanation. Reuse canonical snippets; all definitions must be copyable from the page. Use inline settings in the chooser instead of duplicate executable previews. Fold shared preparation, keeping the guide's new concept visible: evaluation teaches the grading function; feedback teaches evidence and its use; inspection prepares a mixed history before querying it. Persistence keeps saving, the kernel restart, reopening, and export visible. Its reopening cell is self-contained. Include a focused answer to a likely question and explain what to replace for the reader's own task. Update the newcomer and regression handoff with changed cells, setup discovery, question retrieval, and transfer tasks. Agent preflight does not establish independent human understanding. Test each rewritten guide in a fresh namespace and from outside the checkout with the installed package; executing a prerequisite page first is insufficient.

The evaluation guide consolidates the earlier metrics lesson. The limits guide consolidates the earlier threshold and budget lessons. Their previous URLs and fragments redirect to the relevant sections. One SDK notebook guide owns setup and real request wiring. Its accounting and tool details are in Reference; larger SDK applications are in Examples. The old migration URL redirects to the retained removal history. CLI, browser, and extension contracts are in Reference. The SDK introduction keeps installation, credentials, request controls, both callables, declaration, execution, and inspection visible. Only the complete request-accounting wrapper is folded as required setup before use. Keep the request cell separate, explain its bound and rerun behavior, and link deeper failure/accounting details from the point where the reader needs them. Feedback, inspection, and saving also run in fresh notebooks. The saving guide additionally verifies reopening after the original Python process exits, with no proposer or evaluator definitions and no exported source file required. The SDK notebook is tested through the official SDK with simulated HTTP responses, including failed requests and missing usage. Those checks establish the wiring and accounting, not live model performance. The harness guide uses a handwritten help assistant to teach both configuration changes, independent answer checks, fresh held-out evaluation, and export/reload. Tests execute its displayed cells and exercise failures and incompatible grading. The policy guide runs inner number searches to grade candidate search settings. Its notebook retains and reopens every inner history, separates inner and outer work counts, compares fresh held-out runs, and tests the fixed budget ceiling. The artifact-domain guide defines a recipe value and codec in visible cells. It separates structural validity from useful steps, rejects foreign proposals, and reopens saved recipes in a fresh process with only the type and codec. The displayed codec also passes the published conformance suite.

Extract focused code from canonical scripts, keeping required cells in execution order and definitions before use. Start here keeps installation and Python cells visible without CLI drivers or companion lesson imports; its folds contain optional explanations. Tests execute required folded cells, preserve indentation, and match rendered copyable code. Preserve historical fragments; setup links land at the visible fold so readers can expand it. Continuations name their prerequisite page and define each addition. Put verified output beside the command, preferably as comments; longer transcripts can use adjacent output blocks. Explain what changed and why, including failed attempts. Prefer readable fields and response evidence to raw object dumps.

Use consistent roles: artifact/seed, proposer, evaluator, task and objectives, search, experiment, session, run, explicit feedback/experience, and external controls. Introduce only the roles the current question needs. Selection never grants deployment authority. A failed measurement has no score; a measured wrong response may have a low score. Persistence does not imply resumability, and recorded replay does not rerun a model.

docs.title: Evidence and compatibility
docs.text:
Use only Shipped, Experimental/live-only, and Design—not shipped as status labels. Describe deterministic fixtures, dry runs, and retained live captures separately as evidence modes. Shipped lessons need no repeated banner. Never replace missing live evidence with a transcript that looks like a model run. Label illustrative output explicitly; exercises predict qualitative behavior, not guaranteed live scores. Live claims must match retained authorized evidence.

Example pages name editable content, independent grading, selection data, separate final checks when present, replacement points, and evidence limitations. Notebook mirrors remain byte-identical to their canonical sources. Site builds publish saved outputs without executing notebooks. Keep unique historical measurements and research decisions even when beginner prose is superseded.

docs.title: Destination coverage
docs.text:
Each maintained page should answer a distinct reader question. Extend an existing page when the explanation belongs there. Keep unique measurements and design decisions accessible through Development; a historical inventory entry does not require a page in the learning path.

Add a guide: write the task, setup, runnable cells, expected observations, and adaptation advice. Link it from the appropriate index or navigation and add relevant execution/output checks. No history or redirect entry is required.

Edit a guide: run its affected executable checks and the rendered-link checks. Tests protect results, complete copyable setup, actual destinations, and evidence. They do not prescribe sentences, cell counts, or submenu layouts. Review explanations and claims against the canonical contracts; use the newcomer walkthrough to assess understanding, answer-finding, and adaptation.

Move or retire a page: inspect repository links, known published routes, and the fixed tests/fixtures/documentation_routes.json compatibility baseline. Preserve supported anchors with explicit IDs or add a source, destination, and explicit fragment mappings to docs/redirects.json. Remove the obsolete source file; the existing MkDocs hook generates its route, working fallback links, and search exclusion. To move only old fragments from a maintained page, omit target and supply fragments; known bookmarks redirect in the browser while ordinary visits and unknown fragments retain the page. Point current internal links directly to maintained pages. Missing destinations, collisions, and redirect chains fail the build; rendered checks catch broken links and fragments. Keep unknown existing promises until there is evidence for a deliberate retirement, recorded with its reason and replacement in the review. Repository privacy does not establish lack of use.

The compatibility fixture is a fixed set of promises, not a current page or heading inventory. Add entries only for deliberate compatibility commitments. The pre-#299 migration inventory is retained in history; no hook or test consumes it. The maintenance review records which checks moved, what was removed, and the retained hook responsibilities. #300's contributor instructions should link here rather than duplicate these rules.

docs.title: Historical review record
docs.text:
The parser and prompt entrance and downloads came from #278–#280; #281 supplied the capability continuation. Meeting notes retains extraction evidence, and agent test-repair retains source-tree and command-grading evidence. The #283 consolidation changes navigation and destination coverage, not those experiments. The historical destination map preserves the earlier manual split.

Independent newcomer walkthroughs and their acceptance ownership remain separate from automated checks. See the walkthrough. Research migrations retain their existing owners; editorial work does not reopen them. The handoff separates participant prompts from observer answers and records navigation, predictions, adaptations, and assistance. Agent preflight findings are recorded there separately from human session results.

docs.title: Entrance build and checks
docs.text:
Notebook tests execute displayed cells, verify output, and reopen persisted history in a fresh process. Source-package ZIPs contain installable source and metadata; lesson ZIPs contain runtime files without test clients or repository imports. Missing files fail the build. Download checks execute extracted files outside the checkout and reopen saved results in a fresh process.

uv sync --locked --group docs
uv run --locked --group docs mkdocs build --strict

Run the affected lesson and example checks whenever code or captured output changes. The Docs workflow owns the integrated test selection and fresh-install notebook, SDK and download checks. Inspect navigation, code, and output on desktop and mobile. Automated execution and agent visual inspection do not establish human usability.

Handwritten pages normally stay below 300 lines and notebook cells below 40. The retained live parser and routing guides are exceptions: each keeps an existing complete SDK execution, accounting, and persistence protocol together, with expandable full source. These guides preserve the earlier live walkthroughs; the first-run notebook path stays small and uses the shipped callable API.

docs.title: Evidence and verification
docs.text: These records preserve measurements and the circumstances in which they were obtained. For a runnable starting point, choose an example. Use current status and the roadmap to distinguish available behavior from work still in development.

docs.title: Historical learning notebooks
docs.text:
These detailed tours retain the original demonstrations and saved outputs. Their terminology and progression reflect the project at the time; the task guides teach the current authoring path. Site builds publish saved notebook outputs without executing them again.

Subject Explanation Recorded notebook Search policies Policy tour Executed tour Policy comparison Comparison lesson Comparison report Experience reuse Experience tour Executed tour Pushed and pulled experience Push and pull lesson Lab Derivation and comparison Derivation lesson Lab Crash recovery Recovery lesson Executed notebook Source patching Source tour Executed notebook

docs.title: Maintained example supplements
docs.text:
Start with the linked walkthrough for setup, interpretation, and limitations. These notebooks supplement maintained examples; they are not model-performance claims.

Purpose Walkthrough Recorded notebook Improve a research procedure Autoresearch Nested improvement Optimize a scheduler Systems optimization Simulator experiment Improve skill documents Skill library Captured live OfficeQA notebook Improve a context playbook ACE Context playbook Improve a repair harness Meta-Harness Standalone lesson, live outputs pending

The policy-evolution roadmap owns its flagship scope; A5 owns the research migration.

docs.title: Live research and provider records
docs.text:
The three featured lessons have different evidence and execution requirements. Availability is the catalog status; it does not identify whether a model account is needed. Read a capture without making calls, or follow the lesson's setup to run a new experiment whose outcome may differ.

Lesson Retained evidence Execution and source SVG Feedback Descent September 21 live capture: all seven images, critiques, scores, parent choices, selected SVG, and reported usage; records Codex authentication; the self-contained notebook owns the executable example EvoSkill September 21 Claude/OfficeQA capture: native skill creation/use, population attempts, held-out tie, and SDK receipts; code fingerprint protects saved outputs Claude authentication; canonical Python generates the page and notebook with versioned support files Meta-Harness Offline installed-package and copied-page SDK rehearsals; live capture pending Claude authentication and supported local confinement; canonical Python generates both routes; the deterministic reference retains its separate evidence

These records describe particular source/configuration snapshots, not benchmark gains or guaranteed rerun outcomes. Their local presence does not establish that new download routes have been published. Use package and support archives from the same verified documentation build; publication remains an independent gate.

The bounded live-agent track records provider setup and evidence limitations. The SealQA labs are Experimental/live-only; their notebooks remain explicitly unexecuted until an authorized capture exists:

  • SealQA prompt adaptation and notebook.
  • AutoData walkthrough and notebook.

The Experimental/live-only Meta-Harness lesson and standalone notebook use Claude SDK agents. The notebook has no saved live outputs; its verification record covers offline transport rehearsals, independent grading, and standalone execution.

The retired API spike's source, notebooks and capture and findings retain the original tested API. Plain callables worked, but provider evidence and both proposer/evaluator usage needed durable recording; random seeds did not make hosted responses reproducible. The prototype internals were not durable kernel contracts. M8’s first authorized SDK capture failed strict schema validation before native mutation decoding; later captures reached the trusted successor boundary. These outcomes remain in closed, unmerged PR #162. The A4 stack also retains an equivalent capture in the repository: two complete manifests through successor validation, SHA-pinned by tests. Neither the failures nor the later successes were rewritten into evidence of statistical generalization. M8 closure did not merge additional harness code from PR #162.

The live parser and live routing examples are Experimental/live-only. Retained live evidence remains pending in #271, under #270's protocol. Independent SDK rehearsal remains with #269. Offline checks establish request wiring and accounting, not live model quality.

The research catalog connects these experiments to their source methods.

docs.title: Documentation and usability verification
docs.text:
These receipts remain while release and independent review are active. Their source/package pins and read-versus-resume results must not be regenerated as if they were old evidence.

  • API release #319: integrated verification, decision baselines, reference, partial budgets, callback context and run summaries.
  • Authoring and newcomer handoff: first run, feedback, display, small-path options, reopening and practical journeys. The walkthrough owns #275/#277's independent review; #343 owns the teaching revisions. Agent rehearsals are recorded separately.
  • First notebook #344: Jupyter acceptance records Salah's review, five-cell execution, installer provenance and the remaining hosted Colab/site follow-up.
  • Plain introduction #345: story acceptance records the homepage, README, concrete illustrations, glossary and reviewed notebook, with automated evidence and visual/hosted verification limits.
  • Other decisions: comparison review retains source checks and outstanding independent review; SDK accounting explains the narrowed implementation and remaining limits.
  • Trusted-worker administration #203: M11.4 verification records the commits, the checks, the mutations that did not redden a law and a live run with real processes and no provider spend.
  • Ongoing checks: editorial conventions and the maintained CI/Docs workflows own the current procedure.

docs.title: Completed design and documentation work
docs.text:
Completed work orders and dated reports live at this fixed source revision. They preserve rationale and evidence, including unsuccessful outcomes, without competing with current guides or making historical proposed APIs look available.

  • Historical roadmap and technical plan: completed acceptance checklists and stage-by-stage decisions. Their old compatibility policy is superseded by the current release policy.
  • M8 design, M10 six-journey scorecard, proposal/citation decisions, source-view decisions and SDK removal decision. Current contracts live in architecture, experience and SDK reference; example-specific rationale lives with the harness example.
  • Completed API and UX plans preserve selected and rejected designs. The current foundation and comparison decisions own release rationale.
  • Editorial plans and verification preserve the #278–#310 source/environment pins, commands and review limits, including research source inspections. The frozen migration inventory is historical bookkeeping; current destination promises are tested independently.

docs.title: Bounded feedback verification
docs.text: Source work for #332, September 19, 2026, on base 1607afbb81f7c5e457f97eb437b13ffb9ad63267. This records source verification, not package publication or independent newcomer validation. Concurrent #331, #333, #334, and #335 changes remain separate work. The plan records the selected contract and the experience guide explains migration.

docs.title: Historical evidence
docs.text:
Before changing runtime source, the base revision's src/ tree was extracted with git archive. A Python 3.12.13 process explicitly imported that tree and captured a durable run interrupted after five actual committed batches. Its committed context selection and best value 1 remain in tests/fixtures/pre_332_evidence/interrupted; no event prefix was fabricated. The frozen components.py, capture receipt, store hashes, and reproduction instructions are retained beside it. The receipt separates SQLite's ephemeral sidecars from committed database and artifact bytes. The historical check copies only committed files into a fresh temporary directory, so it also verifies a checkout without those sidecars.

A separate copy resumed under that matching runtime to the exact serialized event stream of an uninterrupted run. The final best value was 2: the old 20-record ancestor selection fed stale evidence into the third proposal. The new policy's six-proposal example reaches 6 under a two-record bound while preserving exact evidence provenance. This is a deterministic mechanism check, not evidence of model improvement.

docs.title: Source identity changes
docs.text:
No durable record or event schema changed. Registered proposer manifests now automatically cover the evidence views, ProposerContext, ContextDisabled, and actual sequential/distributed context construction in addition to the existing invocation, adapter, and user dependencies. Evaluator dependencies remain unchanged. This intentionally changes all registered proposer hashes, including callbacks that do not consume evidence.

The context-policy module is hashed in full, so adding the recency policy changes the hashes below even though AncestorsOnly@1 and BestSibling@1 retain their prior selection semantics:

Policy Previous implementation digest Current implementation digest ancestors-only@1 d2ef7615b61b17b04651d9ca06fdfe4d3f0541f18d5b4be9d51e65292e9ea75e d214c18a4665f821559466987483ba36d03931cb9cbbbe3634be56c0e23e04ba best-sibling@1 8180b93acf6b2be7638e709e9412abaf1794df5e06e50427343dd0e3d58dd7e3 18587b8be83b1f6a9aca019aba8dd5310d8f480ba56122ef2b207e44db899315 recent-ancestors@1 No previous implementation 49ac89266afa9a467a805bf91a75555ea7246536a25a16db6c62faeb8e2469c7

Historical stores and selections stay readable. Tests compare each changed manifest independently, then prove refusal before runner construction, preflight, proposer/evaluator work, or event/usage changes. Old #316 captures also retain their original bytes; their context-enabled case now encounters context-policy drift first, while the context-disabled case encounters search drift. Independent invocation checks remain in both cases. An unchanged run ID never substitutes for matching source. Continue old runs in their matching environment or explicitly declare a new run after migration.

docs.title: Acceptance evidence
docs.text:
• test_context_evidence.py checks disabled versus declared-empty selection, exact labels/order, immutable data/provenance, optional off comparisons, producer-label limits, no pull calls, and reads after storage closes.
  • test_recent_ancestors.py checks conformance, the growing-history regression, zero/small record and text limits, hidden/future/rejected records, sibling selection, and explicitly selected failed-evaluation evidence without scores.
  • test_recent_context_resume.py checks every interrupted batch boundary, committed selection reuse, policy identity/reconstruction, source drift, and fresh-process imports. Existing callback tests cover distributed delivery.
  • test_context_evidence_history.py checks the captured old store and refuses incompatible continuation without new work.
  • The feedback lesson keeps scores 2/6, 4/6, 1 with feedback and 2/6, 2/6, 2/6 with the explicit optional guard and context disabled; each uses two proposals and three evaluations. The reference example exercises six improvements with structured evidence and deliberately clipped text.

docs.title: Final verification

docs.title: Agent SDK accounting: first implementation for #337
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

The requested lightweight first slice of #337 is implemented under experiments/sdk_accounting/, with usage instructions in its README. Run it from the source checkout with:

uv run --locked python -m experiments.sdk_accounting.run

The historical plan retains the broader proposed study; its matrix is outside the accepted scope. The accepted lightweight scope closes the decision with usable small recipes and focused offline evidence. Full runtime acceptance and a live SDK campaign are not claimed. No public provider API is added.

docs.title: Disposition
docs.text:
Keep the three wrapper recipes and the small experiment-local reporting function. A public helper is not justified by this slice. Shared result construction is useful, but Resources and the existing rich results already cover much of it. SDK-specific usage scope, lifecycle and failure handling remain the larger work.

The comparison retains a plain constructor baseline in comparison.inline_report and compares it with accounting.finish after identical native extraction. This is a narrow before/after reporting comparison, not proof that the complete new wrappers are equivalent to historical live drivers. Historical captures and their assumptions remain unchanged.

Target Concrete accounting trace Before/after reporting Codex Thread snapshots 8 → 17 contribute 17 once; a prior thread total is explicitly subtracted on continuation. Failed-turn notifications remain available. Same candidate/failure, resources and receipt evidence. Claude Agent SDK Main-loop fields describe 14 tokens; the two model entries describe 14 + 3 = 17. The last query snapshot contributes 17, not the sum of snapshots or both accounting views. Same candidate/failure, resources and receipt evidence. Pi Session total 100 → 117 contributes 17 after settlement; context size 9,999 is not consumed work. Compaction events can follow agent_end. Same candidate/failure, resources and receipt evidence.

These numbers are synthetic fixtures. All three runnable examples retain unknown spend, one proposal and two evaluations. The fixed Python grader assigns 2 to durable typed records; this is not a model-improvement measurement.

docs.title: What was simplified, and what was not
docs.text:
Author work Result of the first slice Build a rich result without dropping failed-work costs One local finish() consistently preserves resources and omits the candidate keyword on failure. Explicit candidate=None is not the same as omitting it. Validate/convert an exact bill, preserve its source, retain unknown spend Shared reporting handles this small repeated operation; estimates and bill lookup policy remain with the caller. Decide which token totals mean this invocation's work Still different in all three wrappers. No universal event decoder is warranted. Start, consume, interrupt and close the SDK Still native: Codex turn handles, Claude async iterators, Pi subprocess/RPC. Pi's bridge is materially larger than its result constructor. Change tools, permissions, models, session policy or grading Remains explicit caller configuration and independent evaluation. There is no new provider registry or coordinator branch.

The benefit is consistent reporting, not an elimination of the important author decisions. The shared function also adds code for bills and diagnostics that the unknown-bill constructor baseline does not need. A shorter call site therefore does not establish a total reduction in complexity or justify a public API.

Codex's pinned convenience collector can raise on a failed turn before returning its collected usage; the recipe consumes notifications directly. Claude's richer model totals still have a documented coverage boundary: some internal helper calls are excluded. Pi's bridge requires a settled event and a final statistics reply. An unavailable measurement escapes with a receipt rather than becoming zero usage or a low score. These wrappers report runtime-reported invocation work, without certifying otherwise unobservable calls.

The callable improvement loop, configurable experiments, bounded search, explicit experience, durable history, and local inspection are Shipped. The task guides show how to use them; the examples apply them to prompts, source, skills, harnesses, search policies, and a systems simulator.

The programming model owns the public API contract; the roadmap owns milestone status and scope.

docs.text:
The integrated source Shipped partial budget restrictions, keyword-only plain callback context, winner-independent summaries, budget-led preset limits, and component Resources. Follow Migrate to 0.2. The package still reports 0.1.0 pending the coordinated 0.2.0 release; use this documentation's source download or matching commit. The version string alone does not identify this source revision. Package publication remains #319's separate gate.

The integration verification identifies source, tests, installed examples, history compatibility, and deployment.

docs.title: Distributed execution
docs.text:
M11.0–M11.4 are Shipped: the design record, concurrency-ready fold, durable work table, dispatcher, generational cohorts, explicit worker process backends, and trusted-worker administration. Distributed mode defaults to inline execution. Workers can be spawned for the run (--workers N) or started by an operator against a listening dispatcher (--listen ADDR --key-file PATH, plus meta-evolve worker). Each worker runs one call at a time and is admitted by a handshake that authenticates a shared key and checks that it runs the same build. A worker an operator names must also be enrolled in the run's store (meta-evolve workers add ID --storage PATH); spawned --workers N workers are the dispatcher's own and need no enrolment. An enrolment may declare capabilities (--capability KEY=VALUE), and a worker is admitted only if they meet every component's work_requirements. Revoking a worker (meta-evolve workers revoke) reaches every run in the store: its leases are stale at the next transactional check, and the item runs again elsewhere under the same trial. Recovery is available in both directions: a killed dispatcher leaves no spawned worker behind and its run resumes, and a killed worker costs one attempt.

The worker-process verification record retains the full stabilization receipt and identifies final stack integration separately; the worker-administration record retains M11.4's. The complete M11 gate remains Design—not shipped: multiprocess load validation (#204) and the canonical trusted-workers example (#205) remain unfinished. Measured-budget allocation (#206) and a retained public-API live-concurrency capture (#218) also remain open.

The current scope requires a cohort-capable search policy (BestOfN is the shipped example), no pushed context or pull experience, and budgets whose finite dimensions are trial and evaluation counts. Finite token, elapsed-time, and monetary ceilings are refused. A worker's environment fingerprint is matched at admission against the dispatcher's current build; a run resumed on a build that has moved is not refused, and resume reports the change. Multi-host use is documented and untested: the shared key authenticates a connection and does not encrypt it, so a non-loopback address needs TLS that Meta-Evolve does not provide. See the trusted-concurrency roadmap for the remaining acceptance gates and storage upgrades before opening older stores.

Federation and the post-local-author notebook/browser presentation follow-up also remain Design—not shipped.

docs.title: Implementation history
docs.text:

External SDKs are user-owned callables, with no first-party provider adapter in the package.

Milestone 10 completed the local author experience on August 14, 2026: Experiment, improve(), functional @search, Run.inspect(), read-only storage, paced and resumable Session, and the optional browser with artifact presentation. The roadmap records the individual slices and acceptance criteria.

docs.title: Trusted-worker administration verification
docs.text: Initially verified September 23, 2026 for #203, the M11.4 slice. The plan records scope and the decisions AD1–AD7 and PD1–PD8; the design record owns the rules; the command-line guide owns usage.

docs.title: Source and scope
docs.text:
The checks below ran on local branch m11.4-pr2-capabilities-and-record, whose first 26 commits are the registry-and-revocation pull request (tip a62e3858) and whose base is origin/main at 69354f9ebb66df37e5bfc78c26aecff2d1d78fae. The branch was first verified before review; the sections through Live, no spend are that round's, with each commit it cites rebased to the SHA it has now. A review round from the repository owner followed, as the nine rows beginning "Review:" below. A /pr-review round on the pushed drafts came next, as the eleven rows beginning "pr-review:", and every check was run again on the result; see final re-verification. These sections retain the historical checks and CLI transcripts at c0781f12; the follow-up below records the current integration changes.

Commit Change 88055abb Move the diagnosis rule out of the lease and ledger modules: a pure move that frees both for the revocation sweep. a090dbb6 The trusted worker in the domain; the id grammar and reserved namespace get one home; WorkerNotTrusted. b258b0ac The trusted-worker port (reader and authority), its in-memory adapter and the registry laws. 95857e68 Store schema 5: the trusted_workers table and the write guard on work_items; schema 4 still opens read-only. 1560ac58 The SQLite registry and Storage.trusted_workers(). e43ad3b7 The door: an operator's worker is admitted only if the store trusts it, read at Hello and again before the reservation. 2f2c638a Both brokers refuse a claim from a worker the store does not trust. ca4ed8bd A revoked worker's lease is STALE_GENERATION at the next transactional check. ec10930a The revocation sweep frees the lease at the next broker write and records WorkerRevoked. b54a0e65 The meta-evolve workers verb: add, list and revoke. b1f6d3cf Enrolment and revocation proved with real processes; guides and record updated. 6eeebb4d First two-axis review: the durable reader is a real reader; registry reads fail typed. 24bb74e1 Second review: a damaged trust row's scope stated honestly; the allow-list read lazily. 71f9585e Review: a malformed id is refused by trust and revoke alike, typed; TrustedWorker backstops it. 72f0e335 Review: a read-only registry reads the schema version with its rows, so a held reader sees another connection's migration. 3da528c5 Review: _answer shows answer, release and disconnect in order; dispatch_revocation.py keeps only the predicate. f2ef6368 Review: the directory AST ban is replaced by a law on the real _terms lookup; PD5's evidence restated. dac9594c Review: mypy now checks the handoff path (distributed_drive, dispatch_admission, host, worker_identity, admission, the port). 22e01018 Review: comments trimmed in nine registry modules, comments and docstrings only. 37a17c38 pr-review: rollover runs the revocation arm, so a restarted drive's first write records why it freed a revoked holder's row; a lease both revoked and overdue is lawed. 09433d7b pr-review: workers revoke refuses an id nothing enrols from a read-only look, so a schema-4 store is never migrated only to refuse. 19ab03c7 pr-review: every sqlite3 failure of a trust-row read is DurableStoreError, not only OperationalError. 639970ed pr-review: a damaged trust row stops any listening run its worker connects to;
