workers add --capability KEY=VALUE. 4cbc927e Environment drift reported on resume, never refused (AD6). 0dfebf06 The consolidated evidence that workers mint no identity. f542e863 The record's worker-administration section, status labels, source forward references, this receipt. 25329881 Review fixes: spawned runs with conflicting requirements lawed; a missing capability's refusal worded precisely; plan-label cites disambiguated; one value renderer. 514ac940 The previous round's final re-verification section of this receipt. 8d4e81b5 Review: a refusal too large to frame is sent short, and costs its connection, never the run; capability refusals quote at most 200 characters. 778cafda Review: the resume report validates history once and fingerprints only a distributed run; EnvironmentDrift moves to environment.py. 9976aeaf Review: comments trimmed in the capability modules; three record laws check structure, not sentences. 6f05b895 pr-review: --capability refuses a lone surrogate and a key repeated inside a JSON object as usage errors, before any store opens. 7bd6fd9c pr-review: Run.environment_drift() and EnvironmentDrift in the programming model. 8b62c7ed pr-review: an oversized worker_nonce is refused by name, Terms is sized at the minted nonce length, a raw sqlite3 fault stops the run, and Refused keeps the exception. c891a37a pr-review: the refusal's 200-character quote cut-off is pinned by a unit law. c0781f12 This receipt, brought up to date for the /pr-review round.

docs.title: Mutations that did not redden a law
docs.text:
Every law was planted with its named mutation and watched going red, except these. They are retained as the commits reported them. Every law the review round and the /pr-review round added went red under its named mutation (the one law that pins existing behaviour is noted below), so none is listed here.

  • Removing the Hello trust read alone (b1f6d3cf) leaves the process laws green: the second read, just before the reservation, refuses the same worker. The ordering is pinned in tests/test_worker_trust_admission.py instead.
  • Dropping the sweep's generation arm on the submission path (b1f6d3cf) leaves the process law green: answering a revoked holder releases its lease, and that release is the broker write that frees the row. The sweep laws pin the arm.
  • Keeping the verifier when the sweep frees a lease (ec10930a) leaves every law green: the cause write already refuses a later diagnosis, and every other path meets the generation check first. The verifier is cleared because the record requires it and because it is one statement shared with release and rollover.
  • workers list opening the store durable (b54a0e65) leaves the held-store law green, because SQLite tolerates a second writer; the read-only claim rests on the byte-identity law.
  • Skipping the shared freeze of a declared capability (e75a1891) stays green: the value is also frozen by the SQLite encoding and compared by canonical bytes, so any one of the three is masked by the other two. The command-line array law goes red instead under "the command line takes arrays and objects as literal text".
  • Three identity mutations (0dfebf06) go red through the replay fold's own refusal rather than the law's assertion: a second guard in the domain.
  • The revoked-door law's cost assertions (24bb74e1) — rows ready at attempt 0, epoch unchanged — cannot redden under a door mutation, because the handshake holds no broker and acquire refuses a revoked worker on its own. They record the refusal's cost rather than guard it.

docs.title: Failed attempts retained
docs.text:
• The first real-process revocation law found a defect the wire laws had missed (b1f6d3cf). A revoked holder's result is classified by submission_status, which is a read and moves nothing, and the dispatcher drops the binding before settling, so the row stayed LEASED with nothing bound to it and the undecidable-frontier refusal aborted the drive. "Freed at the next broker write" had no next write on that path. Answering a revoked holder now releases its lease first. The wire law that had asserted rows() == before for that path was pinning the stranding, and now asserts the release.
  • The durability guide, the plan page, a law's docstring and a commit message once said an unreadable trust row stops every run in the store. The sweep is scoped to its run, so it stops only the runs its worker holds a lease in; the documents were corrected in 24bb74e1 and the law now pins both halves.
  • The byte-gate script used for the first pull request drives inline durable-local runs, distributed runs at widths 1–3 under the default inline execution, and three failure paths. It spawns no worker process, so on its own it does not cover --workers N. For this receipt a second script drove the same fixture through WorkerProcesses(1) and WorkerProcesses(2) on both trees; see the gate table.
  • During the live check below, a first ps | grep -c for leftover workers counted 1. The one match was the invoking shell's own command line, which contained the search text; listing the matching lines on the rerun showed no worker or dispatcher process.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
Environment: macOS 26.5, Python 3.12.11, SQLite 3.49.1 as linked by that interpreter, with the locked development, browser and documentation dependencies installed in the isolated worktree.

Check Result .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider 7,128 passed, 94 skipped, no failures, 668.79 seconds. uv run --locked ruff check src Passed. uv run --locked mypy Passed: 24 configured source files. uv run python -m compileall -q -x '/candidate/' src tests examples, after the suite; the resulting __pycache__ directories were then removed Passed. uv run --locked --group docs mkdocs build --strict Passed with no MkDocs warning of its own. The 93 pandoc "Div … unclosed" notices printed during the notebook conversion also appear on origin/main. Five canonical CI examples (number search, policy comparison, text optimization, SQL migrations, durable operations) All exited 0. Experiment 17 driver.py --dry-run All 11 scenarios passed; none errored, failed a check, or omitted its verdict. StubProvider, no provider spend. Byte gate, inline: the first pull request's script with this tree's src on PYTHONPATH, against its capture from origin/main Byte-identical (118,089 bytes): durable-local, distributed widths 1–3 and three failure paths. Byte gate, spawned workers: the same fixture through WorkerProcesses(1) and WorkerProcesses(2), origin/main against this tree, each side run twice Event bytes (ordered for one worker, as a sorted multiset for two) and work rows identical; each side agreed with itself across runs; this tree's registry is empty after both.

The 94 skips comprise 36 inapplicable extension-conformance laws (24 cohort laws for a program with no cohort method, 12 codec and evaluator fixture laws a fixture declared empty), 55 checks needing an optional package this environment does not install (pydantic, openai, openai_codex, claude_agent_sdk), and 3 platform cases: macOS has no Landlock, no /proc/self/root, and an enforcement mechanism that makes the no-mechanism case inapplicable.

The suite ran once, on the tree with this receipt present and its results not yet filled in; filling them changed only this table and this paragraph. After that the record and receipt laws, the documentation ownership and consolidation laws and the strict build were run again and passed. One design-record cell was also reworded after the suite started, to say that a missing capability is refused naming the key and the required value rather than "both values"; the same laws and the strict build were rerun after it.

docs.title: Live, no spend
docs.text:
Real local processes in a scratch directory, with the fixture experiment the process tests use (tests/worker_process_support.py, whose evaluator waits on a per-process marker file) and no model call or network beyond 127.0.0.1. Every process ran under a hard wall-clock alarm (perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'). Output trimmed; the run id is run-dd36512e….

$ meta-evolve workers add shed-1 --storage store
enrolled shed-1 at generation 1
$ meta-evolve workers add shed-2 --storage store
enrolled shed-2 at generation 1
$ meta-evolve run worker_fixture.py --storage store --mode distributed \
    --listen 127.0.0.1:55929 --key-file worker.key --lease-seconds 10 &
# rows, read on a second connection while the dispatcher holds the store:
epoch 2   evaluation READY attempts 0
$ meta-evolve worker --module worker_fixture.py --connect 127.0.0.1:55929 \
    --key-file worker.key --worker-id ghost
meta-evolve worker: refused (this worker is not enrolled in the dispatcher's
store: enrol it with `meta-evolve workers add ghost --storage <path>`)
exit 2
# rows afterwards: identical, epoch 2, READY, attempts 0
$ meta-evolve worker ... --worker-id shed-1 &     # alone, so it takes the item
# shed-1 is inside its evaluation; then shed-2 is started
epoch 2   evaluation LEASED attempts 1
$ meta-evolve workers revoke shed-1 --storage store
revoked shed-1 at generation 2
this frees every lease it holds, in every run in this store, at that run's
next broker transaction
# shed-1's call is then released; its result meets the revoked store
meta-evolve worker: refused (this worker's enrolment was revoked by the
store's operator, at generation 2)
shed-1 exit 2
# the dispatcher exits 0: lifecycle complete, stop trial_limit_reached,
# evaluations 3, usage trials=2 evaluations=3 tokens=0 spend=$0.000000
shed-2 exit 0
# rows after the run:
evaluation COMPLETED attempts 2 last_failure WorkerRevoked last_failure_attempt 1
(the four other rows COMPLETED at attempts 1, no failure)
$ meta-evolve workers list --storage store
shed-1                  revoked  generation 2  {}
shed-2                  trusted  generation 1  {}

The unenrolled worker was refused with the run untouched: the same rows and epoch before and after it, and the same port then admitted shed-1 and shed-2. The revoked worker exited 2, the item it held finished on the other worker at attempts=2 with the revocation recorded against the first attempt, the run completed, and workers list shows generation 2, revoked. No worker or dispatcher process was left running.

Resume in a changed environment. A uv sync could not be made cheaply and reversibly in the shared worktree environment, so the environment was changed another honest way: one more installed distribution. A .dist-info directory for a package live-drift-probe 0.0.1, placed on PYTHONPATH, is a distribution importlib.metadata reports, so it moves the fingerprint exactly as installing a package would, without touching the virtual environment. A second store's run was started listening, never served, and killed with SIGKILL; it was then resumed in the changed environment:

$ python -c '...environment_fingerprint()'                     # unchanged
meta-evolve/environment/v1:0f9c5a5254af9cec…
$ PYTHONPATH=drift-site python -c '...environment_fingerprint()'
meta-evolve/environment/v1:ac1b7481919f00b7…
# Run.environment_drift(): None unchanged, and in the changed environment
environment changed since start: recorded 0f9c5a5254af, current ac1b7481919f
(one digest over every input, so it cannot say which one changed)
$ PYTHONPATH=drift-site meta-evolve resume run-dd36512e… \
    --module worker_fixture.py --storage store2 --workers 1 --lease-seconds 10
environment changed since start: recorded 0f9c5a5254af, current ac1b7481919f
(one digest over every input, so it cannot say which one changed)
run             run-dd36512e…
lifecycle       complete
...
exit 0
# rows: epoch 3, all five COMPLETED at attempts 1

The drift row printed and the resume proceeded to completion, its spawned worker admitted against the resuming dispatcher's own build. The same behaviour is lawed in tests/test_resume_environment_drift.py, for the inline and the spawned-worker resume.

docs.title: Live, capabilities
docs.text:
Before the review round, a second live check exercised capabilities, with the same fixture's evaluator declaring work_requirements={"gpu": True}:

$ meta-evolve workers add shed-1 --storage store --capability gpu=true
enrolled shed-1 at generation 1
$ meta-evolve workers add shed-2 --storage store --capability gpu=true --capability arch=arm64
$ meta-evolve workers add cpu-1 --storage store --capability gpu=false
$ meta-evolve workers add bad --storage store --capability gpu=true --capability gpu=false
meta-evolve workers add: error: argument --capability: the capability 'gpu' is declared twice
exit 2
# listening run started; garbage bytes sent to its port by a peer holding no key:
# the host sent its challenge, and the dispatcher was still running afterwards
# (which refusal arm met the bytes was not observed; the laws in
# tests/test_handshake_unexpected_raise.py pin that)
$ meta-evolve worker ... --worker-id ghost
meta-evolve worker: refused (this worker is not enrolled in the dispatcher's
store: enrol it with `meta-evolve workers add ghost --storage <path>`)
exit 2
$ meta-evolve worker ... --worker-id cpu-1
meta-evolve worker: refused (this run requires the capability gpu=true, and
this worker declares gpu=false)
exit 2
# rows and epoch identical before and after the junk bytes, ghost and cpu-1
# shed-1 inside its evaluation, shed-2 started, shed-1 revoked mid-call:
shed-1 exit 2 (revoked at generation 2); dispatcher exit 0, lifecycle complete
evaluation COMPLETED attempts 2 last_failure WorkerRevoked last_failure_attempt 1
$ meta-evolve workers list --storage store
cpu-1                   trusted  generation 1  {"gpu":false}
shed-1                  revoked  generation 2  {"gpu":true}
shed-2                  trusted  generation 1  {"arch":"arm64","gpu":true}
$ meta-evolve workers add shed-2 ... --capability ram=64       # widen
widened shed-2's capabilities at generation 1: {"arch":"arm64","gpu":true,"ram":64}
$ meta-evolve workers add shed-2 --storage store --capability gpu=true   # narrow
error: InvalidTrustedWorker: ... the declaration drops arch, ram; a trusted
worker's declaration is only widened; revoke it first to drop or change one
exit 1
# a run whose proposer requires gpu=true and evaluator gpu=false:
$ meta-evolve run conflict_fixture.py ... --listen 127.0.0.1:PORT --key-file keyB
error: CapabilityError: no worker can run this run: the evaluator tests:score@1
requires gpu=false and the proposer tests:increment@1 requires gpu=true
exit 1                                  # no key file written
$ meta-evolve run conflict_fixture.py ... --workers 1
exit 0                                  # spawned workers match nothing

The drift resume above was repeated on this tree with the same result: the row printed, and the resume completed with exit 0. No worker or dispatcher process was left running.

docs.title: Final re-verification
docs.text:
After the /pr-review round, every check was run again on c891a37a, with origin/main at 69354f9e:

Check Result Full suite 7,160 passed, 94 skipped, no failures, 1109.85 seconds. ruff check src, mypy (30 configured source files), strict docs build Passed; the same 93 pandoc notices and no MkDocs warning of its own. compileall, after the suite Passed. Five canonical CI examples; experiment 17 --dry-run All exited 0; all 11 scenarios passed. Byte gate, inline Byte-identical to the origin/main capture (118,089 bytes). Byte gate, spawned workers (WorkerProcesses(1) and (2)) Events and work rows identical; the allow-list reads "n/a" on origin/main and [] here.

The review round's laws, each seen red before its fix and under its named mutation:

  • A malformed id is refused by trust and revoke alike, typed, on both registries (check_a_malformed_id_is_neither_trusted_nor_revoked); red with only the record's backstop in place.
  • A read-only registry held across another connection's migration sees the enrolment (test_a_held_reader_sees_a_migration_another_connection_made).
  • The listening host obtains a live reader before opening, and never asks for write authority (tests/test_trust_lookup_handoff.py); red when _terms asks for authority eagerly or inside the closure.
  • A real host refuses a 20,000-character declaration with the truncated reason and a healthy worker then finishes the run; red without the truncation. A keyless oversized kind, an oversized manifest mismatch and the host's own record of the full reason are each red without the fallback (tests/test_handshake_unexpected_raise.py).
  • A durable-local resume report validates history once and computes no fingerprint, and a drifted distributed run still leads with the drift (tests/test_resume_environment_drift.py); 2 loads and 1 fingerprint before.

The /pr-review round's laws, each seen red before its fix or under its named mutation:

  • Rollover records WorkerRevoked for a revoked holder's row, on both adapters (check_a_rollover_records_why_it_frees_a_revoked_workers_row); red before the fix. A lease revoked and overdue at once reports the revoke (check_a_lease_both_revoked_and_overdue_reports_the_revoke); red when expiry is weighed first.
  • workers revoke on a copy of a schema-4 capture refuses and leaves every byte alone (tests/test_cli_worker_administration_stores.py); red before the fix: the old command stamped it schema 5.
  • A trust-row read of a malformed file is DurableStoreError on all three readers (tests/test_trusted_worker_read_faults.py), and a raw sqlite3 fault at the door stops the run (tests/test_handshake_escapes.py); red without the typing.
  • A revoked holder's item is released when its answer fails to send (tests/test_worker_revocation_send_failure.py); red with the release after the send.
  • A guard trigger kept under its name with another body is corruption (tests/test_store_write_guard.py); red when only names are compared.
  • A lone surrogate, escaped or from an undecodable argv byte, and a key repeated inside a JSON value are usage errors before any store opens (tests/test_cli_worker_capabilities.py); red before the fix.
  • An oversized worker_nonce is refused by name and the door stays open (tests/test_handshake_escapes.py); red without the bound. The host keeps the exception behind a refusal nothing expected (tests/test_handshake_unexpected_raise.py).
  • A damaged trust row at the door stops the run (tests/test_damaged_trust_row_at_the_door.py). This pins existing behaviour, so it has no red run.

The keyless-kind case was not introduced by this branch: on origin/main, one unauthenticated frame could stop a run whose frame bound is below the 64 KiB Hello limit.

docs.title: Negative claims
docs.text:
• No paid run was made and none was needed: the live check used the test fixture, and experiment 17 ran with StubProvider.
  • Nothing entered the closed wire error map _ERRORS: src/meta_evolve/distributed/messages.py is unchanged on the branch. WorkerRevoked is a cause recorded on a row, never an exception on the wire.
  • A host is handed a lookup that reads only through a reader: the store hands out a reader, and tests/test_trust_lookup_handoff.py shows a drive's lookup never asks for write authority. No claim is made that authority is unreachable through the object graph.
  • The frozen schema-4 stores under tests/fixtures/api_v01/ are untouched: the branch changes nothing under tests/fixtures/, and they open read-only byte-identical.
  • No root export, no event byte and no DURABLE_TYPES entry was added.
  • This receipt claims no multi-host or TLS validation, no concurrent renewal-versus-expiry or over-capacity race test (#204), no canonical trusted-workers example (#205), and no completion of M11.5–M11.6. The design record stays Design—not shipped until the milestone gate closes.

docs.title: September 26 integration follow-up
docs.text:
The follow-up to c0781f12 addresses the final repository review:

  • Administration commands report the row their transaction committed. They no longer classify an operation using a separate earlier read. Two deterministic interleavings over separate SQLite connections cover concurrent revoke during add and concurrent re-enrolment during revoke (tests/test_cli_worker_administration_races.py). The earlier CLI transcripts above remain historical; the command-line guide shows the current output.
  • A listening host obtains the store's live enrolment reader before creating its key, binding its port, or rolling the epoch. Missing registry support fails at open; spawned backends leave the factory unused. The handoff tests retain the reader-only boundary and prove that subsequent registry changes are visible.
  • Repeated source explanations are condensed. Documentation checks retain published anchors, contract references, availability, and evidence links without requiring exact prose or section adjacency.

The focused regression set passed all 108 tests, including real worker processes. Ruff, mypy's 30 configured files, compilation, and whitespace checks also passed. Full integration verification is recorded in the pull request.

docs.title: September 26 boundary follow-up
docs.text:
Review of the integrated second slice found three remaining input boundaries:

  • Nonces of the right character count could grow through JSON escaping and exceed a tight Terms frame bound. Admission now requires the hexadecimal format workers mint. tests/test_handshake_nonce.py covers malformed values, unchanged queued work, and a healthy worker admitted under the same bound.
  • Unexpected exceptions retained their connection buffers through an unbounded refusal history. The listener now retains its latest 16 refusals. tests/test_handshake_retention.py verifies eviction, collection of the old handshakes, and preservation of recent exception tracebacks.
  • Excessive capability JSON nesting escaped the command-line usage-error path. tests/test_cli_worker_capabilities.py covers both parsing and recursive value validation, with an exit-2 refusal before any store opens.

All 138 focused regression tests passed, including real worker processes. Restoring the three defects made all four targeted regression checks fail; the fixes were then restored. Ruff and mypy passed. The follow-up pull request retains the full integration check results.

docs.title: Worker-process stabilization verification
docs.text: Stabilization baseline verified September 21, 2026 for #353. The repair plan records scope; the execution contract owns usage.

docs.title: Source and scope
docs.text:
The completed stabilization run checked local revision 9f72cae5f7c281b1bad28075dc77e723b45f4d27 on codex/353-worker-stabilization, based on PR head 170e4a26b8401b6d6560d9b18b459cac60595791. This receipt was added afterward; it changes no runtime or test source. At that checkpoint the original main working tree was preserved, and no branch had been pushed or merged. Subsequent authorized stack integration is tracked below.

Commit Repair f7aa7db6 Reject malformed MACs and invalid UTF-8 body encoding as connection-scoped handshake refusals. 4a7a1fd2 Retain completed results before writing, reconnect on socket-operation failures, close served sockets, and refuse crossing run identities with a pending result. e04ce617 Recheck and reserve identity at final admission, preserve ownership throughout a pending batch, and clean up only the failed connection's reservation. 238bdead Replace a handshake test's fixed spin count with bounded socket-readiness waiting. 9f72cae5 Align default inline execution, explicit process backends, admission ordering, and remaining M11 scope across documentation.

These repairs add no durable schema, root API, coordinator special case, worker administration, or new retry policy. The existing M11.3 stack remains the base; this verification does not close the broader M11 acceptance gate.

docs.title: Regressions demonstrated before the fixes
docs.text:
• A non-ASCII MAC raised TypeError through both the real host handshake and pending dispatcher admission. A separate escaped-surrogate body raised UnicodeEncodeError before authentication could return a refusal.
  • Write-side loss raised BrokenPipeError instead of retaining the completed result. The initial worker regressions produced 13 failures and 2 passes. The cross-run probe separately demonstrated an old result being forwarded to a newly admitted run; its refusal regression failed before the guard.
  • Three overlapping-admission cases accepted two peers instead of one: different incarnations of an external ID, and same/different incarnations competing for a minted slot. Every Hello preceded either final Manifests.

The repaired tests use real framed socketpairs, explicit execution barriers, the production pending-admission loop, and an actual dispatcher lease. They prove a malformed peer cannot prevent a valid worker from completing bootstrap evaluation, a completed call is not repeated across failed resends, and a late contender cannot release the first owner's lease or its accepted result. Cleanup cases cover failed admission writes, same-incarnation reconnects, batch exceptions, and endpoint handoff failures. CLI preflight is exercised too.

Independent code review checked admission ownership and worker pending-state handling. Focused suites passed before the integrated run, including the existing real-process reattachment, interruption, and cleanup tests. These overlapping focused counts are not added to the complete-suite count below.

docs.title: Stabilization baseline checks
docs.text:
Environment: macOS, Python 3.12.13, with the locked development, browser, and documentation dependencies installed in the isolated checkout.

Check Result .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --durations=10 6,639 passed, 47 skipped, no failures, 512.33 seconds. .venv/bin/ruff check src Passed. .venv/bin/python -m mypy Passed: 23 configured source files. .venv/bin/python -m compileall -q -x '/candidate/' src tests examples Passed. .venv/bin/python -m mkdocs build --strict Passed; rendered documentation checks also ran in the complete suite. Canonical number search, policy comparison, text optimization, SQL migration, and durable operations commands from CI All passed. Experiment 17 with --dry-run All 11 scenarios passed; no scenario errored or omitted its verdict. Uses StubProvider, with no provider spend. git diff --check Passed.

The 47 skips comprise 36 inapplicable extension-conformance fixture laws, 8 checks requiring optional SDK packages, and 3 platform/enforcement cases. The run includes actual worker-process execution, killed workers and dispatchers, recovery, CLI signals, lease liveness, cohort barriers, wire failure classification, broker contracts, and the inherited #341 regressions.

The first integrated run reported 6,638 passed, 47 skipped, 1 failed in 518.99 seconds. Its sole failure was test_a_frame_over_the_small_bound_crosses_once_the_key_is_proven: the helper exhausted 500 nonblocking advances before its peer thread answered. After the test-only readiness fix, all 39 handshake/admission tests passed, followed by the clean complete run above. The earlier failure is retained here rather than treated as an uninterrupted pass.

docs.title: Stack integration
docs.text:
After the stabilization baseline passed, the user authorized pushing and merging the #353 stack, reconciling related issue tracking, and updating documentation. The final runtime revision is 0288969125c1ff58041615488629130ac9c2d3aa, which integrates the repaired #341 base and main 4af50b40. This receipt update changes documentation only; the baseline counts above remain a separate run.

Review of #341 found an additional liveness case: after one completion blocks, the next completion must consume buffered heartbeats before protecting its own lease. The regression produced Accepted followed by Stale(EXPIRED) before the repair, and two accepted results afterward. EOF and failed-neighbor cases preserve final broker authority and connection-scoped failure handling.

Integration evidence Result #341 source 833f08f8 6,524 passed, 47 skipped in 509.63 seconds; 58 focused liveness/transport checks also passed. #341 hosted checks Both CI runs and docs passed; push CI reports 6,427 passed, 129 skipped. #341 merge fbcc6ade1af3e0f5648d0abe99416c59649418ae; merged tree equals tested source. #353 complete suite at 02889691 6,715 passed, 47 skipped, no failures, 546.76 seconds. Integrated merge review Only the reviewed settling-lease ordering changes runtime behavior relative to the stabilized #353 source; worker admission/reconnect behavior is preserved. Ruff, mypy, compilation, strict docs, whitespace All passed; mypy checks all 23 configured roots. Five canonical CI examples All passed on the integrated revision. Experiment 17 --dry-run All 11 scenarios passed with StubProvider, with no failed, errored, or missing verdict and no provider spend.

The first #341 integration attempt ran inside the tool sandbox and reported 260 failures, 6,262 passes and 47 skips. Its confined subprocess examples could not invoke nested sandbox-exec (sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted). The identical failing catalog test passed with normal subprocess access, then the complete suites above passed without changing runtime behavior. The #341 final run includes two additional connection regressions added after the first run collected its tests. The skip categories are the same as the baseline.

The #353 merge and checks record the final publication revision. Tracking reconciliation belongs to #202, #10, #12, and #268. M11.3's Shipped label does not complete M11.4–M11.6, measured-budget allocation, or retained live-concurrency evidence. Explicit concurrent renewal and over-capacity claim race tests remain part of #204's acceptance; serialized broker-law orderings do not establish those races. Package publication remains the separate author API release gate.

The dry run exercises its existing inline contract; real process behavior is covered by the deterministic process tests. This receipt claims no paid-model run, multi-host/TLS validation, cross-version resume guarantee, worker administration, or completion of M11.4–M11.6.

docs.title: API examples and edge cases
docs.text:
These small deterministic examples answer questions about the API reference. They use numbers so counting, selection, and failure behavior are easy to see. The duration-parser tutorial provides the complete installation-to-result introduction.

Run the setup once, then the cells in order. Only an installed meta_evolve package is required; there are no model calls or credentials. The same code is available in reference_cases.py.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
The proposer adds one to its parent; the evaluator measures the resulting value. The default objective maximizes that measurement as score.

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import EvaluatorFailure


def propose(value):
    return value + 1


def evaluate(value):
    return value

docs.title: Seed evaluation and proposal counts
docs.text:
improve(trials=0) evaluates the seed without asking for a revision. trials=2 allows two successor attempts, in addition to the seed. Run.trials() includes the seed record, while Usage.trials counts only successor attempts.

seed_only = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=evaluate, trials=0)
counted = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=evaluate, trials=2)
for result in (seed_only, counted):
    print([attempt.artifact.value for attempt in result.trials()])
    print("proposals:", result.usage().trials, "evaluations:", result.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# [0]
# proposals: 0 evaluations: 1
# [0, 1, 2]
# proposals: 2 evaluations: 3

A failed proposal consumes an attempt without requiring an evaluator call. A failed evaluation still consumes an evaluation. Therefore proposal counts, evaluation counts, and the number of history records need not be equal.

docs.title: Ties, regressions, and the selected result
docs.text:
Greedy proposes from the best measured artifact so far. It keeps an earlier successful evaluation on an exact tie. Regressions remain in history, and the seed can remain the selected result.

selection_cases = {}
for label, measure in (("ties", lambda value: 0), ("regressions", lambda value: -value)):
    result = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=measure, trials=2)
    selection_cases[label] = result
    selected = result.best_trial()
    print(label, "winner:", selected.artifact.value, "score:", selected.metrics["score"])
    print("history:", [attempt.artifact.value for attempt in result.trials()])
# Output:
# ties winner: 0 score: 0
# history: [0, 1, 1]
# regressions winner: 0 score: 0
# history: [0, 1, 1]

Both successors contain 1: neither replaced the seed as Greedy's parent. best() returns an artifact view with decoded .value; best_trial() returns the producing attempt with its artifact, metrics, evidence, and usage. Neither means “the last attempt.”

BestOfN always proposes from the seed, even when a successor ranks better. Enabled feedback can still carry earlier observations; independent parent selection does not imply statistically independent model calls.

docs.title: One objective on the short path
docs.text:
Pass one Maximize or Minimize as improve(objective=...). A scalar evaluator measures that objective's named metric. Here the evaluator returns distance from three; minimizing error stops as soon as that distance reaches zero:

def distance(value):
    return abs(3 - value)


closest = meta.improve(
    seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=distance, trials=5,
    objective=meta.Minimize("error", satisfy=0),
)
print("selected:", closest.best().value)
print("error:", closest.best_trial().metrics["error"])
print("proposals:", closest.usage().trials, "evaluations:", closest.usage().evaluations)
print("stop:", closest.summary().stop_reason)
# Output:
# selected: 3
# error: 0
# proposals: 3 evaluations: 4
# stop: objective_satisfied

A mapping or EvaluationResult must instead contain the exact declared metric. A missing measurement is a typed evaluation failure. objective=None keeps the default Maximize("score") with no satisfaction target. If the seed meets an explicit target, search stops after its evaluation, even with trials=0.

docs.title: Ordered objectives and satisfaction
docs.text:
Task.objectives defaults to (Maximize("score"),) with no target. A scalar evaluator is valid only with one objective. With several, return a mapping containing every objective's metric; additional metrics are retained without changing the selection rule.

The first objective controls default ranking and built-in satisfaction stopping. Maximize(..., satisfy=x) accepts values at least x; Minimize accepts values at most x. A target on a secondary objective is not another stopping condition.

def measure_tradeoff(value):
    return {"quality": value, "cost": value}


tradeoff = meta.run(meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(
        evaluator=measure_tradeoff,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=2), meta.Minimize("cost", satisfy=0)),
    ),
    seed=0,
    proposer=propose,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
))
print("primary winner:", tradeoff.best().value)
print("lowest cost:", tradeoff.best("cost").value)
print("proposals:", tradeoff.usage().trials)
print("stop:", tradeoff.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# primary winner: 2
# lowest cost: 0
# proposals: 2
# stop: objective_satisfied

The seed already meets the secondary cost target, but the run continues until quality reaches two. Querying best("cost") afterward ranks the retained history by that declared objective; it does not rerun search or change its decisions. This declaration does not request Pareto or joint multi-objective optimization.

docs.title: Tighten one budget dimension
docs.text:
Budget controls allowed work independently of search. run(experiment) uses the task budget. In a supplied budget=, omitted or None fields inherit task ceilings; supplied finite limits cannot exceed them.

When the task bounds both proposals and evaluations, passing only Budget(evaluations=2) tightens evaluations and retains the trial ceiling. Inspect the resolved budget to see both limits:

task = meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate, budget=meta.Budget(trials=4, evaluations=5))
experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=0, proposer=propose, search=meta.Greedy(4))
tighter = meta.Budget(evaluations=2)
limited = meta.run(experiment, budget=tighter)
print("retained proposal ceiling:", limited.inspect().declaration.effective_budget.trials)
print("proposals:", limited.usage().trials, "evaluations:", limited.usage().evaluations)
print("stop:", limited.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# retained proposal ceiling: 4
# proposals: 1 evaluations: 2
# stop: budget_exhausted

Budget() retains every task limit. Explicit widening, such as Budget(evaluations=6) against this task's five-evaluation ceiling, raises ValueError before component calls or committed run facts. See the migration notes for previously rejected partial overrides.

docs.title: Preset defaults follow the allowance
docs.text:
Greedy, BestOfN, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch inherit finite effective Budget.trials when max_trials is omitted or None. Without that ceiling, they use 20, or 100 for TreeSearch. An explicit integer is a voluntary stop. improve(trials=...) keeps its integer-only default of 20.

allowance = meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate, budget=meta.Budget(trials=25))
for search in (meta.Greedy(), meta.Greedy(max_trials=20)):
    result = meta.run(meta.Experiment(task=allowance, seed=0, proposer=propose, search=search))
    print("proposals:", result.usage().trials, "evaluations:", result.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# proposals: 25 evaluations: 26
# proposals: 20 evaluations: 21

See Migrate to 0.2 to retain earlier work amounts.

docs.title: Proposer arguments and feedback
docs.text:
A plain proposer accepts (parent) or explicitly requests ProposerContext with (parent, *, context). Ordinary optional arguments retain their Python defaults:

def scale_candidate(parent, scale=2):
    return parent * scale


scaled = meta.improve(seed=1, proposer=scale_candidate, evaluator=evaluate, trials=1)
print(scaled.best().value)
# Output:
# 2

Request framework state explicitly:

def advance(parent, *, context):
    return parent + context.step


advanced = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=advance, evaluator=evaluate, trials=2)
print(advanced.best().value)
# Output:
# 3

To receive feedback, pass context=RecentAncestors(...) to improve() or Experiment and accept the keyword-only context in the proposer. Read context.evidence.latest(kind) or the bundle's bounded .rendered text. Pushed feedback is off by default; recording evidence alone does not enable it. PullAccess separately supplies an audited reader as context.experience. Follow the feedback guide for a complete example. The migration guide covers existing positional callbacks and registered histories.

This bounded loop uses exact evaluator evidence to propose the next value. Two records hold one evidence item and its evaluation in this example; a different evaluator may need a larger bound. One rendered character deliberately demonstrates that structured evidence remains available when text is clipped.

def feedback_score(value):
    return meta.EvaluationResult(metrics={"score": value}, evidence=(
        meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="feedback", data={"value": value}),
    ))


def feedback_revision(parent, *, context):
    item = context.evidence.latest("feedback")
    if item is None:
        return parent
    return meta.ProposalResult(candidate=item.data["value"] + 1,
                               derived_from=(item.ref,))


feedback_run = meta.improve(
    seed=0, proposer=feedback_revision, evaluator=feedback_score, trials=6,
    context=meta.RecentAncestors(max_records=2, max_chars=1),
)
print("selected:", feedback_run.best().value)
print("proposals:", feedback_run.usage().trials,
      "evaluations:", feedback_run.usage().evaluations)
# Output:
# selected: 6
# proposals: 6 evaluations: 7

latest() raises meta_evolve.errors.ContextDisabled with pushed context off; an enabled policy with no selected match returns None. Check .enabled when feedback is an optional dependency. The experience guide explains selection order, provenance, and upgrading durable histories.

docs.title: Plain values and result records
docs.text:
A proposer can return a candidate directly; an evaluator can return a scalar or metric mapping. Use ProposalResult and EvaluationResult when you also need observations, usage, or typed failures. Their maps are frozen on construction.

def propose_with_usage(parent):
    return meta.ProposalResult(
        candidate=parent + 1,
        hypothesis="A larger value should score higher.",
        usage=meta.Resources(tokens=5, spend_micros=None),
    )


def evaluate_with_evidence(value):
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": value},
        evidence=(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="measurement", data={"value": value}),),
    )


recorded = meta.improve(
    seed=0, proposer=propose_with_usage, evaluator=evaluate_with_evidence, trials=1,
)
selected = recorded.best_trial()
print("value:", selected.artifact.value, "score:", selected.metrics["score"])
print("evidence:", selected.evidence[0].data["value"])
print("tokens:", recorded.usage().tokens, "spend:", recorded.usage().spend_micros)
# Output:
# value: 1 score: 1
# evidence: 1
# tokens: 5 spend: None

The token amount above is a declared fixture, not measured provider activity. Rich results take Resources, containing tokens, billed micro-USD, and elapsed seconds. The engine owns counts and records Usage. Passing the old Usage value to a rich result raises at construction.

docs.title: Forward nested resources
docs.text:
Project inner.usage().resources, then add the evaluator's own costs once. Here each outer evaluation runs one inner proposal reporting five tokens and unknown spend, then adds two tokens of its own. Inner counts remain inner:

def evaluate_procedure(value):
    inner = meta.improve(seed=value, proposer=propose_with_usage, evaluator=evaluate, trials=1)
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": inner.best().value},
        usage=meta.Resources(tokens=2) + inner.usage().resources,
    )


nested = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=evaluate_procedure, trials=1)
print("outer proposals:", nested.usage().trials, "evaluations:", nested.usage().evaluations)
print("tokens:", nested.usage().tokens, "spend:", nested.usage().spend_micros)
# Output:
# outer proposals: 1 evaluations: 2
# tokens: 14 spend: None

docs.title: Unknown spend and monetary ceilings
docs.text:
Resources(spend_micros=0) means known free work. None means an unknown bill; adding an unknown amount makes the aggregate unknown. Estimates belong in evidence. One micro-USD is one millionth of a US dollar.

With no monetary ceiling, the preceding run can evaluate its successor. Under a monetary ceiling, an unknown proposal charge prevents further work:

unknown_spend = meta.run(meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(evaluator=evaluate_with_evidence, budget=meta.Budget(spend_micros=100)),
    seed=0,
    proposer=propose_with_usage,
    search=meta.Greedy(2),
))
print("states:", [attempt.state for attempt in unknown_spend.trials()])
print("candidate retained:", unknown_spend.trials()[-1].artifact.value)
print("best measured:", unknown_spend.best().value)
print("stop:", unknown_spend.inspect().overview.stop_reason)
# Output:
# states: ['evaluated', 'unevaluated']
# candidate retained: 1
# best measured: 0
# stop: accounting_unavailable

The proposed value is retained, but was never evaluated. It cannot replace the measured seed. If the evaluator instead reports unknown spend, its completed measurement is retained and further work stops.

Resource reports are checked after calls return. A reported monetary overrun is charged and recorded as a typed ResourceExhausted failure. A zero spend ceiling permits known free work. These ceilings neither interrupt an in-flight SDK request nor guarantee a provider hard spending cap. See evaluation and budgets for accounting details.

docs.title: No successful evaluation
docs.text:
Failures such as EvaluatorFailure, ProposerFailure, and InvalidOutput are data from meta_evolve.domain, not exceptions to raise. Return them directly, or attach one to a result record. A failed proposal omits candidate; a failed evaluation omits metrics. Contradictory records raise ValueError.

def unavailable(value):
    return meta.EvaluationResult(failure=EvaluatorFailure(message="grader unavailable"))


failed = meta.improve(seed=0, proposer=propose, evaluator=unavailable, trials=0)
try:
    failed.best()
except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
    print("No successful evaluation")
print("state:", failed.trials()[0].state)
report = failed.summary()
print("evaluations:", report.evaluation_count)
print("rankability:", report.rankability)
print("score:", report.primary_score, "lineage:", report.winning_lineage)
print("lifecycle:", report.lifecycle)
# Output:
# No successful evaluation
# state: evaluation_failed
# evaluations: 1
# rankability: unrankable
# score: None lineage: ()
# lifecycle: complete

NoSuccessfulEvaluation is an exception: best(), best_trial(), and default-winner lineage() raise it when nothing ranks. summary() returns state, absent score, and recorded costs; trials(), usage(), and inspect() also remain available. See the summary migration guide.

Invalid output and ordinary exceptions inside a proposer or evaluator become typed outcomes. Declaration errors, unsupported capabilities, and infrastructure faults can raise instead of returning a Run; they are not candidate scores.

docs.title: Retained history and resume
docs.text: Passing Storage.durable(path) to improve() or local run() saves history. Reopen it with Run(run_id, storage) to inspect facts without executing components. Resuming unfinished work additionally requires a supported mode and registered, reconstructible components. Follow save and reopen and recovery for those separate workflows.

docs.title: Shipped API reference
docs.text:
Choose the part of the experiment you are working on. Each section contains signatures and descriptions generated from the package used for this build. For a first complete run, start with the parser.

You want to… Reference Declare and run an experiment Run an experiment Replace a proposer or evaluator Proposers and evaluators Load files, propose edits, and run a grader Artifacts and source repair Choose which candidate to try next Search Give the proposer previous feedback Feedback and memory Inspect the selected artifact, history, and costs Results and inspection Save, reopen, or step through a run Storage and sessions Understand an exception Errors

The core-object walkthrough explains the relationships between these objects. API examples cover counts and edge cases; Migrate to 0.2 explains API changes.

docs.title: Run an experiment
docs.text:
Start with improve for a bounded loop, or compose a Task and Experiment when you need explicit evaluation, search, and limits. Both entrances return a Run. Resources reports component costs; Usage includes the run's counts.

Worked examples: first parser · set limits.

docs.title: improve
docs.text:
improve(
    *,
    seed,
    proposer,
    evaluator,
    trials=20,
    storage=None,
    random_seed=0,
    objective=None,
    context=None,
)

Run a bounded greedy improvement loop with a callable evaluator.

This constructs Task, Experiment, and Greedy, then calls run. By default it maximizes score with no satisfaction target and supplies no pushed feedback. Declare one objective or an explicit context policy here. Use the expanded path for multiple objectives, custom artifacts, budgets, search, pulled experience, execution mode, or registry components.

The seed is evaluated before successor attempts. A tie or regression keeps the earlier best result; an attempt need not improve anything. Supplying durable storage preserves local history but does not make this run resumable.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default seed

Initial immutable JSON-like value, such as a string or number.

required proposer

Callable accepting (parent) or (parent, *, context), or a local proposer adapter. Return a candidate or ProposalResult.

required evaluator

Independent callable returning a finite scalar measured under the objective's name, a mapping containing that metric, or EvaluationResult. Missing measurements become typed evaluation failures, not scores.

required trials int

Maximum number of successor proposals; defaults to 20. Zero evaluates only the seed. Failed proposals still count. Must be a non-negative integer; booleans and None are rejected.

20 storage

Artifact and event storage; defaults to isolated memory.

None random_seed int

Integer seed for recorded deterministic choices, default 0; does not make external providers deterministic.

0 objective Maximize | Minimize | None

One Maximize or Minimize; None uses Maximize("score") without a satisfaction target. A satisfied seed needs no proposals.

None context ContextPolicy | None

Explicit policy for bounded pushed feedback, such as RecentAncestors. None and NoMemory disable it. This never enables pull access. The proposer reads evidence through its keyword-only context.

None

Returns:

Type Description Run

A Run, even if all evaluations failed. Winner queries then raise NoSuccessfulEvaluation; trials(), inspect(), and usage() remain available.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If a declared input has an unsupported type.

ValueError

If a limit is negative or the declaration is invalid.

docs.title: Task dataclass
docs.text:
Task(
    *,
    evaluator,
    artifact=None,
    objectives=(Maximize("score"),),
    budget=None,
    environment=FrozenMap(),
    artifact_kind="python-value",
    artifact_representation="canonical-json",
)

Define independent evaluation, objectives, artifact type, and budget.

Construction declares the rules without evaluating a candidate. The seed belongs to Experiment. Candidate proposals cannot revise this contract.

Malformed declarations raise TypeError or ValueError. During a run, invalid returned measurements become typed outcomes, not fabricated scores.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default evaluator ComponentRef | Callable[..., object]

Callable receiving the decoded candidate, or a registered evaluator reference. Return a finite number for exactly one objective, a mapping covering every objective, EvaluationResult, or a typed failure from meta_evolve.domain. Booleans are not scores.

required artifact InitVar[type | None]

Optional artifact type, such as Text, with declared kind and representation; an instance is rejected. Omit it for ordinary immutable JSON-like values, including strings.

None objectives tuple[Objective, ...]

Non-empty ordered objectives with unique metric names. Defaults to (Maximize("score"),) with no satisfaction target. The first controls default ranking and built-in satisfaction stopping. Extra reported metrics are retained without changing that selection.

(Maximize('score'),) budget Budget | None

Optional Budget; None adds no task ceiling. Search can still impose its own finite attempt limit.

None environment Mapping[str, object]

Evaluator-owned JSON-like metadata, frozen on construction and included in task identity. It does not configure an OS environment.

FrozenMap() artifact_kind str

Advanced codec kind; defaults to "python-value".

'python-value' artifact_representation str

Advanced codec representation; defaults to "canonical-json". Prefer artifact= for declared artifact types; conflicting explicit kind or representation values are rejected.

'canonical-json'

docs.title: Experiment dataclass
docs.text:
Experiment(
    *,
    task,
    seed,
    proposer,
    search=None,
    context=None,
    experience=None,
    random_seed=0,
    registry=None,
)

An immutable evaluated-search declaration.

Execution starts only when passed to run or Session.start. Construction does not invoke components; execution validates their compatibility. Storage, mode, and a narrowing budget are execution options. Use dataclasses.replace to make a new declaration while reusing unchanged components.

Equality is ordinary dataclass equality over these eight fields. In particular, no structural equality is promised for live proposer or registry objects.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default task Task

Evaluation contract, artifact type, objectives, and optional budget ceiling.

required seed object

Initial value accepted by the task's artifact codec.

required proposer ProposerLike

Callable accepting (parent) or (parent, *, context), adapter, or registered proposer component. Only keyword-only context requests ProposerContext; other defaults remain unchanged.

required search SearchProgram | None

Search policy; None means budget-led Greedy() at execution time.

None context ContextPolicy | None

Policy-pushed feedback, such as AncestorsOnly. None and NoMemory select no records.

None experience ExperienceAccess | None

Bounded agent-pulled access, such as PullAccess. None provides no reader. Recording evidence does not enable either feedback channel automatically.

None random_seed int

Integer seed for recorded deterministic search choices; defaults to 0.

0 registry Registry | None

Extra artifact codecs and registered durable components; None uses built-ins and live local callables.

None

docs.title: run
docs.text:
run(
    experiment: Experiment,
    /,
    *,
    storage: Storage | None = None,
    budget: Budget | None = None,
    mode: ExecutionMode = "local",
) -> Run

run(
    *,
    task: Task,
    seed: object,
    proposer: ProposerLike,
    search: SearchProgram | None = None,
    context: ContextPolicy | None = None,
    experience: ExperienceAccess | None = None,
    storage: Storage | None = None,
    budget: Budget | None = None,
    random_seed: int = 0,
    mode: ExecutionMode = "local",
    registry: Registry | None = None,
) -> Run

Run one evaluated improvement search and return its inspectable history.

Pass an Experiment as the positional argument. The source-compatible keyword form accepts its declaration fields instead; supplying both forms raises TypeError. The keyword form retains the effective defaults search=None, context=None, experience=None, random_seed=0, and registry=None. The default Greedy() inherits finite trial allowance, falling back to 20 when unbounded. Both forms use the same Session as paced and resumed execution.

storage=None creates separate in-memory storage. A durable storage handle preserves local history; resumability additionally requires registered, reconstructible components and a supported execution mode.

budget=None uses the task budget, or an unrestricted resource allowance if the task has none. In a supplied Budget, omitted or None dimensions inherit task ceilings. Finite values may tighten or introduce ceilings; exceeding a finite task ceiling raises ValueError before work starts. Budget() preserves all task ceilings.

mode="local" accepts live Python callables and provides no isolation. "durable-local" adds reconstructible execution and recovery. "distributed" uses the durable dispatcher and currently executes serially, one worker at a time; it does not provide multiprocess concurrency. The latter two modes require durable storage, registered components, and their declared capabilities. See the programming model's execution profiles.

Invalid proposals and ordinary proposer or evaluator failures are recorded as typed trial outcomes; they are not converted to low scores. Capability and infrastructure exceptions can abort execution instead of producing a Run.

Returns:

Type Description Run

A Run for result, history, usage, and comparison queries, including when no evaluation succeeded.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If a declared public input has the wrong type.

ValueError

If a declaration is invalid or the task budget is widened.

BudgetUnavailable

If the seed cannot be admitted.

CapabilityError

If the requested execution requirements cannot be satisfied.

Maximize(metric, satisfy=None)

Prefer larger values of one named evaluation metric.

Use Maximize("quality", satisfy=0.9) in Task.objectives. Built-in search uses the first objective for ranking and satisfaction; additional objectives do not automatically become joint stopping conditions.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default metric str

Non-empty metric name returned by the evaluator.

required satisfy float | None

Optional finite target; a value greater than or equal to it satisfies this objective. None supplies no target.

None

docs.text:
Minimize(metric, satisfy=None)

Prefer smaller values of one named evaluation metric.

For example, Minimize("errors", satisfy=0) targets zero errors. Objective values are measurements; a typed failure is never a low score. See Task for ordering and evaluator return forms.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default metric str

Non-empty metric name returned by the evaluator.

required satisfy float | None

Optional finite target; a value less than or equal to it satisfies this objective. None supplies no target.

None

docs.title: Budget dataclass
docs.text:
Budget(
    *,
    evaluations=None,
    trials=None,
    tokens=None,
    spend_micros=None,
    wall_seconds=None,
)

Immutable resource ceilings, checked against recorded Usage.

Every field defaults to None (no ceiling for that resource). Counts must be non-negative integers; booleans are rejected. A budget bounds work independently of a search preset's own attempt limit.

Resource reports are checked after actions return; an in-flight SDK call is not interrupted. A monetary overrun is charged and recorded as a typed failure. This is not a hard provider spending cap.

In run(..., budget=...), omitted or None fields inherit task ceilings. Supplied limits may tighten or introduce ceilings, but exceeding a finite task ceiling raises ValueError before work starts. Budget() retains every task ceiling; zero remains a real limit. run documents execution defaults; the limits guide supplies complete examples.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default evaluations int | None

Maximum evaluator invocations, including the seed. Zero cannot admit the seed and raises BudgetUnavailable at run start. Failed evaluations still consume this allowance.

None trials int | None

Maximum successor proposal attempts; the seed consumes none. Zero permits seed evaluation only.

None tokens int | None

Ceiling on component-reported tokens.

None spend_micros int | None

Ceiling on billed micro-USD; zero permits known free work. Unknown spend makes a monetary ceiling unverifiable and stops more work.

None wall_seconds float | None

Ceiling on reported non-negative finite elapsed seconds.

None

allows(usage)

remaining_after(usage)

narrow(other)

docs.title: Proposers and evaluators
docs.text:
A proposer receives the parent artifact and returns a candidate. An evaluator receives that candidate and returns a score or named measurements. Use the result records below when either callback also reports evidence, costs, or a typed failure. A proposer can request context to read declared feedback.

Worked examples: live parser · SVG Feedback Descent · define evaluation · use your SDK.

docs.title: ProposerContext dataclass
docs.text:
The candidate-facing state authorized for one proposal.

A plain callback requests this with def propose(parent, *, context). A default on that keyword does not disable delivery. Ordinary optional arguments keep their Python defaults; variadics alone do not request context. Structural objects retain their explicit propose(parent, context) port.

rng supplies recorded per-attempt randomness. step is the successor's logical step, starting at one; objectives is the task's ordered tuple. bundle.records contains pushed feedback and bundle.rendered its bounded text. evidence.latest(kind) reads its last matching evidence; evidence.enabled distinguishes disabled context from a missing match. With no context policy the bundle is empty. experience is an audited reader only when pull access is enabled; otherwise None. Repository adapters may supply workspace with controlled execution and history information; ordinary callables receive None there.

docs.title: evidence property
docs.text:
Evidence in this bundle, with explicit enabled/truncated status.

Manually constructed contexts must supply context_policy to enable lookup; neither an empty bundle nor its reason proves policy status.

docs.title: ProposalResult dataclass
docs.text:
ProposalResult(
    *,
    candidate=_MISSING,
    failure=None,
    hypothesis=None,
    predicted_outcomes=FrozenMap(),
    metadata=FrozenMap(),
    evidence=(),
    usage=Resources(),
    derived_from=(),
)

A normalized candidate or typed proposer failure.

candidate is a value in the task's artifact type, not a durable payload: the registered codec is the one authority for that translation, and it runs where the task's kind and representation are known.

Plain proposers can return the candidate directly. Use this record when reporting usage, observations, or a failure from meta_evolve.domain.

Malformed records raise TypeError or ValueError on construction. During a run, ordinary exceptions raised inside a proposer become typed proposer failures; capability and infrastructure errors can abort the run.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default candidate object

Required for success; even None can be a valid value. The displayed _MISSING default means omitted. Omit this argument entirely when supplying failure.

_MISSING failure Failure | None

Typed proposer or shared failure, such as ProposerFailure or InvalidOutput. A failure cannot also carry a candidate.

None hypothesis str | None

Optional non-empty explanation of the proposed change.

None predicted_outcomes FrozenMap | Mapping[str, object]

Optional JSON-like predictions, not evaluator scores.

FrozenMap() metadata FrozenMap | Mapping[str, object]

Optional JSON-like proposal metadata, frozen on construction.

FrozenMap() evidence tuple[EvidenceDraft, ...]

Tuple of EvidenceDraft observations.

() usage Resources

Resources, defaulting to known free work. Report unknown bills explicitly with Resources(spend_micros=None). Engine-owned trial and evaluation fields are not accepted.

Resources() derived_from tuple[ExperienceRef, ...]

Unique authorized prior ExperienceRef values, in declared order; empty by default. Recording a reference grants no access.

()

docs.title: EvaluationResult dataclass
docs.text:
EvaluationResult(
    *,
    metrics=FrozenMap(),
    failure=None,
    uncertainty=FrozenMap(),
    evidence=(),
    usage=Resources(),
)

Independent measurements or a typed failure, plus evidence and usage.

Successful metrics must cover the task objectives. A failed measurement has no rankable metrics. Return this explicitly to attach evidence, uncertainty, tokens, monetary spend, or elapsed usage; plain evaluators may return a scalar or metric mapping when no extra observations are needed.

Invalid field shapes raise TypeError or ValueError on construction. Missing task metrics are detected during execution as InvalidOutput. Ordinary exceptions inside the evaluator become typed evaluator failures; capability and infrastructure exceptions can abort execution. Inspect Run.trials() for measurements and failure records.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default metrics FrozenMap | Mapping[str, object]

Non-empty mapping of metric names to finite real numbers for success. Booleans, NaN, and infinity are rejected. Every task objective must be present; extra metrics are retained. Omit on failure.

FrozenMap() failure Failure | None

Typed evaluator or shared failure from meta_evolve.domain. Supplying both a failure and metrics raises ValueError.

None uncertainty FrozenMap | Mapping[str, object]

Optional named non-negative finite numeric estimates; retained as observations, not used automatically for ranking.

FrozenMap() evidence tuple[EvidenceDraft, ...]

Tuple of EvidenceDraft observations.

() usage Resources

Action resources; defaults to Resources(), meaning known free work. Components report tokens, spend, and elapsed time. Failure usage still counts; trial/evaluation fields are not accepted.

Resources()

An observation attached to a proposal or evaluation before commitment.

Attach these to result records. Recording evidence does not automatically show it to a proposer; configure experiment feedback explicitly.

Parameters:
